Eight suspects were arrested and the servers used to provide illegal access to the channels shut down.<\/p>\n\n<p>A joint investigation led by the <a class=\"external\" href=\"https:\/\/www.policia.es\/\" target=\"_blank\">Spanish National Police<\/a>, with the support of the <a class=\"external\" href=\"http:\/\/www.gdbop.bg\/bg\/\" target=\"_blank\">Bulgarian authorities<\/a>, Europol and <a class=\"external\" href=\"http:\/\/www.eurojust.europa.eu\/Pages\/home.aspx\" target=\"_blank\">Eurojust<\/a>, has resulted in the dismantling of a criminal network specialised in the illegal distribution of pay-TV channels on a European scale.<\/p>\n\n<p>The network is accused of illicitly distributing pay-TV channels in various European countries through two legally established Internet Service Provider (ISP) companies, located in Spain and Bulgaria, by using Internet Protocol television (IPTV) technology.<\/p>\n\n<p>In a coordinated action, eight suspects were arrested and 12 searches carried out simultaneously in Spain and Bulgaria. Investigators seized the servers used to provide illegal access to the channels, alongside numerous documents.<\/p>\n\n<p><img alt=\"Operation Casper\" height=\"375\" src=\"https:\/\/www.europol.europa.eu\/sites\/default\/files\/images\/editor\/op_casper2_0.jpg\" width=\"1514\" loading=\"lazy\"><\/p>\n\n<p>Europol supported the investigations by providing information exchange, operational coordination and support, and forensic expertise. During the investigations, Europol organised an operational meeting at its headquarters in The Hague, and facilitated information exchange between law enforcement agencies and private-sector partners. On the action day, two experts from Europol\u2019s Intellectual Property Crime Coordinated Coalition (IPC3) and two from Europol\u2019s European Cybercrime Centre (EC3) were deployed to Spain and Bulgaria, equipped with mobile offices to support the actions on the spot. This allowed for real-time intelligence analysis and cross-checks against Europol\u2019s databases, as well as forensic support. <\/p>\n\n<p><br>\nOperation Casper began when a representative from a broadcast rights holder filed a complaint against the owner of an Internet Service Provider (ISP) located in M\u00e1laga (Spain), for illicitly distributing pay-TV channels to thousands of clients in different EU countries. Investigations revealed that the ISP owner, a Danish citizen, was the leader of a criminal network who operated on a European scale. Investigators also unveiled the existence of a second ISP in Silistra (Bulgaria) owned by the network, which was permanently connected to the ISP in Spain and provided coverage to other European countries. Both ISPs were legally established in both countries and performed legal activities while, in parallel, exploiting their capacities to carry out illegal activities.<\/p>\n\n<p>The crime group also used a network of shell companies, which relied technically on the ISPs, and were in charge of distributing the illicit TV signals to the end clients.<\/p>\n\n<p>Operation Casper represents a great example of cross-border cooperation against intellectual property rights infringements.<\/p>\n\n<h3>Intellectual property crime in the EU<\/h3>\n\n<p>Intellectual property crime is a significant problem that hits the EU particularly hard. Criminal groups get involved in these illegal activities, attracted to its relatively low risk and high levels of revenue.<br>\nTo strengthen the fight against counterfeiting and piracy online and offline, Europol and the<a class=\"external\" href=\"https:\/\/euipo.europa.eu\/ohimportal\/en\" target=\"_blank\"> European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO)<\/a> joined forces to launch the <a href=\"https:\/\/www.europol.europa.eu\/about-europol\/intellectual-property-crime-coordinated-coalition-ipc3\">Intellectual Property Crime Coordinated Coalition (IPC3<\/a>).<\/p>\n\n<p> Further details available on <a class=\"external\" href=\"https:\/\/www.policia.es\/prensa\/20170406_1.html\" target=\"_blank\">Policia\u2019s press release<\/a>.<\/p>\n\n<p> <\/p>","summary":"The crime group owned two Internet Service Providers (ISPs) in Spain and Bulgaria, that illicitly offered more than 1000 TV channels to clients across Europe using Internet Protocol television (IPTV) technology. Eight suspects were arrested and the servers used to provide illegal access to the channels shut down.<\/p>\n\n<p>A joint investigation led by the <a class=\"external\" href=\"https:\/\/www.policia.es\/\" target=\"_blank\">Spanish National Police<\/a>, with the support of the <a class=\"external\" href=\"http:\/\/www.gdbop.bg\/bg\/\" target=\"_blank\">Bulgarian authorities<\/a>, Europol and <a class=\"external\" href=\"http:\/\/www.eurojust.europa.eu\/Pages\/home.aspx\" target=\"_blank\">Eurojust<\/a>, has resulted in the dismantling of a criminal network specialised in the illegal distribution of pay-TV channels on a European scale.<\/p>\n\n<p>The network is accused of illicitly distributing pay-TV channels in various European countries through two legally established Internet Service Provider (ISP) companies, located in Spain and Bulgaria, by using Internet Protocol television (IPTV) technology.<\/p>\n\n<p>In a coordinated action, eight suspects were arrested and 12 searches carried out simultaneously in Spain and Bulgaria. Investigators seized the servers used to provide illegal access to the channels, alongside numerous documents.<\/p>\n\n<p><img alt=\"Operation Casper\" height=\"375\" src=\"https:\/\/www.europol.europa.eu\/sites\/default\/files\/images\/editor\/op_casper2_0.jpg\" width=\"1514\" loading=\"lazy\"><\/p>\n\n<p>Europol supported the investigations by providing information exchange, operational coordination and support, and forensic expertise. During the investigations, Europol organised an operational meeting at its headquarters in The Hague, and facilitated information exchange between law enforcement agencies and private-sector partners. On the action day, two experts from Europol\u2019s Intellectual Property Crime Coordinated Coalition (IPC3) and two from Europol\u2019s European Cybercrime Centre (EC3) were deployed to Spain and Bulgaria, equipped with mobile offices to support the actions on the spot. This allowed for real-time intelligence analysis and cross-checks against Europol\u2019s databases, as well as forensic support. <\/p>\n\n<p><br>\nOperation Casper began when a representative from a broadcast rights holder filed a complaint against the owner of an Internet Service Provider (ISP) located in M\u00e1laga (Spain), for illicitly distributing pay-TV channels to thousands of clients in different EU countries. Investigations revealed that the ISP owner, a Danish citizen, was the leader of a criminal network who operated on a European scale. Investigators also unveiled the existence of a second ISP in Silistra (Bulgaria) owned by the network, which was permanently connected to the ISP in Spain and provided coverage to other European countries. Both ISPs were legally established in both countries and performed legal activities while, in parallel, exploiting their capacities to carry out illegal activities.<\/p>\n\n<p>The crime group also used a network of shell companies, which relied technically on the ISPs, and were in charge of distributing the illicit TV signals to the end clients.<\/p>\n\n<p>Operation Casper represents a great example of cross-border cooperation against intellectual property rights infringements.<\/p>\n\n<h3>Intellectual property crime in the EU<\/h3>\n\n<p>Intellectual property crime is a significant problem that hits the EU particularly hard. Criminal groups get involved in these illegal activities, attracted to its relatively low risk and high levels of revenue.<br>\nTo strengthen the fight against counterfeiting and piracy online and offline, Europol and the<a class=\"external\" href=\"https:\/\/euipo.europa.eu\/ohimportal\/en\" target=\"_blank\"> European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO)<\/a> joined forces to launch the <a href=\"https:\/\/www.europol.europa.eu\/about-europol\/intellectual-property-crime-coordinated-coalition-ipc3\">Intellectual Property Crime Coordinated Coalition (IPC3<\/a>).<\/p>\n\n<p> Further details available on <a class=\"external\" href=\"https:\/\/www.policia.es\/prensa\/20170406_1.html\" target=\"_blank\">Policia\u2019s press release<\/a>.<\/p>\n\n<p> <\/p>","summary":"The crime group owned two Internet Service Providers (ISPs) in Spain and Bulgaria, that illicitly offered more than 1000 TV channels to clients across Europe using Internet Protocol television (IPTV) technology. Eight suspects were arrested and the servers used to provide illegal access to the channels shut down.<\/p>\n\n<p>A joint investigation led by the <a class=\"external\" href=\"https:\/\/www.policia.es\/\" target=\"_blank\">Spanish National Police<\/a>, with the support of the <a class=\"external\" href=\"http:\/\/www.gdbop.bg\/bg\/\" target=\"_blank\">Bulgarian authorities<\/a>, Europol and <a class=\"external\" href=\"http:\/\/www.eurojust.europa.eu\/Pages\/home.aspx\" target=\"_blank\">Eurojust<\/a>, has resulted in the dismantling of a criminal network specialised in the illegal distribution of pay-TV channels on a European scale.<\/p>\n\n<p>The network is accused of illicitly distributing pay-TV channels in various European countries through two legally established Internet Service Provider (ISP) companies, located in Spain and Bulgaria, by using Internet Protocol television (IPTV) technology.<\/p>\n\n<p>In a coordinated action, eight suspects were arrested and 12 searches carried out simultaneously in Spain and Bulgaria. Investigators seized the servers used to provide illegal access to the channels, alongside numerous documents.<\/p>\n\n<p><img alt=\"Operation Casper\" height=\"375\" src=\"https:\/\/www.europol.europa.eu\/sites\/default\/files\/images\/editor\/op_casper2_0.jpg\" width=\"1514\" loading=\"lazy\"><\/p>\n\n<p>Europol supported the investigations by providing information exchange, operational coordination and support, and forensic expertise. During the investigations, Europol organised an operational meeting at its headquarters in The Hague, and facilitated information exchange between law enforcement agencies and private-sector partners. On the action day, two experts from Europol\u2019s Intellectual Property Crime Coordinated Coalition (IPC3) and two from Europol\u2019s European Cybercrime Centre (EC3) were deployed to Spain and Bulgaria, equipped with mobile offices to support the actions on the spot. This allowed for real-time intelligence analysis and cross-checks against Europol\u2019s databases, as well as forensic support. <\/p>\n\n<p><br>\nOperation Casper began when a representative from a broadcast rights holder filed a complaint against the owner of an Internet Service Provider (ISP) located in M\u00e1laga (Spain), for illicitly distributing pay-TV channels to thousands of clients in different EU countries. Investigations revealed that the ISP owner, a Danish citizen, was the leader of a criminal network who operated on a European scale. Investigators also unveiled the existence of a second ISP in Silistra (Bulgaria) owned by the network, which was permanently connected to the ISP in Spain and provided coverage to other European countries. Both ISPs were legally established in both countries and performed legal activities while, in parallel, exploiting their capacities to carry out illegal activities.<\/p>\n\n<p>The crime group also used a network of shell companies, which relied technically on the ISPs, and were in charge of distributing the illicit TV signals to the end clients.<\/p>\n\n<p>Operation Casper represents a great example of cross-border cooperation against intellectual property rights infringements.<\/p>\n\n<h3>Intellectual property crime in the EU<\/h3>\n\n<p>Intellectual property crime is a significant problem that hits the EU particularly hard. Eight suspects were arrested and the servers used to provide illegal access to the channels shut down.<\/p>\n\n<p>A joint investigation led by the <a class=\"external\" href=\"https:\/\/www.policia.es\/\" target=\"_blank\">Spanish National Police<\/a>, with the support of the <a class=\"external\" href=\"http:\/\/www.gdbop.bg\/bg\/\" target=\"_blank\">Bulgarian authorities<\/a>, Europol and <a class=\"external\" href=\"http:\/\/www.eurojust.europa.eu\/Pages\/home.aspx\" target=\"_blank\">Eurojust<\/a>, has resulted in the dismantling of a criminal network specialised in the illegal distribution of pay-TV channels on a European scale.<\/p>\n\n<p>The network is accused of illicitly distributing pay-TV channels in various European countries through two legally established Internet Service Provider (ISP) companies, located in Spain and Bulgaria, by using Internet Protocol television (IPTV) technology.<\/p>\n\n<p>In a coordinated action, eight suspects were arrested and 12 searches carried out simultaneously in Spain and Bulgaria. Investigators seized the servers used to provide illegal access to the channels, alongside numerous documents.<\/p>\n\n<p><img alt=\"Operation Casper\" height=\"375\" src=\"https:\/\/www.europol.europa.eu\/sites\/default\/files\/images\/editor\/op_casper2_0.jpg\" width=\"1514\" loading=\"lazy\"><\/p>\n\n<p>Europol supported the investigations by providing information exchange, operational coordination and support, and forensic expertise. During the investigations, Europol organised an operational meeting at its headquarters in The Hague, and facilitated information exchange between law enforcement agencies and private-sector partners. On the action day, two experts from Europol\u2019s Intellectual Property Crime Coordinated Coalition (IPC3) and two from Europol\u2019s European Cybercrime Centre (EC3) were deployed to Spain and Bulgaria, equipped with mobile offices to support the actions on the spot. This allowed for real-time intelligence analysis and cross-checks against Europol\u2019s databases, as well as forensic support. <\/p>\n\n<p><br>\nOperation Casper began when a representative from a broadcast rights holder filed a complaint against the owner of an Internet Service Provider (ISP) located in M\u00e1laga (Spain), for illicitly distributing pay-TV channels to thousands of clients in different EU countries. Investigations revealed that the ISP owner, a Danish citizen, was the leader of a criminal network who operated on a European scale. Investigators also unveiled the existence of a second ISP in Silistra (Bulgaria) owned by the network, which was permanently connected to the ISP in Spain and provided coverage to other European countries. Both ISPs were legally established in both countries and performed legal activities while, in parallel, exploiting their capacities to carry out illegal activities.<\/p>\n\n<p>The crime group also used a network of shell companies, which relied technically on the ISPs, and were in charge of distributing the illicit TV signals to the end clients.<\/p>\n\n<p>Operation Casper represents a great example of cross-border cooperation against intellectual property rights infringements.<\/p>\n\n<h3>Intellectual property crime in the EU<\/h3>\n\n<p>Intellectual property crime is a significant problem that hits the EU particularly hard. Criminal groups get involved in these illegal activities, attracted to its relatively low risk and high levels of revenue.<br>\nTo strengthen the fight against counterfeiting and piracy online and offline, Europol and the<a class=\"external\" href=\"https:\/\/euipo.europa.eu\/ohimportal\/en\" target=\"_blank\"> European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO)<\/a> joined forces to launch the <a href=\"https:\/\/www.europol.europa.eu\/about-europol\/intellectual-property-crime-coordinated-coalition-ipc3\">Intellectual Property Crime Coordinated Coalition (IPC3<\/a>).<\/p>\n\n<p> Further details available on <a class=\"external\" href=\"https:\/\/www.policia.es\/prensa\/20170406_1.html\" target=\"_blank\">Policia\u2019s press release<\/a>.<\/p>\n\n<p> <\/p>","summary":"The crime group owned two Internet Service Providers (ISPs) in Spain and Bulgaria, that illicitly offered more than 1000 TV channels to clients across Europe using Internet Protocol television (IPTV) technology. NOT coded domain-seizure or content-delisting: NO record mentions domains, websites, apps or social accounts at all -- this network ran on two licensed ISPs, and the frontmatter agrees (results.domains_seized: 0). NOT coded intermediary-process, blocking-order, payment-disruption, end-user-action, voluntary-transfer.
JUDICIAL: arrests n=8, stated identically by all three tier-1 records. The Danish leader is inside the 8 ("'Operation Casper', som den blev kaldt, endte med 8 anholdte, deriblandt en dansker.", raw/news/2017-04-11_recordere_dansker-styrede-europas-stoerste-pirat-tv.md:935 -- not cited, tier-2 restatement). indictments not-reported -- no cited record states a charge, a referral to a prosecutor, or an open proceeding; the language is accusation-and-investigation only ("The network is accused of illicitly distributing pay-TV channels", a raw:16; "the individuals under investigation", b raw:994). `pending` was deliberately NOT used, unlike the two Italian rows in this batch (Impero, Taken Down) where the record itself describes a procedimento penale at a named stage, and unlike Aphrodite where the record states "37 others were reported to the judicial authorities": Casper has no equivalent sentence. Spanish specialised computer-crime prosecutors are named as participants in the ACTION (b raw:992), which is not a statement about proceedings. convictions/imprisonments not-reported; the page confirms the gap ("Public sources reviewed for this ingest do not disclose subsequent indictments, convictions, appeals, or asset-recovery outcomes.", op page:162). latest_record_date 2017-07-21 = the WIPO ACE/12/10 Rev. contribution, the latest cited record; every fact it carries is a restatement of the April action, so the row is effectively censored at three months after the action day.
RECONSTITUTION: not-reported. No cited record speaks to what happened to the two ISPs or the service after April 2017; the WIPO contribution three months later repeats the action-day facts and adds no status. The page's forward-looking language is about judicial follow-through ("The operation should be revisited if Spanish or Bulgarian court records become available", op page:162), not about succession or effectiveness, so open-question was not used.
⚠ CORPUS DEFECT (linkage gap + near-duplicate source pages): wiki/sources/2017-04-06_europol_operation-casper-spain-bulgaria-iptv-pay-tv-1000-channels.md is a SECOND source page in the corpus for the same 6 April 2017 Europol material about this operation, and the operation page cites only the other one (op page:97-104) (corpus-search). It is NOT cited here for two reasons: it duplicates the cited Europol release, and its capture is RECONSTRUCTION-tier by its own admission -- "Europol Operations pages SPA-rendered. Content reconstructed from multiple corroborating tier-2 outlets (TorrentFreak, Broadband TV News, Infosecurity Magazine, Trademarks & Brands Online, Advanced Television) all dated 2017-04-07 to 2017-04-11 and citing the Europol press release verbatim." (that raw:18). Its blockquotes are therefore reconstructed prose, not Europol's own wording, and they differ verbatim from the real release (e.g. "In a coordinated action, 12 searches were carried out simultaneously in Spain and Bulgaria, with investigators seizing the servers.", that raw:32) while carrying the same facts. Two source pages, two different source_urls (newsroom news item vs. Operations page), one underlying operation -- an L54-class canonicalisation question for the coordinator. Its extra claim that "Operation Casper benefited from private-sector cooperation with the English Premier League and Irdeto" (that raw:38) is true but is properly sourced from the AAPA release, which is cited.
CORPUS SEARCH ("Casper" over wiki/sources/): 10 hits. Six are the operation's own cited sources; one is the duplicate above; two mention Casper only as a comparative exemplar in other documents (2020-11-25 EC IP Action Plan, 2020-02-05 Europol Huge Hit); one (2026-01-09 boston.com) is an unrelated homonym. No other uncited source about this operation.
OTHER FIGURES (no column): more than 1,000 pay-TV channels across two legally established ISPs in Málaga (Spain) and Silistra (Bulgaria); "thousands of consumers and businesses across Europe" as the customer base (b raw:999); "The crime group also used a network of shell companies, which relied technically on the ISPs, and were in charge of distributing the illicit TV signals to the end clients." (a raw:16) -- the AAPA version says "The disbanded criminal organization also controlled three other entities that provided the content to its customers." (b raw:1005), a specific count (three) the Europol release leaves as "a network of shell companies"; no shell-company action is coded because neither record states one. Europol deployed two IPC3 and two EC3 experts with mobile offices to Spain and Bulgaria (a raw:16).

converted from paper2/coding/germany-zcb-europe-wide-cardsharing-takedown-luxtv-worldtv-2017.json (coder agent-w2-2, 2026-08-13); date_source=raw-frontmatter; source_of_record=raw/press-releases/2017-12-05_justiz-bayern_zcb-europaweit-koordinierte-massnahme-luxtv-worldtv.md; tier_basis=raw-dir:press-releases; other_cited_captures=1; quotes are the cited lines as of the coding date; stratum from wiki fields (participating_countries=4, participating_agencies=1); official_release_sourced=True. CAPTURE TIERS — both ZCB captures are USABLE, contrary to the batch warning that German ZCB captures are often reconstruction-tier digests. Each holds the publisher's full German release text under "## Extracted Text" (word_count 519 and 644, curl_cffi chrome124, http 200, storage_mode fulltext), preserves the publisher's own soft-hyphen line breaks (durch-sucht, fest-genommen, Zentral-stelle, Land-kreis) rather than normalising them, and records a cross-extraction agreement check against the Cyber-crime-DE archive walk (2017 raw:63-66, 2018 raw:61-64). I cite only German sentences from those bodies. The 2017 capture's extraction note warns that one sentence is split mid-clause by a source
(raw:39/41) and that a quotation must not span the break — I have not quoted across it. MODALITY. arrest-search: "Im Rahmen eines Ermittlungsverfahrens der Zentralstelle Cybercrime Bayern bei der Generalstaatsanwaltschaft Bamberg wurden im Rahmen einer europaweit koordinierten Maßnahme in den Abendstunden des 28.11.2017 insgesamt 15 Geschäfts- und Privaträume in Deutschland und dem europäischen Ausland (Niederlande, Lettland und Österreich) durch-sucht und umfangreiche Beweismittel sichergestellt." (2017 raw:31) and "Gegen sechs der Beschuldigten im In- und Ausland wurden Haftbefehle vollstreckt." (2017 raw:33). hosting-takedown: "Es gelang zudem, mehrere Server, über welche die kriminellen Dienstleistungen angeboten wurden, abzuschalten." plus "Zudem wurden unmittelbar bei deutschen und ausländischen Hosting-Providern, bei denen die Beschuldigten die für ihre Angebote notwendige Infrastruktur unterhielten, die inkriminierten Inhalte gesichert." (both 2017 raw:31). asset-seizure: "Im Auftrag der Zentralstelle Cybercrime Bayern wurden bei den Durchsuchungen erhebliche Vermögenswerte sichergestellt." (2017 raw:49) — Vermögenswerte is the publisher's own word for assets, distinct from the Beweismittel secured in the searches, so this one is unambiguous even under the strict reading I applied elsewhere in this batch; no figure is given. NOT coded domain-seizure, and the operation page reaches the same conclusion for the same reason (op:81, op:151): the release says the domains "sind im Internet nicht mehr erreichbar" — unreachable, which is the downstream effect of the servers being switched off — and the only Beschlagnahme it names is of content, not of a domain: "Bei Aufruf der ebenfalls genutzten Seite simsonclub.xobor.de erscheint nunmehr ein Hinweis auf die Beschlagnahme der illegalen Inhalte." (2017 raw:31). Coding a domain seizure here would put a word in the publisher's mouth that it did not use. I also did not code content-delisting for that seizure notice: simsonclub.xobor.de is a third-party forum page, but the act described is a criminal Beschlagnahme of content executed alongside the securing of content at the hosting providers, which hosting-takedown already carries — not a notice-and-takedown or platform delisting. NOT coded intermediary-process: content was secured directly at German and foreign hosting providers, but no subpoena, order or disclosure channel is named, and the operation page notes it is not stated whether that was voluntary or compelled (op:163). JUDICIAL. arrests n=6: six arrest warrants executed at home and abroad, followed by pre-trial detention — "Die Beschuldigten befinden sich seitdem in Untersuchungshaft." (2017 raw:33); the 2018 release confirms the same action date for the later defendants, "Zwei der Angeklagten, die allesamt am 28.11.2017 festgenommen worden waren, befinden sich nach wie vor in Untersuchungshaft." (2018 raw:43). The drop from six arrested to five indicted is attrition, not a count conflict. indictments n=5: "Am 15.11.2018 beginnt vor der Wirtschaftsstrafkammer des Landgerichts Regensburg die Hauptverhandlung gegen fünf Männer" (2018 raw:31) and "hat bereits im Sommer gegen fünf Männer Anklage wegen einer Vielzahl von Fällen der Bildung einer kriminellen Vereinigung, des gewerbsmäßigen Computerbetrugs, Verstößen gegen das Urhebergesetz und anderer Delikte erhoben" (2018 raw:33). convictions pending: the record states the main hearing opens on a named date before a named court — proceedings underway, not silence. imprisonments not-reported and this is the cell the v2 custodial rule decides: the only custody in the record is Untersuchungshaft (pre-trial detention) for two defendants with the remaining warrants "gegen Auflagen außer Vollzug gesetzt" (2018 raw:43), which is neither a conviction nor an imposed custodial term. The operation page is explicit that no judgment is in the corpus and that its results.convictions 0 means "a stage not reached, not an acquittal" (op:84, op:153) — I code that as pending/not-reported rather than as a zero. latest_record_date 2018-11-08. CAPTURE TIER: USABLE — measured, not assumed. The coordinator's standing warning is that German ZCB captures are often reconstruction-tier digests; this one is not. It is a curl_cffi:chrome124 HTTP 200 fulltext of justiz.bayern.de Pressemitteilung 9/2018 with the complete German release body verbatim at raw:27-47, and its Extraction Notes record a second independent extraction of the same page by the Cyber-crime-DE archive walk that agrees word for word after whitespace normalisation (raw:59-62). The notes even preserve the publisher's own typography errors rather than repairing them (the spacing error 'D er Beschuldigte' at raw:33, noted raw:63; the U+201E/U+201C quotation marks around the EG Streams unit name, noted raw:65) — the opposite of a digest. Everything on this row is raw-level; no page_only cell. MODALITY: arrest-search — "Bereits am 08.05.2018 fand unter Federführung der ZCB und der KPI Rosenheim eine groß angelegte Durchsuchungsaktion statt, über welche die Öffentlichkeit aus ermittlungstaktischen Gründen erst jetzt informiert werden kann. Dabei wurden drei Privatwohnungen und 13 Gewerbebetriebe im Bereich der Polizeipräsidien Oberbayern Süd, Oberbayern Nord, Schwaben Süd/West und in Baden-Württemberg durchsucht." (raw:39) — sixteen premises searched; note the code covers searches of premises even where no arrest is stated, and none is. hosting-takedown — "In Deutschland wurden fünf Server und im europäischen Ausland (Österreich, Frankreich, Niederlande) im Wege der Rechtshilfe vier Server beschlagnahmt." (raw:41): nine cardsharing servers seized, five domestic and four in Austria, France and the Netherlands by way of mutual legal assistance. That single sentence is also the whole international-cooperation content of the record. Did NOT code asset-seizure: the release labels the rest of the haul evidence, not assets — "Es wurden umfangreiches Beweismaterial (unter anderem 135 Receiver, zehn Computersysteme und 40 Mobiltelefone), sowie eine große Datenmenge von über 50 Terabytes sichergestellt." (raw:43); the EUR 250,000 figure is the providers' established damage, not a seizure or forfeiture, and the operation page's audit note agrees the release mentions no asset recovery at all. Did NOT code intermediary-process: Rechtshilfe here is the channel through which foreign authorities executed SEIZURES, not a subpoena or disclosure order to a host, CDN or registrar to identify an operator — coding it would double-count the same sentence already carried by hosting-takedown. BORDERLINE CALL — end-user-action NOT coded: thirteen of the sixteen searched premises were Gewerbebetriebe (raw:39) and the customer base is described as "Bisher konnten über 500 Kunden ermittelt werden, welche diese illegalen Dienste in Anspruch nahmen. Darunter befinden sich auch mehrere Gewerbebetriebe." (raw:31), so it is tempting to read the day's searches as reaching customers. The release never joins the two statements, and the operation page itself only calls the overlap a suggestion ("which suggests the customer side was itself a target of the day's measures; the release does not say the customers were charged"). Customers were IDENTIFIED, not acted against, on the face of the record — not coded. No domain, portal or platform name appears anywhere in the release, so no domain-seizure, blocking-order or content-delisting is available (the operation page carries the same audit note for domains_seized). JUDICIAL: arrests not-reported — the release names one Beschuldigter, aged 27, and describes only searches and seizures; it never says whether he was detained. This is source silence, not a stated zero, which is exactly what the operation page's 2026-08-02 audit note records ("arrests is flagged missing, not verified zero"); empty cites per the protocol's silence rule, and the frontmatter seed results.arrests: 0 is NOT read as a source statement. indictments pending — DEFINITIONAL CALL, flagged for the audit: the record states a formal prosecutor-led criminal investigation is underway against an identified accused and has been for a year — "Bereits seit Mai 2017 ermitteln die fünfköpfige Ermittlungsgruppe ... und die spezialisierten Staatsanwälte der bei der Generalstaatsanwaltschaft Bamberg eingerichteten Zentralstelle Cybercrime Bayern gegen einen 27-Jährigen aus dem südlichen Landkreis Rosenheim" (raw:31) and "Die umfangreichen und technisch komplexen Ermittlungen wegen gewerbsmäßigen Computerbetrugs werden seit rund einem Jahr von der Zentralstelle Cybercrime Bayern und dem K 11 der Kriminalpolizeiinspektion Rosenheim geführt." (raw:37), with the data evaluation expected to run several more months (raw:43). A German Ermittlungsverfahren conducted by the Staatsanwaltschaft against a named Beschuldigter is the pre-charge phase of criminal proceedings, structurally the same object as the Bulgarian pre-trial proceedings coded pending on the bulgaria-gdbop-europol-huge-hit-iptv-distributors-2020 row — so pending, for consistency across the two. It is distinguished from the disney-star-dubai-police row, where the only forward-looking statement was police investigating whether OTHER unidentified individuals were linked, which is not proceedings against anyone. No count is coded: no charge has been filed, and the frontmatter seed indictments: 0 remains correct as a count. convictions and imprisonments not-reported — no charge, trial, judgment or sentence is in any record; the operation page states the Bavarian archive walk of 292 releases found no later release on this case, and the corpus's other ZCB indictment release (wiki/sources/2018-11-08_justiz-bayern_zcb-cardsharing-anklage-regensburg.md, five men charged to the Landgericht Regensburg) belongs to the SEPARATE 2017 LuxTV/WorldTV case — its own source page says so, its defendants were all arrested 28.11.2017 by the Polizeipräsidium München, and its foreign set is Latvia rather than Austria/France/Netherlands. It is NOT a follow-on to this row and is not coded here. Right-censored at 2018-05-14, six days after the action. latest_record_date 2018-05-14 = the release byline, the only record. RECONSTITUTION not-reported: no cited record speaks to what happened to the cardsharing service after 8 May 2018 — the release does not even name a platform or domain that could be observed up or down, and the archive walk found no later release on the case. CORPUS SEARCH ('Rosenheim', 'EG Streams', 'cardsharing'/'Card-Sharing' across wiki/sources/): five files hit — the cited release, the 2017-12-05 LuxTV/WorldTV Europe-wide action and its 2018-11-08 Regensburg indictment follow-on (both the OTHER ZCB case), a 2018 Brazilian STJ signal-sharing decision, and a 2019 Eurojust AAPA report. NO LINKAGE GAP for this row. Noted for the coordinator: the record's four foreign server seizures were each executed by an authority in Austria, France and the Netherlands and the release names none of them, so this row's cross-border modality is country- and instrument-level only.

arrests.quote: > After a year-long complex investigation coordinated by Europol, authorities in Hampshire, south east England, Scotland and Ireland have arrested six, suspected of illicitly distributing premium TV channels by using Internet Protocol television (IPTV) technology.
quotes: > After a year-long complex investigation coordinated by Europol, authorities in Hampshire, south east England, Scotland and Ireland have arrested six, suspected of illicitly distributing premium TV channels by using Internet Protocol television (IPTV) technology.

> Police officers carried out house searches on 11 September at different locations in Ireland and the UK. A man and a woman from Bursledon were arrested by the Hampshire County Council's Trading Standards Service and Hampshire Constabulary. Four people were detained in Crumlin and Ashbourne (Ireland) and also several actions took place in Scotland. During the house searches, computer equipment and cash was seized and several bank accounts were frozen.

An Garda Síochána, working with the Garda Intellectual Property Crime Unit (Garda National Bureau of Criminal Investigation), today arrested four people — two women aged 37 and 40 years and two men aged 42 and 45 years — as part of a coordinated investigation into the illegal distribution of premium TV channels through Internet Protocol Television (IPTV) technology.

Two houses were raided as part of the operation today, one in Crumlin (Dublin) and one in Ashbourne (Co. Meath). Searches were also carried out at the homes of the arrested individuals.

> Police officers carried out house searches on 11 September at different locations in Ireland and the UK. During the house searches, computer equipment and cash was seized and several bank accounts were frozen.
Six bank accounts and two credit union accounts have been identified, and freezing orders pursuant to Money Laundering legislation have been invoked. In total, €84,000 has been frozen as a result.

rows.notes: converted from paper2/coding/spain-denmark-uk-policia-nacional-premier-league-iptv-server-farms-2019.json (coder agent-w2-1, 2026-08-13); date_source=raw-frontmatter; source_of_record=raw/news/2019-03-22_aapa_premier-league-irdeto-iptv-raids-spain-denmark-uk.md; tier_basis=raw-dir:news; other_cited_captures=0; quotes are the cited lines as of the coding date; stratum from wiki fields (participating_countries=3, participating_agencies=6); official_release_sourced=False. CAPTURE TIER: RECONSTRUCTION. The single capture's frontmatter claims "fetch_method: WebFetch (verbatim capture)" and "content_format: AAPA-hosted press release text", but the body is not the release — it is an agent-authored digest of it: six analyst headings (Operation Summary / Arrests & Charges / Infrastructure Uncovered / International Criminal Network / Financial Impact / Named Quotes / AAPA Role) over bullet lists in label-colon-value form ("Subscription cost: starting at 40 Euros per month" raw:33; "Estimated revenue: approximately 8 million euros" raw:41; "Imprisonments in Spain: 3 individuals" raw:43). Only the two attributed quotes at raw:47 and raw:49 are marked verbatim, and neither carries a coded fact. Everything on this row is therefore page_only with the (reconstruction) marker. The operation page independently records that no tier-1 record exists for this action ("No published Europol own-domain press release for this specific action day — tier-1 confirmation unavailable"), and source_tier is 2. MODALITY: arrest-search — "Spanish National Police, working with law enforcement in the United Kingdom and Denmark, Europol, the Premier League, and Irdeto, conducted raids at 14 locations across Spain, Denmark, and the United Kingdom." (raw:21) with five arrests (raw:25). asset-seizure — "Seized assets: 12 high-end vehicles, real estate, blocked bank accounts" (raw:42): vehicles, real property and frozen accounts are proceeds-side assets, not evidence, so this is the row's second modality (contrast the Singapore ISDs and the German receivers, which were contraband/evidence and were not coded). BORDERLINE CALL — hosting-takedown NOT coded, and this one runs against the wiki page: the record's server-farm material sits under the heading "## Infrastructure Uncovered" (raw:27) and states only what was FOUND — "11 server farms distributed globally" and "Some facilities contained over 44 servers" (raw:29-30). No sentence in the capture says a server, farm or hosting account was seized, shut down or taken offline; the words 'offline', 'shut', 'dismantle' and 'takedown' do not appear in the capture body at all. The operation page's Results section nevertheless asserts "11 server farms identified globally; service taken offline" and "800+ TV channels removed from illegal distribution to 30+ country market" — neither clause is in the record, and the same page's frontmatter carries servers_seized: 0, contradicting its own prose. Coded from the record, not the page. No domain-seizure, blocking-order, content-delisting, payment-disruption, intermediary-process or end-user-action is stated anywhere. JUDICIAL: arrests n=5 — "Five individuals arrested for crimes including belonging to a criminal organisation, intellectual property theft, fraud, and money laundering." (raw:25). indictments pending — the second sentence of the same line, "Three individuals were detained and imprisoned in Spain following court appearances.", puts the case before a Spanish court within days of the raids; that is proceedings underway, not a count of charges filed, and the arrest offences listed are the grounds of arrest rather than filed charges. convictions not-reported — no record states a verdict, plea or sentence for anyone. imprisonments not-reported, AND THIS CONTRADICTS THE OPERATION PAGE, deliberately: the page's frontmatter carries results.imprisonments: 3 and its Results section reads "3 detained and imprisoned in Spain following court appearances", but the underlying record is an action-week press release describing detainees brought before a court immediately after the raids — under Spanish procedure that is prisión provisional (pre-trial remand ordered by the investigating judge), not a custodial sentence. The protocol defines imprisonments as custodial components actually IMPOSED, i.e. sentencing outcomes; a stage-3 conviction does not exist on this row, so a stage-4 imprisonment cannot. Reading "detained and imprisoned" as three custodial sentences would manufacture three sentences out of a remand order and would make this row report imprisonments with no conviction anywhere behind them. The three remand detentions are recorded here instead, and the frontmatter seed is flagged for the coordinator as a probable mis-seed. latest_record_date 2019-03-22 = Irdeto release date (AAPA republished 2019-03-25 per raw:17; the earlier date is the byline). Right-censored on the action week — the record is days old relative to the raids, which is why every downstream stage is silent. RECONSTITUTION not-reported: no cited record speaks to the service's status after March 2019, no successor is named, and the capture's forward-looking content is limited to two promotional quotes. CORPUS SEARCH ('Irdeto', 'Premier League', 'server farm' across wiki/sources/ and raw/): no uncited record of this action. The nearest neighbours are all different cases — Operation Casper (2017 Spain-Bulgaria, same Premier League/Irdeto/AAPA pattern, two source pages), the Kenya MultiChoice/Irdeto matters (2024-2025), Cyber Patrol (2025 Portugal-Spain), Kratos 2 (2026), and the Audiencia Nacional RapidIPTV case (wiki/sources/2022-07-22_poderjudicial-cgpj_audiencia-nacional-procesamiento-rapidiptv-15-millones-dash-irani.md), which I checked specifically as a possible judicial follow-on and rejected: RapidIPTV is a different network (9 defendants, ~2 million users, ~40 server farms across 14 countries, EUR 15M proceeds, Nagravision as the complaining vendor) and its own operation page dates the case from 2020-01-01, after this action. NO LINKAGE GAP. Noted for the coordinator: this row's entire evidentiary base is one reconstruction-tier digest of a private rights-holder's press release, with no LE publisher of record on either side of the three raid jurisdictions.

converted from paper2/coding/bulgaria-gdbop-europol-end-of-broadcast-iptv-cable-piracy-2019.json (coder agent-w2-4, 2026-08-13); date_source=raw-frontmatter; source_of_record=raw/press-releases/2019-06-17_europol_end-of-broadcast-bulgaria-iptv-cable-operators-ipc3-aapa.md; tier_basis=raw-dir:press-releases; other_cited_captures=0; quotes are the cited lines as of the coding date; stratum from wiki fields (participating_countries=1, participating_agencies=5); official_release_sourced=True. Single cited source: wiki/sources/2019-06-17_europol_end-of-broadcast-bulgaria-iptv-cable-operators-ipc3-aapa.md -> raw/press-releases/2019-06-17_europol_end-of-broadcast-bulgaria-iptv-cable-operators-ipc3-aapa.md. CAPTURE TIER: mixed within one file. raw:26-34 is a verbatim body recovered from the AAPA mirror of the Europol release (the capture states "Verbatim content recovered from the AAPA mirror, which reproduces the Europol press release in full", raw:18) and is treated as USABLE; raw:36-56 ("Key extracted facts", "Tier-1 status verification") is agent-authored digest with post-hoc comparative claims (e.g. the TorrentFreak-sourced rights-holder list at raw:48, and the raw:54 comparison to the 2019 Italian Black IPTV operation) and is RECONSTRUCTION-tier -- not cited. Europol's own SPA page did not resolve in WebFetch (raw:18) = the L52/L11 Europol pattern; the mirror is the only body text.
MODALITY: hosting-takedown only. Source verb: "The entire illegal hardware infrastructure used for the criminal activity, including all servers used to distribute the channels, has been seized." (raw:30). NO arrest-search coded: the release's only action verb for persons/premises is "police officers from the Bulgarian Cybercrime Department from the General Directorate Combating Organised Crime of the Ministry of Interior carried out a joint action against five cable operators in Bulgaria" (raw:26) -- "joint action" with no arrest, raid, or house-search verb anywhere in the body. The operation page's frontmatter carries enforcement_type: search-seizure and mechanisms_used: [[search-seizure]] (op page:14, 44); per CODING.md's frontmatter-seed rule the modality follows the source text's verbs, and the source text does not state a search or an arrest. Physical seizure of head-end hardware at five operators plainly happened somewhere, but the record does not say premises were searched, so the inference is left uncoded and flagged here. No domain, blocking, delisting, payment, or asset (non-evidence) action stated.
JUDICIAL: arrests not-reported -- the release is silent on arrests (frontmatter results.arrests: 0 is a seed, not an affirmative "no arrests" statement, so `none-stated` was not used). indictments = pending, PAGE-ONLY and flagged as a possible corpus defect: the claim "Administrative and criminal procedures initiated against the five operators." appears twice in the wiki page (frontmatter results.other, op page:63; Results and Impact, op page:129) and appears NOWHERE in the only cited record -- the Europol/AAPA body (raw:26-34) says nothing about administrative or criminal procedure. Coded as `pending` under the "proceedings are underway" rule with page_only=true; a coordinator repairing the wiki side should either source or withdraw that line. convictions/imprisonments not-reported; the page itself flags the gap: "It is unclear from public reporting how many of the five operators were criminally prosecuted versus only administratively sanctioned." (op page:160). latest_record_date 2019-06-17 = the single cited record's byline.
RECONSTITUTION: not-reported. No cited record speaks to what happened after June 2019. The page's Contradictions section raises prosecution-breakdown questions, not succession/effectiveness of the takedown, so `open-question` was not used. The page's remark that the relationship to Huge Hit (Feb 2020) is "*highly likely* a continued enforcement arc against the Bulgarian illegal-IPTV ecosystem" (op page:161) is about the enforcement series, not about this network reconstituting -- notes only.
CORPUS SEARCH ("End of Broadcast", Kardzhali, Gotse Delchev, GDBOP over wiki/sources/): no uncited in-corpus source page covers this action. The four other hits -- 2017-04-06_europol_operation-casper..., 2020-02-05_europol_huge-hit-bulgaria..., 2019-03-22_aapa_premier-league-irdeto..., 2020-11-25_ec-europa-eu_ip-action-plan... -- name "End of Broadcast" only in comparative prose about their own different operations. No linkage gap.
OTHER FIGURES (not coded, no column): five cable operators across eight cities, "more than 60 premium TV channels", "More than 700 000 subscribers", damage "over 10 million Bulgarian leva (approximately €5 million)" (raw:28, 32); worldwide mobile-app redistribution alongside cable (raw:30). [2026-08-17 coordinator: indictments reset pending->not-reported. The cell cited the operation page's line 'Administrative and criminal procedures initiated against the five operators', which the page WITHDREW on 2026-08-15 (no capture carries it); surfaced by register_from_ic resolving cites at the coding-date blob. The Europol capture (raw/press-releases/2019-06-17_europol_end-of-broadcast-bulgaria-iptv-cable-operators-ipc3-aapa.md:26) says the police acted 'Under the supervision of the Bulgarian Supreme Prosecutor's Office of Cassation' -- supervision of an action, not a proceeding stated in its own words; a coder who reads BG prosecutor supervision as pre-trial proceedings (CODING.md pending floor, 'BG pre-trial proceedings') could code pending referral-inferred from that line; recorded here as the alternative reading, not applied.]

reconstitution.quote: Eurojust went into action in September last year with the coordination of judicial investigations and cooperation against Organised Crime Groups (OGCs), who have been expanding their illegal activities into fraud and copyright piracy with pay-TV and streaming services. In a major operation in September 2019 led by the Italian desk at Eurojust, over 200 servers were taken down to prevent the fraud from propagating. The Agency was recently awarded by the AUDIOVISUAL ANTI-PIRACY ASSOCIATION (AAPA) for its work in this connection.
quotes: Eurojust went into action in September last year with the coordination of judicial investigations and cooperation against Organised Crime Groups (OGCs), who have been expanding their illegal activities into fraud and copyright piracy with pay-TV and streaming services. In a major operation in September 2019 led by the Italian desk at Eurojust, over 200 servers were taken down to prevent the fraud from propagating. The Agency was recently awarded by the AUDIOVISUAL ANTI-PIRACY ASSOCIATION (AAPA) for its work in this connection.

Investigations into this particular network have been ongoing for some time, leading to the further action taken this week. Copyright holders, including major European pay-TV channels and American film studios, have lodged complaints with the authorities in Italy against the large scale piracy that has been depriving them of tens of millions of euros.

Eurojust continues to support the crackdown on large-scale piracy and fraud with pay-TV and film streaming, by coordinating an action day at the request of the Italian authorities. Over 5.550 computer servers, which were used to transmit and store television broadcasts, live sports games and films without paying the legitimate copyright holders, have been taken down in Italy, Bulgaria, France, Germany, Lithuania, Malta, Romania, Slovenia, Sweden and The Netherlands. The online streaming services have now been blocked for customers in Italy, who watched the television feed through cheap set-top boxes, paying far below market subscription fees.

CODED FROM THE 18 SEPTEMBER 2019 RECORDS ONLY. I read paper2/coding/operation-perfect-storm-pay-tv-piracy-2019.json for its capture-tier findings, as the task permits, and re-verified every tier claim in it against the captures myself (all three confirmed). No cell value was carried across: this row's modality set, its arrests value and its reconstitution value all differ from the parent's, and each was re-derived from the 2019 records.

CAPTURE TIERS, verified file by file.
USABLE (1) raw/press-releases/2019-09-18_poliziadistato_italy-eclissi-iptv-paytv-takedown.md -- own-domain Polizia di Stato release; verbatim Italian body at raw:16-36 with a working English translation below it. I cite the Italian.
USABLE (2) raw/press-releases/2019-09-18_gdf_operazione-black-iptv-xtream-codes.md -- frontmatter carries verbatim: true; full Italian body at raw:15-25.
CAPTURE-UNUSABLE (3) raw/press-releases/2019-09-18_eurojust_eurojust-helps-unravel-massive-trans-european-pay-tv-fraud.md -- despite text_status: parsed and word_count: 623, its "## Extracted Text" (raw:33-153) is the Internet Archive capture banner, the Archive Team collection blurb and the Eurojust site menu, with no article text at all. The only case prose in the file is the ingest agent's own summary at raw:27-29, which is RECONSTRUCTION tier. Nothing is cited from it.
CONSEQUENCE, and it lands on this component's own split rationale: the census entry for this component (tools/paper2_dataset.py:152) describes it as "200+ servers seized, 150+ PayPal accounts blocked", and the second of those two figures exists in NO usable capture. "blocked over 150 PayPal accounts" and "identified 22 suspects" appear only in that agent digest (raw:29) and, restated, on the operation page (op:123, op:157). See payment-disruption below.
CORPUS SEARCH over wiki/sources/ for Perfect Storm | Eclissi | Xtream | Black IPTV returned 39 files; none other is a record OF the September 2019 action. Two near-misses checked and rejected: 2019-11-21_eurojust_tackling-audio-visual-piracy-aapa-iptv-expertise (a 20-21 November 2019 AAPA seminar; says nothing about this network's post-action status) and 2019-04-25_ustr_2018-notorious-markets-list-vader-streams-omniverse-xtream-codes (predates the action, so history, not durability).

SCOPE -- why the GdF "Black IPTV" release is coded as a record of THIS action. The operation page flags the Black IPTV = Perfect Storm name equation as editorial inference (op:26); that caution is about the NAME, which no cell here relies on. What the cells rely on is that the two releases describe the same day's execution: same date, same platform architecture (an administration-panel product supplied by a company fronted by two Greek nationals -- "una società di diritto bulgaro, gestita dai due cittadini greci" at polizia raw:28, "la piattaforma Xtream Codes, ideata da 2 cittadini greci" at gdf raw:19), the same 80 domains/sites, the same five foreign jurisdictions executing simultaneously that morning, the same named rightsholders, the same ~5 million Italian subscribers. DIVERGENCES, recorded rather than reconciled: the Polizia names the Rome PPO as coordinating prosecutor while the GdF names the Naples PPO as directing prosecutor; servers are "oltre 200 Server" (polizia raw:20) against "183 server" (gdf raw:23), the GdF figure being the more specific but counting only servers "dedicati alla riproduzione e diffusione dei flussi audiovisivi"; searches are 20 across Europe at company and provider premises (polizia raw:20) against "25 gli obiettivi delle perquisizioni odierne sul territorio nazionale" (gdf raw:25), which are different populations rather than a contradiction; turnover is about two million euros a month (polizia raw:22) against "circa 60 milioni di Euro annui" (gdf raw:19). No cell on this row turns on which figure is right, so both are recorded and neither is coded as a count.

MODALITY, taken from the source text's verbs.
domain-seizure -- "Nell'operazione sono stati sequestrati oltre 200 Server e 80 domini e sono state effettuate 20 perquisizioni in tutta Europa presso sedi di società e provider." (polizia raw:20) and "oltre al sequestro ed all'oscuramento della intera piattaforma Xtream Codes, di 80 siti internet e di 183 server dedicati alla riproduzione e diffusione dei flussi audiovisivi" (gdf raw:23). Judicial seizure of 80 domains/sites: state process, control transferred.
hosting-takedown -- the same two lines carry the servers (200+ / 183), and polizia raw:20 states the result: "rendere inattiva la complessa infrastruttura tecnologica operante a livello internazionale".
arrest-search -- "Oltre 100 militari del Nucleo Speciale Tutela Privacy e Frodi Tecnologiche e dei reparti territoriali della Guardia di Finanza stanno eseguendo, in queste ore, provvedimenti di perquisizione locale, informatica e conseguente sequestro" (gdf raw:15); "25 gli obiettivi delle perquisizioni odierne sul territorio nazionale" (gdf raw:25); the eight EIOs executed abroad "nei confronti di 3 aziende e 5 persone fisiche" (gdf raw:23); and the 20 European searches at company and provider premises (polizia raw:20). Searches and seizures against persons and premises; neither release claims an arrest.
asset-seizure -- "mirano ad aggredire i proventi illecitamente conseguiti dall'organizzazione mediante il sequestro di 197 rapporti finanziari tra account paypal, postepay e conti corrente" (gdf raw:25): an explicit attack on proceeds by seizure of financial accounts, not evidence collection.
NOT payment-disruption, and this is the closest call on the row. The census rationale for this component says PayPal accounts were blocked, but no publisher text in any usable capture uses the verb blocked or gives the figure 150. The only usable account of that measure is the GdF's, which frames it as sequestro of 197 rapporti finanziari aimed at the proceeds -- asset-seizure, already coded. "blocked over 150 PayPal accounts" exists solely in the agent digest inside the unusable Eurojust capture (raw:29) and, restated, on the operation page (op:157). Because the entire distinction between asset-seizure and payment-disruption here would rest on a verb no publisher wrote, and CODING.md fixes the modality to the source text's verbs, the measure is coded once, as asset-seizure. The two figures are plausibly the same measure, 150+ PayPal accounts being a subset of the 197 paypal/postepay/bank relationships.
NOT end-user-action -- gdf raw:25 closes with "nei confronti dei fruitori del servizio è prevista la reclusione da sei mesi a 3 anni e la multa fino a 25.822 Euro": the statutory penalty range applicable to subscribers, i.e. what the law allows, not a measure applied to any identified end user in this action.
NOT blocking-order -- oscuramento appears only in the same breath as sequestro of the platform, the sites and the servers (gdf raw:23): control taken, not access blocked with the site left standing. No DNS/ISP order or dynamic injunction is described.
NOT intermediary-process -- the eight EIOs were executed as searches and seizures against companies and natural persons (gdf raw:23), which arrest-search carries; no disclosure request to a registrar, host or CDN is described.
NOT content-delisting -- no notice-and-takedown, delisting or platform-side removal in either 2019 release; the 350 Telegram channels belong to the 2020 component.

JUDICIAL.
arrests not-reported -- neither release states an arrest, and neither describes the outcome completely enough for the absence to be a fact: the GdF release is written while the searches are still running, "stanno eseguendo, in queste ore" (gdf raw:15). Silence, so not-reported rather than none-stated.
indictments pending -- "Nei confronti dei responsabili dell' organizzazione si procede per Associazione a delinquere finalizzata alla riproduzione e commercializzazione illecita di IPTV con la circostanza aggravata del reato trasnazionale" (gdf raw:25). Italian "si procede per" is prosecutor-led, pre-charge proceedings language; under CODING.md's non-common-law mapping this sits at the indictments stage with value pending (referral-inferred). No count: the record does not enumerate the responsabili, and the unusable digest's 22 identified suspects is not used.
convictions / imprisonments not-reported -- no cited record reaches trial or sentence. The reclusione da sei mesi a 3 anni at gdf raw:25 is a statutory range for service users, not a sentence imposed on anyone, and must not be read as an imprisonment.
latest_record_date 2020-11-11 -- the latest publication date among THIS row's cited records is the Eurojust release cited for reconstitution, not the action-day releases.

RECONSTITUTION relaunch-reported, as_of 2020-11-11. The evidence postdates the coded action by fourteen months and comes from a usable capture. Eurojust's November 2020 release states what the 2019 action did -- "In a major operation in September 2019 led by the Italian desk at Eurojust, over 200 servers were taken down to prevent the fraud from propagating." (raw/press-releases/2020-11-11_eurojust_new-major-crackdown-on-fraud-with-illegal-use-of-pay-tv-signals.md:45) -- and then that "Investigations into this particular network have been ongoing for some time, leading to the further action taken this week." (raw/press-releases/2020-11-11_eurojust_new-major-crackdown-on-fraud-with-illegal-use-of-pay-tv-signals.md:47), the further action having taken down "Over 5.550 computer servers" (raw/press-releases/2020-11-11_eurojust_new-major-crackdown-on-fraud-with-illegal-use-of-pay-tv-signals.md:39): the same network, running roughly twenty-seven times the 2019 server count, fourteen months after the 2019 infrastructure was reported rendered inoperative. Eurojust's National Member for Italy frames it the same way: "After the major operation in Italy of last year, we haven’t stopped to assist and support our national authorities. We have taken on the challenge to continue our work, as we can’t be satisfied by a single operation" (raw/press-releases/2020-11-11_eurojust_new-major-crackdown-on-fraud-with-illegal-use-of-pay-tv-signals.md:49). HONEST LIMIT ON THE CODE: no record uses the word relaunch and none names a successor platform, so the alternative reading -- that part of the network was never taken down in 2019 rather than rebuilt after it -- cannot be excluded from the record. That is precisely the distinction the withdrawn target-persisted category named; with it withdrawn, and with the record affirmatively resolving this target's post-action status rather than leaving it open, relaunch-reported is the code the Column-3 precedence rule gives, and the ambiguity is recorded here instead of in a new category. Note also that the action and the frontmatter announced date coincide for this component (2019-09-18), so table S5b has nothing to flag here -- the S5b ambiguity belonged to the undivided parent, whose announced was 2021-10.

PARTICIPATING COUNTRIES ESTABLISHED FOR THIS COMPONENT: SIX -- Italy, France, Netherlands, Germany, Bulgaria, Greece. "Insieme alla Polizia postale italiana hanno partecipato alle indagini anche le Polizie e delle Autorità giudiziarie di Francia, Paesi Bassi, Germania, Bulgaria e Grecia." (polizia raw:18), independently corroborated by the GdF, whose eight EIOs "sono stati eseguiti simultaneamente questa mattina in Olanda, Francia, Grecia, Germania e Bulgaria dalle rispettive polizie giudiziarie" (gdf raw:23). Each of the six has a named or expressly identified LE/judicial actor: Italy through the Polizia Postale with the Rome PPO and the GdF Nucleo Speciale with the Naples PPO, the other five through their own police and judicial authorities. Lithuania, Romania, Slovenia, Sweden and Malta appear in NO 2019 record; they enter only with the 2020 component. The operation page's ten-country frontmatter list (op:35-45) is therefore the union of the two actions and over-attributes four participants to this one.

rows.title_original: Huge hit to illegal IPTV distributors in Bulgaria — €650 000 in penalties for one of the six companies involved in the illegal activity (5 February 2020)
rows.scope_reason: IC census row: pool tag illegal-iptv-ic; medium defaults to iptv-service (re-read as found)

indictments.quote: > Six pre-trial proceedings were opened against the suspects.
quotes: > Six pre-trial proceedings were opened against the suspects.

modality_quotes: > The investigation targeted six companies active in the Bulgarian cities of Sofia and Varna and the region of Burgas. The national authorities carried out 17 house searches and seized a large number of documents and digital information.
rows.notes: converted from paper2/coding/bulgaria-gdbop-europol-huge-hit-iptv-distributors-2020.json (coder agent-w2-1, 2026-08-13); date_source=raw-frontmatter; source_of_record=raw/press-releases/2020-02-05_europol_huge-hit-bulgaria-iptv-distributors-650k-eur-ipc3.md; tier_basis=raw-dir:press-releases; other_cited_captures=0; quotes are the cited lines as of the coding date; stratum from wiki fields (participating_countries=1, participating_agencies=4); official_release_sourced=True. CAPTURE TIER: RECONSTRUCTION — the single capture presents a section headed 'Europol press release — extracted body' with blockquoted paragraphs (raw:24-34), but it carries no fetch metadata at all (no http_status, no content_hash, no fetcher, no word_count) and the operation page's own challenges_encountered records why: "Europol.int returned a JS-only loading state during initial WebFetch (consistent with L11 patterns); content verified through Sofia Globe, BroadbandTVNews, Advanced Television, and WebSearch index extracts." (wiki/operations/bulgaria-gdbop-europol-huge-hit-iptv-distributors-2020.md:72). So the blockquotes were assembled from tier-2 mirrors and WebSearch index extracts, not extracted from the own-domain document — the WebSearch-summary provenance tell. The trailing blockquote raw:34 ("This is Bulgaria's third successful Europol-supported operation against illegal IPTV distributors within the past year, following the End of Broadcast operation (June 2019) and earlier actions.") reads as summarizing prose rather than release copy, corroborating the tier. Everything on this row is therefore page-level support: page_only true throughout, with the (reconstruction) marker on each cite. This is an L52/L11 case, not an L57 nav shell — the capture is not empty, it is second-hand. MODALITY: arrest-search only — "The national authorities carried out 17 house searches and seized a large number of documents and digital information." (raw:26). Did NOT code asset-seizure for the fine: "One of the six companies involved was fined €650 000." (raw:28) is an imposed monetary penalty, not a freeze or forfeiture of assets tied to this action (same call as the Singapore row, where fines were held to be penalties). The seized documents and digital information are evidence, not assets. Did NOT code hosting-takedown: no server, hosting or infrastructure seizure or shutdown is stated anywhere in the record — 'digital information' is evidentiary material taken in the house searches, and the operation-page frontmatter agrees (servers_seized: 0, domains_seized: 0). Did NOT code end-user-action: the 30 000 subscribers were IDENTIFIED from the evidence ("The examination of the evidence concluded that at least 30 000 people were subscribed to the illegally distributed signal.", raw:28), with no action stated against any of them. No blocking, delisting, payment or intermediary step appears in the record — this is a pure search-and-evidence action plus a company fine, which is why the operation-page enforcement_type reads search-seizure + administrative-penalty. JUDICIAL: arrests not-reported — no arrest is stated in any record; the operation page's frontmatter seed results.arrests: 0 is a seed, not a source statement, and the release is simply silent (empty cites per the protocol's silence rule). indictments pending — "Six pre-trial proceedings were opened against the suspects." (raw:32) states criminal proceedings are underway against identified suspects; under Bulgarian procedure досъдебно производство (pre-trial proceedings) is the pre-charge investigative phase, so this is proceedings-underway support for pending rather than a count of charges filed, and it is NOT coded as n=6 indictments (the six are proceedings, and they map to the six COMPANIES, not to six charged individuals). Borderline call flagged. convictions and imprisonments not-reported: no cited record states any trial outcome, and the operation page's own open questions confirm the criminal track for five of the six companies is unspecified in public reporting ("The criminal-procedure track for the other five companies is not specified in public reporting (administrative vs. criminal).", operation page:154). Right-censored 2020-02-05, five days after the action month opened. latest_record_date 2020-02-05 = Europol byline and the only record date; the Sofia Globe mirror listed as source_url_secondary carries the same date. RECONSTITUTION not-reported: no cited record speaks to what happened to the six companies or the illegal signal distribution after February 2020; the later Bulgarian operations in the corpus (Kratos 2, 2026) are separate census operations against different targets, not durability evidence for these six companies. CORPUS SEARCH ('Huge Hit', 'GDBOP', '650 000'/'€650' across wiki/sources/ and raw/): eleven files mention GDBOP or Huge Hit, but every one of them is either a different Bulgarian operation (Casper 2017, End of Broadcast 2019-06, Kratos 2 2026-06, the 2026-01-30 justice.gov Bulgarian sites takedown), an organisation page for GDBOP (netlaw-bg x2, gdbop-bg, bta-bg restructuring), or an EU policy document listing Huge Hit in a roll-up of operations (2020-11-25 IP Action Plan). None of them adds a record of this action. NO LINKAGE GAP — the operation page cites the only same-operation source in the corpus. Noted for the coordinator: source_count is 1 for a row whose sole capture is reconstruction-tier, so this row's entire evidentiary base is second-hand; a Camoufox re-fetch of the europol.int newsroom URL would promote it.

rows.title_original: Nielegalnie rozprowadzał sygnał telewizyjny. Łączne straty, jakie poniosły firmy z branży mediów, szacowane są na kwotę około 6 mln złotych

arrests.quote: Policjanci zwalczający przestępczość gospodarczą z Komendy Wojewódzkiej Policji w Olsztynie zatrzymali 49-latka podejrzanego o "sharing".

indictments.quote: Zatrzymanej osobie przedstawiono zarzuty z art. 299§1 i §6 kk oraz z art. 6 ust. 1 Ustawy o ochronie niektórych usług świadczonych drogą elektroniczną opartych lub polegających na dostępie warunkowym.

modality_quotes: W wyniku przeszukań zrealizowanych na terenie 3 województw zlikwidowano trzy serwery sharingowe obsługujące około 800 użytkowników, zabezpieczono szereg przedmiotów w postaci urządzeń służących do rozprowadzania sygnału telewizyjnego, dekodery telewizyjne, dokumenty, telefony, karty SIM, komputery pieniądze oraz cyfrową walutę BitCoin.

Na poczet przyszłych kar i grzywien w ramach postępowania przygotowawczego Prokuratura Okręgowa w Olsztynie zabezpieczyła kryptowalutę BitCoin o wartości około 600 tysięcy złotych, nieruchomości i pojazd o łącznej wartości około 400 tysięcy złotych.
rows.notes: publish_date 'Data publikacji 24.02.2020'; no action date given. Poland only; named bodies with a role: KWP Olsztyn (executing), Prokuratura Okręgowa w Olsztynie (jointly conducting, supervising, secured assets), Stowarzyszenie Sygnał (rights-holder association whose representatives took part in the searches - named rights-holder, counts), Sąd Okręgowy w Olsztynie (ordered the 3-month tymczasowe aresztowanie) -> cooperative on orgs. arrests n=1 (49-year-old detained; remand = arrest stage). indictments n=1: PL 'przedstawiono zarzuty' = charges presented in preparatory proceedings (art. 299 kk money laundering + art. 6 ust. 1 conditional-access act) - a filed charge in the Polish system; the coordinator may re-map to pending if 'zarzuty' is treated as pre-indictment. hosting-takedown: three sharing servers 'zlikwidowano' (~800 users). asset-seizure: BTC ~PLN 600k + real estate and vehicle ~PLN 400k secured toward future penalties (money seized in the search is evidence). Losses ~PLN 6M. Users not stated as subject to any measure. No conviction/durability statement. modality_quotes: Durante los dos registros domiciliarios practicados por la Policía Nacional en los domicilios de los dos investigados, se cortó la señal ilícita que administraban y redistribuían

Grep '500.000 usuarios' hits spain-europol-ace-iptv-malaga-resellers-malta-uk-portugal-cyprus-greece-2022 but that is the October 2022 Malaga/ACE/Europol ring (500K subscribers, since 2012) -- a different action from this March 2020 Córdoba/Málaga case (2 arrests, ~300 servers, 20,000 connected users, capacity 500,000); verdict new. Judicial: 2 detained + 1 'investigada' (not detained; ES investigado status is pre-charge and not an arrest) -> arrests n=2; nothing on charges/outcomes -> not-reported. Sold IPTV-ready equipment via a web plus redistributed signal (15,000 live channels).

modality_quotes: > Europe-wide operation Aphrodite has brought together 21 countries* to target counterfeit goods trafficking. The eight-month operation was co-led by the Italian Finance Corps (Guardia di Finanza) and the Irish National Police (An Garda Síochána) with support from Europol. From December 2019 to July 2020, law enforcement authorities tracked online sales of a large variety of counterfeit items, culminating in checks in warehouses, shops and marketplaces in Belgium, Cyprus, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Portugal, Romania and Spain.

> The operation led to 123 social media accounts and 36 websites selling counterfeit products to be taken down. During the operation, law enforcement authorities seized nearly 28 million illegal and counterfeit goods among which were 800 000 counterfeit items of clothing, sportswear, footwear, personal accessories, **IPTV set-top boxes** and toys. Ten people were arrested in Greece and 37 others were reported to the judicial authorities in Greece, Italy and Portugal. More than €700 000 was also seized.

In total, 6,340 suspected counterfeit or copyrighted items/materials were seized by An Garda Síochána. The aforementioned investigations resulted, in particular, in the seizure of 4,000 illicit set top boxes in three (3) particular searches undertaken in the midlands and Dublin. Two of the three sites of those searches were wholesale distributors of these illicit set top boxes.

CAPTURE TIERS: (1) raw/press-releases/2020-09-25_europol_operation-aphrodite-21-countries-counterfeit-iptv-set-top-box.md is USABLE for raw:23-49, the Europol body "extracted from Europol newsroom JSON payload (SPA-rendered)" (raw:27); the same file's raw:53-65 Garda section is agent "verbatim/paraphrased" (raw:57) = RECONSTRUCTION and is NOT cited -- the standalone Garda capture is used instead. (2) raw/press-releases/2020-09-25_garda-ie_operation-aphrodite-iii-iptv-counterfeit.md is USABLE ("(Verbatim extract from the An Garda Síochána Office of Corporate Communications press release dated 25 September 2020.)", raw:12). (3) raw/press-releases/2020-09-25_euipo-europa-eu_success-operation-aphrodite.md is RECONSTRUCTION and is cited in NO cell: its own closing line says "page Cloudflare-protected for unauthenticated fetch; content confirmed via EUIPO+Europol cross-mirror and Garda own-domain release of same date" (that raw:28), and the operation page records the same failure ("the EUIPO success-of-operation-aphrodite URL returned HTTP 403", op page:96). It adds no fact the other two lack (28M / 800k / 123+36 / 27M masks all restated).
MODALITY: arrest-search -- "law enforcement authorities tracked online sales of a large variety of counterfeit items, culminating in checks in warehouses, shops and marketplaces in Belgium, Cyprus, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Portugal, Romania and Spain" (eu raw:29), "Ten people were arrested in Greece" (eu raw:33), and in Ireland "the seizure of 4,000 illicit set top boxes in three (3) particular searches undertaken in the midlands and Dublin" (garda raw:20). content-delisting -- "The operation led to 123 social media accounts and 36 websites selling counterfeit products to be taken down." (eu raw:33). ⚠ DOMAIN-SEIZURE DELIBERATELY NOT CODED: the frontmatter carries results.domains_seized: 36, enforcement_type: domain-seizure and mechanisms_used: [[domain-seizure]] (op page:15, 58, 64), and the page's prose asserts the 36 were "taken down through coordinated platform-engagement requests" (op page:191) -- but NO cited record uses a seizure verb, names a court or judicial order, or describes control passing to authorities for those 36 websites. The record's only verb is "taken down", in the same sentence and with the same verb as the 123 social-media accounts. Under the CODING.md frontmatter-seed rule the code follows the source text, so both counts sit in content-delisting; if the 36 were in fact judicial seizures, the record does not say so. PRIOR CODE asset-seizure (withdrawn 2026-08-18, CODING v4 VALUE-not-THINGS) rested on "More than €700 000 was also seized." (eu raw:33) -- a sweep total with no freeze, account or proceeds language; note the record does not use the word "proceeds" (that is the wiki's gloss at op page:177), but the sum is money seized in an anti-trafficking action rather than an evidentiary exhibit. NOT coded asset-seizure: the ~28 million goods, the 800 000 counterfeit items including IPTV set-top boxes, the 27 million facemasks, the 4,000 Irish set-top boxes and the 6,340 Irish items -- all contraband/evidence. NOT coded: hosting-takedown (no server or hosting action anywhere; frontmatter results.servers_seized: 0 agrees), blocking-order, payment-disruption, intermediary-process, end-user-action, voluntary-transfer.
JUDICIAL: arrests n=10 -- "Ten people were arrested in Greece and 37 others were reported to the judicial authorities in Greece, Italy and Portugal." (eu raw:33). Unlike the IOS XIII row, this release keeps the two stages in separate clauses, so the arrest count is an operation-level figure and no stage-merging problem arises; the 10 are all in Greece and no other jurisdiction is given an arrest count (the page flags this asymmetry at op page:223). indictments = pending, referral-inferred: "37 others were reported to the judicial authorities" is the referral statement CODING.md maps to `pending` for the next stage, reinforced on the Irish side by "Investigation files in Ireland were being prepared for the Director of Public Prosecutions under Section 140 of the Copyright and Related Rights Act 2000 (television broadcast piracy) and Section 92 of the Trade Marks Act 1996 (counterfeit)." (garda raw:26) -- files being prepared, i.e. not yet charged. n=37 was NOT used: being reported to a judicial authority is not a charge, and the Irish referrals are additional to (and uncounted within) the 37. convictions/imprisonments not-reported -- no cited record reaches a court outcome. latest_record_date 2020-09-25 (all three records share the date; the operational phase itself closed 2020-07-31).
RECONSTITUTION: not-reported. No cited record postdates the action or speaks to whether the seller accounts, websites or the set-top-box wholesale chain came back. The page's open questions are disclosure gaps (per-country arrests, per-country box counts, OCG identity, operation versioning) and flag no succession/effectiveness question, so open-question was not used. The Irish 4,200 further websites "selling copyrighted materials across the European Union and beyond being identified" (garda raw:22) are a forward pipeline of NEW targets, not evidence about this action's targets.
CORPUS SEARCH ("Aphrodite" over wiki/sources/): 16 hits, no uncited source about THIS action. Two are other editions of the same series and are worth recording as series context the page does not cite: wiki/sources/2019-06-13_europol_counterfeit-crackdown-aphrodite-ii-30-suspects-ipc3-gdf.md (Aphrodite II, 13 June 2019, 18 countries, 30+ suspects arrested) and wiki/sources/2024-04-30_euipo-europa-eu_operation-aphrodite-vi-empact-3-1-operational-action-plan.md (Aphrodite VI, 2024) (corpus-search). The remaining hits mention Aphrodite only as a series exemplar.
OTHER FIGURES (no column): ~28 million counterfeit and illegal goods; 800 000 counterfeit items "of clothing, sportswear, footwear, personal accessories, IPTV set-top boxes and toys" -- the IPTV hardware is inside an undifferentiated 800 000 line with no IPTV-only count (eu raw:33); 27 million facemasks seized by the Guardia di Finanza as a COVID-19 scope expansion (eu raw:35); Ireland 14 investigations, 6,340 items, 4,000 set-top boxes, two of three searched sites being "wholesale distributors of these illicit set top boxes" (garda raw:18, 20). modality_quotes: Seizure warrants have been executed against three domain names of commercial websites engaged in the illegal reproduction and distribution of copyrighted works in support of a Brazilian-led takedown of digital piracy sites there, dubbed "Operation 404". The coordinated federal law enforcement operation targeted online services that provided illegal copies of copyrighted works, including television shows and movies.

The seized domains are in the custody of the federal government. Visitors to the sites will now find a seizure banner that notifies them that the domain name has been seized by federal authorities and educates them that willful copyright infringement is a federal crime.
During Operation 404, over 250 piracy sites were taken down cooperatively, and Brazilian authorities made five arrests and seized 11 vehicles and one firearm, as well as bulk cash.
