CAPTURE TIER: RECONSTRUCTION for the whole row -- every cell is page_only and every cite carries the marker. The file has two parts. Its "Extracted Text" (raw:67-104, word_count 153) is Wayback banner + Eurojust page chrome with NO article body = CAPTURE-UNUSABLE (L57). The prose the codes rest on (raw:31-48, headed "Press release content (tier-1 own-domain text)") is the project's collection-time transcription from a 2026-05-22 WebFetch (raw:62), not text recoverable from the stored capture. The operation page already says so in its own warning callout: "The Eurojust source for this page was captured through the Wayback Machine and its extracted text is **page chrome, not the release** — site navigation, the capture banner and the footer, `word_count: 153`. Every figure on this page (20,000 households, EUR 1.9 million, three suspects, eleven servers, seven prosecutors' offices) therefore rests on the **project's own collection-time summary** written into the raw file, not on captured publisher wording." (op page:108, flagged by tools/check_quote_provenance.py). The transcription reads as release prose and is internally consistent with the wiki, so it is coded -- but as reconstruction-tier page-level support, never as raw evidence.
MODALITY (verbs as transcribed): arrest-search -- "three suspects were arrested by the Swiss authorities" (raw:37). hosting-takedown -- "11 servers were taken down in France, Germany, Monaco, The Netherlands and Switzerland" (raw:35), restated as cross-border cooperation "to seize servers used to relay the illegal streams" (raw:41). blocking-order -- "the website promoting the illegal service blocked" (raw:37) and "to block the website" (raw:41): the verb is BLOCK, not seize or take down, which is exactly the v2 blocking-order case (access disabled, no transfer of control stated); domain-seizure was therefore NOT coded, and the frontmatter agrees (results.domains_seized: 0). asset-seizure -- "eight bank accounts in Switzerland seized" (raw:37): account seizure, i.e. the organisation's cash position, not evidence. NOT coded end-user-action: the K-boxes already in "over 20,000 households" (raw:39) are the customer layer and no action against subscribers is stated; the record does not even say whether K-box stock was seized (the page raises the same point, op page:172). NOT coded content-delisting, payment-disruption, intermediary-process, voluntary-transfer.
JUDICIAL: arrests n=3 (raw:37). indictments/convictions/imprisonments not-reported -- the release is an action-day announcement and no cited record reaches any charging or court stage; the page confirms the gap twice ("Public-source follow-on prosecutions for the three arrested suspects were not disclosed in the November 2020 release.", op page:155; "Follow-on prosecution outcome of the three Swiss arrestees is not in the public Eurojust record as of 2026-05-22.", op page:197). `pending` was not used: the record states no referral, no charge and no open proceeding. latest_record_date 2020-11-10 = the only cited record, which is also the action day -- the row is censored at day zero.
RECONSTITUTION: not-reported. No cited record postdates the action day, so nothing can speak to durability; an announcement-day status would fail the 14-day window in any case. BORDERLINE NOTED: the page's Lessons section observes that "seizing the digital infrastructure alone does not necessarily prevent re-use of K-boxes already in 20,000 households" (op page:176) -- read as a general lesson about the set-top-box modality rather than a flagged unresolved question about THIS network's succession, so open-question was not used; a coordinator who reads it as an effectiveness question would code open-question, page-only, on op page:176.
CORPUS SEARCH ("K-box"/"K box"/Kbox/Vaud, and Monaco, over wiki/sources/): the only K-box/Vaud hit is the cited source itself; the three other Monaco hits are unrelated (DPRK IT-worker indictment, CoE Monaco cybercrime profile, DAG Lisa Monaco remarks -- a homonym). No uncited in-corpus source about this operation; no linkage gap.
OTHER FIGURES (no column): 11 servers across 5 countries; ~82,000 episodes; >20,000 households; rights-holder damage "over EUR 1.9 million" (raw:35 -- framed as depriving legitimate business, i.e. harm, not the group's revenue); seven public prosecutors' offices and over thirty police officers mobilised in France, Germany, Monaco and The Netherlands, with no foreign agency named (raw:41, 46). modality_quotes: Eurojust continues to support the crackdown on large-scale piracy and fraud with pay-TV and film streaming, by coordinating an action day at the request of the Italian authorities. Over 5.550 computer servers, which were used to transmit and store television broadcasts, live sports games and films without paying the legitimate copyright holders, have been taken down in Italy, Bulgaria, France, Germany, Lithuania, Malta, Romania, Slovenia, Sweden and The Netherlands. The online streaming services have now been blocked for customers in Italy, who watched the television feed through cheap set-top boxes, paying far below market subscription fees.

Dal pomeriggio del 6 novembre, infatti i poliziotti della Polizia postale insieme ai militari della Finanza, hanno gradualmente spento da remoto le piattaforme, i server e le smart card utilizzate dai pirati, nonchè provveduto a oscurare siti web e i canali Telegram dedicati alla vendita e riproduzione dei contenuti dell’IPTV illegale. Sono state oscurate oltre 5.500 risorse informatiche tra server di trasmissione, piattaforme di gestione, siti vetrina e siti di live streaming e oltre 350 canali Telegram.

(raw/press-releases/2020-11-11_eurojust_new-major-crackdown-on-fraud-with-illegal-use-of-pay-tv-signals.md:41). rows.title_original: Operation In Our Sites takes down 21 910 websites selling counterfeit goods
rows.scope_reason: IC census row: pool tag illegal-iptv-ic; medium defaults to iptv-service (re-read as found)
modality_quotes: > As part of the international operation 'In Our Sites' (IOS) XI, law enforcement authorities from 26 EU Member States and third parties have seized together with Europol and the US National Intellectual Property Rights Coordination Centre over 21 910 domain names offering counterfeit and pirated items over the internet. More than €2.5 million worth of such products have been seized, including counterfeit pharmaceuticals and pirated films, illegal television streaming, music, software and other bogus products.
rows.notes: converted from paper2/coding/europol-ios-xi-counterfeit-piracy-21910-domains-takedown-2020.json (coder agent-w1-4, 2026-08-13); date_source=raw-frontmatter; source_of_record=raw/press-releases/2020-11-30_europol_in-our-sites-xi-21910-websites-counterfeit-piracy-takedown.md; tier_basis=raw-dir:press-releases; other_cited_captures=0; quotes are the cited lines as of the coding date; stratum from wiki fields (participating_countries=26, participating_agencies=3); official_release_sourced=True. Capture tier: USABLE — verbatim release body extracted from the Europol React SPA's window.SERVER_DATA JSON (raw:29-54), not a SPA shell. Modality: domain-seizure from the record's own verb — LE authorities "have seized together with Europol and the US National Intellectual Property Rights Coordination Centre over 21 910 domain names offering counterfeit and pirated items over the internet" (raw:29). AGGREGATION PROBLEM (per instruction): the record does not separate streaming/piracy domains from counterfeit-goods domains — the 21,910 figure is a single aggregate covering storefronts for physical counterfeits (pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, perfumes, clothing, detergent, condoms) AND digital piracy ("pirated films, illegal television streaming, music, software", raw:29); no per-crime-type or per-country breakdown exists, so the domain action is coded as stated with no IPTV-specific quantum extractable. Second aggregation/taxonomy gap: "More than €2.5 million worth of such products have been seized" (raw:29) with itemised physical-goods counts (raw:37-42) — counterfeit merchandise seizure has no modality code: it is not asset-seizure (not a proceeds freeze/forfeiture) and no raid/search against persons or premises is stated to hang it on arrest-search; flagged as a taxonomy gap (same family as the fase-7 pilot's deindexation gap, which v2 fixed with content-delisting; a contraband/goods-seizure code is still absent). Judicial: the release states no arrests, charges, convictions, or sentences (only seizure metrics) — all four stages not-reported; operation-page frontmatter arrests: 0 / indictments: 0 are seeds, and its own missing_fields lists arrests and indictments as gaps. Reconstitution: nothing post-action is stated for the seized domains; the release's remark that criminals are "deleting their internet tracks in a very short period of time" (raw:33) is a general threat characterisation, not evidence about these 21,910 domains — not-reported. latest_record_date 2020-11-30 (datePublished 2020-11-30T07:00:01+00:00, raw:17; dateModified 2023-03-21 is a site edit, byline governs). Roster note: the opener "26 EU Member States and third parties" conflicts with the enumerated 26-jurisdiction mixed EU/non-EU participating-countries list (raw:46); the capture's own provenance note documents this (raw:62) and the enumerated list is treated as authoritative by the operation page. Corpus search (In Our Sites / IOS XI / 21 910 / 21,910): other IOS iterations' sources and the EUIPO/IPEC report-series pages match on the series name only — neither report-series page mentions IOS XI or its figure; no uncited in-corpus source about IOS XI — no linkage gap.

The Spanish National Tribunal (Audiencia Nacional) issued a landmark sentencing decision on 22 April 2026 against the operators of one of the largest illegal IPTV networks ever dismantled in Spain. The investigation, which began in 2020 and was dismantled at that point, culminated six years later in criminal convictions against the five-defendant ring. The main perpetrator accepted a 23-month prison sentence (suspended subject to conduct), a EUR 8.7 million personal fine, and the court ordered EUR 12 million in compensation to rightsholders (LaLiga and other plaintiffs).

On **2026-04-22**, Spain's Audiencia Nacional (National Court) concluded the criminal prosecution arc against the **RapidIPTV** pay-TV piracy network with a plea-deal sentence. The ringleader (an Iranian national identified in public coverage as "Dash the Iranian") accepted **23 months in prison**, an **EUR 8.7 million fine**, asset confiscation, and approximately **EUR 12 million in civil compensation** to rights-holders. Four other Iranian-origin defendants were charged. Total financial impact, combining fines, civil damages, and confiscation, exceeded **EUR 43 million**.

modality_quotes: Según informa la Dirección General de la Policía, han sido detenidas once personas : cuatro en la provincias de Barcelona y Alicante, uno en Alemania, tres en Suecia y otros tantos en Dinamarca, y se han practicado quince registros, de los que siete han sido en España y el resto en los países europeos donde se han efectuado arrestos.

Como resultado de las investigaciones se han localizado alrededor de mil páginas web que ofrecían acceso a algo más de 40.000 canales televisión , series y plataformas y se han desconectado los 50 servidores que conformaban la red de que disponía la organización, habiendo dejado por tanto sin servicio a los suscriptores.

Gracias a las actuaciones policiales han sido intervenidos dos vehículos de gama alta valorados en 400.000 euros, una vivienda embargada valorada en 1.700.000 euros, cuatro relojes valorados en 45.000 euros, más de 9.000 euros en efectivo, 2.700.000 euros en criptovalores y 1.100.00 euros bloqueados en diversas cuentas bancarias.

rows.title_original: Desarticulada una red criminal que distribuía contenidos audiovisuales de forma ilegal a más de 500.000 usuarios en varios países europeos
rows.scope_reason: IC census row: pool tag illegal-iptv-ic; medium defaults to iptv-service (re-read as found)

arrests.quote: Agentes de la Policía Nacional, en una operación conjunta con EUROPOL, han desarticulado una red criminal que presuntamente distribuía contenidos audiovisuales de forma ilegal a más de 500.000 usuarios en varios países europeos. Los cuatro arrestados operaban desde Málaga y se valían de varias páginas web para publicitar paquetes de suscripción compuestos por más de 2.600 canales de televisión y 23.000 películas y series; además, contaban con más de 95 revendedores ubicados en España, Reino Unido, Malta, Portugal, Chipre y Grecia. Los beneficios obtenidos, que ascendían a unos tres millones de euros anuales, eran blanqueados por la organización adquiriendo bienes muebles e inmuebles en la provincia de Málaga y desviando fondos a través de sociedades españolas a cuentas bancarias ubicadas en paraísos fiscales. Durante los registros, los agentes desconectaron 10 paneles de administración -conectados a 32 servidores ubicados en Francia, Países Bajos y España- donde se alojaban los contenidos ilegales de televisión, e intervinieron material informático, 2.800 euros en efectivo y dos vehículos de alta gama valorados en 180.000 euros. La investigación se inició en el año 2020 gracias a una denuncia presentada por los responsables de Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment, una coalición de empresas cuya finalidad es combatir la piratería online. Las primeras gestiones policiales permitieron constatar la existencia de una organización que, desde el año 2012, estaría comercializando y distribuyendo de forma masiva y fraudulenta -a través de distintas sociedades- contenidos audiovisuales de diferentes plataformas televisivas de acceso condicionado a pago. Concretamente, ofertaban a sus clientes diferentes paquetes de suscripción compuestos por más de 2.600 canales de televisión y 23.000 películas y series. Contaban con más de 95 revendedores en diferentes países europeos y blanqueaban beneficios de 3.000.000 de euros anuales Los investigados se valían de varias páginas web para publicitar la promoción y venta de suscripciones de listados ordenados de canales de televisión y descodificadores que, a través de unas claves y contraseñas, permitían visionar los canales y contenidos pertenecientes a diferentes plataformas de televisión de pago. Además, la organización contaba con más de 95 revendedores (resellers) ubicados en Reino Unido, Malta, Portugal, Chipre y Grecia. Estos compraban grandes paquetes de suscripciones de forma piramidal a la organización para posteriormente revenderlos en sus países a miles de usuarios. Por otra parte, los beneficios obtenidos -que ascendían a unos 3.000.000 de euros anuales- los blanqueaban, por un lado, moviendo los fondos procedentes de los pagos de las suscripciones desde sociedades españolas hacia distintas cuentas bancarias a nombre de empresas ubicadas en paraísos fiscales gestionadas por los investigados; y por otro, mediante la compraventa de viviendas y vehículos de lujo o constituyendo nuevas sociedades para amparar la actividad delictiva. Se han desconectado 10 paneles de administración conectados a 32 servidores ubicados en Francia, Países Bajos y España Durante los registros, los agentes accedieron a 10 paneles de administración conectados a 32 servidores ubicados en Francia, Países Bajos y España donde se alojaban los contenidos ilegales de televisión a través de los que la organización ofrecía el servicio. Tras proceder a su desconexión se dejó sin servicio tanto a los revendedores como a los usuarios finales. Asimismo, la investigación ha permitido bloquear ocho cuentas bancarias e intervenir numeroso material informático, documentación, 2.800 euros en efectivo y dos vehículos de alta gama valorados en 180.000 euros. La operación ha finalizado con cuatro detenidos en los municipios malagueños de Benahavís (2), Mijas (una persona detenida y otra investigada) y Benalmádena (1), si bien continúan las gestiones para identificar a más posibles implicados relacionados con la organización en otros países. NOTA: Los medios de comunicación que lo deseen podrán obtener imágenes en el siguiente enlace: http://prensa.policia.es/fagus.rar

The whole release body sits on ONE line (raw:17), which is why every cite in this row points there — the line, not my reading, is the granularity the capture offers. raw/news/2022-11-21_theshiftnews_...md is RECONSTRUCTION tier: an agent-authored structured digest of the article under editorial headings ("## Operation Summary", "## Infrastructure Seized", "## Cross-corroboration"), fetch_method WebFetch, no verbatim article text. NOTHING IS CITED FROM IT, which also keeps a known error out of the coding: it lists "Bank accounts frozen totalling €3 million" (theshift raw:41) where the official release gives EUR 3,000,000 as the ring's ANNUAL LAUNDERED PROFIT and reports eight accounts blocked with no total — the wiki caught and documented that compression (op:67, op:145, op:177). MODALITY, from the Spanish verbs. arrest-search: "La operación ha finalizado con cuatro detenidos en los municipios malagueños de Benahavís (2), Mijas (una persona detenida y otra investigada) y Benalmádena (1), si bien continúan las gestiones para identificar a más posibles implicados relacionados con la organización en otros países." plus the searches themselves, "Durante los registros, los agentes accedieron a 10 paneles de administración..." (both raw:17). hosting-takedown: "Durante los registros, los agentes accedieron a 10 paneles de administración conectados a 32 servidores ubicados en Francia, Países Bajos y España donde se alojaban los contenidos ilegales de televisión a través de los que la organización ofrecía el servicio. Tras proceder a su desconexión se dejó sin servicio tanto a los revendedores como a los usuarios finales." (raw:17) — coded on the definition's "shut down" limb, NOT on "seized": the wiki is right that no server was seized (op:65, results.servers_seized 0), the police reached the panels and disconnected them, and the service stopped. asset-seizure: "Asimismo, la investigación ha permitido bloquear ocho cuentas bancarias e intervenir numeroso material informático, documentación, 2.800 euros en efectivo y dos vehículos de alta gama valorados en 180.000 euros." (raw:17) — eight bank accounts BLOCKED is an unambiguous freeze, and the cash and vehicles ride with it; the computer material and documentation are evidence and do not carry this code on their own. NOT coded domain-seizure: the release says the ring used web pages to advertise subscriptions but reports no seizure or blocking of any site or domain (results.domains_seized 0, op:59). NOT coded end-user-action: "se dejó sin servicio ... a los usuarios finales" is the consequence of the disconnection, not an action aimed at subscribers. NOT coded blocking-order or payment-disruption: neither appears in the record. CORPUS DEFECT (wiki side, for the coordinator): the operation page asserts "Real estate (movable and immovable property) seized in Malaga province" (op:69, repeated at op:147) and attributes real-estate seizure to the action. The official release says the opposite thing about that property — it is how the money was LAUNDERED, not what was seized: "Los beneficios obtenidos, que ascendían a unos tres millones de euros anuales, eran blanqueados por la organización adquiriendo bienes muebles e inmuebles en la provincia de Málaga y desviando fondos a través de sociedades españolas a cuentas bancarias ubicadas en paraísos fiscales." (raw:17). The seized-items list in the same release is exhaustive and contains no property: computer material, documentation, EUR 2,800 in cash, two vehicles, plus eight bank accounts blocked. The claim traces to the reconstruction-tier capture, which files "Real estate (movable and immovable property in Malaga province) seized" under its "Infrastructure Seized" heading (theshift raw:43). My asset-seizure code does not rest on it. JUDICIAL. arrests n=4 (raw:17). Note alongside it, not in the count: a fifth person in Mijas is "investigada" (under investigation) but not detained, and the release says work continues to identify more implicated persons in other countries. indictments/convictions/imprisonments not-reported: the release names no charge, no statute (the wiki emptied legal_basis for exactly this reason, op:77), no court and no defendant. I did NOT code indictments as pending: the continuing "gestiones" are aimed at IDENTIFYING further suspects, which is investigative expansion rather than a statement that charging proceedings are underway against the four — the distinction the protocol's pending rule turns on. latest_record_date 2022-11-16, the only cited record; the later Shift News piece (2022-11-21) is uncited for tier reasons. RECONSTITUTION not-reported, and this one is BORDERLINE — flagged so the coordinator can flip it if they read the rule differently. The official release is published 28 days after the 19 October 2022 action day, which clears the protocol's 14-day window, and it states the disconnection left resellers and end users without service. But that sentence is past-tense about the moment of disconnection ("Tras proceder a su desconexión se dejó sin servicio..."), not a status check as at publication, and no record says the service stayed down or names a successor. I coded silence rather than durability. CORPUS SEARCH (Benahavís | Benalmádena | Mijas | "500.000 usuarios" | "95 revendedores", then Malaga/Málaga over wiki/sources/) returned the two cited pages plus twelve unrelated files — Operation Casper 2017, the 2021 Policía Nacional pay-TV action with 3,000 users, Black Axe, the Estepona Twitter-hack case and the sources index. No third record about this action day exists in the corpus, and no Europol own-domain release for it has ever been located (op:86, op:190). No linkage gap found.

modality_quotes: > Law enforcement agencies from 27 countries* participated in the 13th edition of Operation In Our Sites, a Europol-coordinated operation to take down websites offering counterfeit goods or involved in online piracy. The recurring operation, which is supported by Eurojust and INTERPOL, targets, investigates and seizes websites hosting a variety of illicit content. The main issues continue to be intellectual property infringement on trademarks, as well as on copyrighted content available on internet protocol television (IPTV) and movie streaming services, peer-to-peer sharing platforms and hosting websites. Key findings of the operation that took place from 1 May to 14 November also show that more counterfeit products are being assembled within the European Union's borders and that intellectual property crime is closely intertwined with serious and organised crime.

converted from paper2/coding/europol-ios-xiii-counterfeit-piracy-12526-domains-takedown-2022.json (coder agent-w2-4, 2026-08-13); date_source=raw-frontmatter; source_of_record=raw/press-releases/2022-11-28_europol_in-our-sites-xiii-12526-websites-counterfeit-piracy-takedown.md; tier_basis=raw-dir:press-releases; other_cited_captures=0; quotes are the cited lines as of the coding date; stratum from wiki fields (participating_countries=27, participating_agencies=5); official_release_sourced=True. CAPTURE TIER: USABLE -- verbatim body recovered from the Europol React SPA payload (`window.SERVER_DATA.NodeLoader.node`) via a TLS-impersonating fetch, HTTP 200, 43,754 bytes, no challenge (raw:28, 103-105); the file carries the introduction, the four body sections and the Kosovo footnote as blockquoted verbatim text (raw:32-64). The tables at raw:70-89 are agent-extracted restatements of those same sentences -- not cited; every code below cites the verbatim body instead.
MODALITY -- AGGREGATION PROBLEM (flagged as instructed): the 12 526 figure is a single undifferentiated count. The release describes the targets as "intellectual property infringement on trademarks, as well as on copyrighted content available on internet protocol television (IPTV) and movie streaming services, peer-to-peer sharing platforms and hosting websites" (raw:36) but NEVER splits the 12 526 into counterfeit-storefront domains vs streaming/piracy domains, and gives no per-country split either. The IPTV leg is separately evidenced only by the 32 servers / 2 294 channels line. Any streaming-only domain count for this row would be a fabrication; the row's domain modality therefore covers a mixed population.
domain-seizure: coded from the intro's verb -- the operation "targets, investigates and seizes websites hosting a variety of illicit content" (raw:36) -- plus the result "law enforcement agencies across several continents have taken down 12 526 websites" (raw:44) and the state/court process marker "10 search warrants were issued" (raw:48). VERB CAVEAT: the results sentence says "taken down", not "seized"; "seizes" appears only in the intro's description of what the recurring operation does. No blocking verb (no injunction, no DNS/ISP block, no Piracy Shield-type measure) and no delisting verb appears anywhere for those 12 526, so blocking-order and content-delisting were NOT coded for them.
hosting-takedown: "disconnected 32 servers used to distribute and host illegal content for 2 294 television channels" (raw:44), restated as "Spanish police disconnected 32 servers hosting the illicit content" (raw:48) -- the operation-wide 32 and the Spain 32 are the same servers.
content-delisting: "shut down 15 online shops selling counterfeit products on social media sites" (raw:44) -- social-profile/storefront removal on a platform, which is the content-delisting definition; these 15 are counterfeit-goods shops, not streaming.
arrest-search: "10 search warrants were issued and 14 people were detained or formally accused", "Spanish Police arrested four people" (raw:48), and in Bulgaria "a number of house searches were conducted and a workshop with sewing and embossing machines was discovered" (raw:50).
PRIOR CODE asset-seizure (withdrawn 2026-08-18, CODING v4): "Spanish police disconnected 32 servers hosting the illicit content and seized cash, documents and two luxury vehicles" (raw:48) is a search inventory; the first coder read the two luxury vehicles as proceeds-converted assets in the record's lavish-lifestyle framing ("earning up to EUR 150 000 a month and living a lavish lifestyle in a luxury house, driving expensive cars", raw:48), and Europol frames the action as "conducting financial investigations and asset recovery concurrently" (raw:52). The cash and documents are ambiguous between proceeds and evidence and are not what carries this code. NOT coded asset-seizure: the 127 365 counterfeit products (raw:44), the 600 counterfeit articles and the firearm (raw:50) -- contraband/evidence.

modality_quotes: On February 14, 2023, the Public Security Bureau of China’s Jiangsu Province detained and interrogated an unemployed male resident of Chongqing, A (age 33), on suspicion of operating “B9GOOD,” the largest anime pirate site for Japanese people, and distributing anime and other works without permission from the rights holders. In addition, from February 18 to March 21, a search was conducted on a company employee female B (age 30) from Chengdu, an unemployed male C (age 38) from Shanghai, and a self-employed female D (age 34) from Fuzhou, Fujian, were searched and interrogated at their homes for distributing animation, movies, dramas, and other works without the right holders’ permission through this website. After the criminal exposé of the main parties involved and an analytical investigation of the servers used, the site was completely shut down on March 27.

Male A also stated that he was acquainted with female B and D, and that he paid them to upload the files. female B was paid 30,000 yuan (approximately 600,000 yen) and female D was paid 80,000 yuan (1.6 million yen).

法廷において男性Aは起訴内容を全面的に認め、反省・謝罪の意を述べました。男性Aは、2008年から2023年2月までの間、中国国内、カナダ、日本等のサーバーをレンタルし、「BLUE920」、「B9DM」、「B9GOOD」とサイト名・ドメインを変更しながら、営利を目的に約15年間にわたり同サイトの運営を続けていました。アップロードは男性A自ら、あるいは女性BやDに報酬を支払う形で行われ、計45,880本ものアニメ等を権利者に無断で掲載していたことが分かりました。判決では、男性Aが不当に得た広告収益として177万7,000元(約3,700万円)が認められたほか、摘発時に公安に差し押さえられた住居（400万元相当：摘発時は約8,000万円）についても、サイト運営による違法収入で購入したものとして押収されています。

indictments.quote: In November 2022, TOEI ANIMATION CO., LTD., TOHO CO., LTD., and Bandai Namco Filmworks Inc. filed criminal referral through CODA against four pirate sites in Brazil that infringe on Japanese animation. The investigation revealed that two of the sites were opened by the same operator. In response to this, since February 8, 2023, raids and other investigations have been conducted in each of the three cases, and a total of 13 sites have been closed down, including these four sites as well as nine related sites operated by the suspects. Furthermore, based on the information revealed by our subsequent investigation, we conducted knock-and-talks (direct negotiations) with the operators of another 9 sites, and as a result, these 9 sites and their 9 affiliated sites, totaling 18 sites, were also shut down. A total of 31 sites were closed as a result of CODA’s involvement.

quotes: In response to the closure of these sites, another 5 piracy sites in Brazil were voluntarily shut down, resulting in the closure of 36 Japanese anime piracy sites in Brazil so far as a result of the series of operations. The average monthly traffic for these 36 sites in the last three months (December 2022-February 2023) reached approximately 83 million, resulting in the closure of 12 of the top 20 animation infringement sites in Brazil as of the time before this measure was implemented (February-April 2022).

Furthermore, 22 of these 36 domains have already been surrendered through negotiations, and access to these sites now automatically redirects visitors to a page opened by CODA notifying them of the closure. Negotiations will continue for the remaining sites to surrender their domains.

Scene of the search①

In November 2022, TOEI ANIMATION CO., LTD., TOHO CO., LTD., and Bandai Namco Filmworks Inc. filed criminal referral through CODA against four pirate sites in Brazil that infringe on Japanese animation. The investigation revealed that two of the sites were opened by the same operator. In response to this, since February 8, 2023, raids and other investigations have been conducted in each of the three cases, and a total of 13 sites have been closed down, including these four sites as well as nine related sites operated by the suspects. Furthermore, based on the information revealed by our subsequent investigation, we conducted knock-and-talks (direct negotiations) with the operators of another 9 sites, and as a result, these 9 sites and their 9 affiliated sites, totaling 18 sites, were also shut down. A total of 31 sites were closed as a result of CODA’s involvement.

Furthermore, 22 of these 36 domains have already been surrendered through negotiations, and access to these sites now automatically redirects visitors to a page opened by CODA notifying them of the closure. Negotiations will continue for the remaining sites to surrender their domains.

This is silence, not an affirmative absence - the parent frontmatter's results.arrests: 0 and its prose 'No arrests reported in either phase' are a schema seed and a statement about reporting, neither of which is evidence for none-stated (CODING.md). indictments pending, referral-inferred: rights holders filed a criminal referral through CODA in November 2022 and three criminal cases were worked with raids (raw:61); CODA's footnote 3 defines the instrument as 'A request to the local police to investigate a suspect because of a suspected crime' (raw:83). ⚠ Re-mapping note for a reader: this is a rights-holder criminal complaint to POLICE (JP 刑事告発), not a referral to prosecution and not a prosecutor-led investigation; it is coded pending on the same footing the manual gives HR kaznena prijava and IT denunciati (pre-charge referral opening a proceeding against identified suspects), and it is more than the bare search-warrant execution the manual excludes, because a formal complaint was filed and three cases exist. No charging decision, prosecutor, or court is named anywhere in the record. convictions / imprisonments not-reported: silence.

RIGHT-CENSORING. latest_record_date 2023-04-20 = this row's only cited record. A later record from the same publisher revisits this component 16 months on - 'Phase 1 of the operation was conducted from February to March 2023, resulting in the shutdown of 36 Japanese anime piracy sites.' (2024 capture, raw:59) - reporting no judicial development and no recurrence, but it is a past-tense restatement rather than a status affirmation (same treatment the corpus's b9good row gives a later past-tense reference), so it is not cited in a cell and does not move the censoring date.

RECONSTITUTION borderline, flagged: the coded evidence is the announcing release's own status statement, and it qualifies only because the announcement lags the action - byline 2023-04-20 against an action ending in March 2023 is at least 20 days, outside CODING.md's 14-day exclusion, and 71 days after the 8 February raids. If a coordinator instead treats the source page's publish_date 2023-03-31 as authoritative, the gap to the March closures can fall inside 14 days and this cell becomes not-reported. Also noted: 14 of the 36 domains were not surrendered ('Negotiations will continue for the remaining sites to surrender their domains.', raw:65) - those sites are stated closed but their domains stayed with the operators; the record does not frame this as an effectiveness question, so it is not open-question. The record's only effectiveness evidence points the other way (legitimate-service search popularity peaking during the closure window, raw:67).

PARTICIPATING COUNTRIES ESTABLISHED BY THIS COMPONENT'S RECORDS: 2 - Brazil (executing: MJSP / Operation 404 raids from 2023-02-08, raw:61, raw:57) and Japan (CODA plus its member rights holders TOEI ANIMATION, TOHO, Bandai Namco Filmworks; the activity 'was part of a project entrusted from the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry', raw:73). South Korea is NOT a phase-1 participant: the strings Korea, COA and webtoon do not occur anywhere in the phase-1 capture (verified by grep, exit 1), and the wiki source page says so explicitly. The parent page's frontmatter participating_countries lists Brazil + Japan + South Korea for the whole page, which over-scopes Korea onto this component.

PAGE DEFECT CONFIRMED (top-20 figures conflated; reported, wiki not edited): the two phases report DIFFERENT top-20 figures against DIFFERENT baselines, and each belongs to its own phase. Phase 1: 'resulting in the closure of 12 of the top 20 animation infringement sites in Brazil as of the time before this measure was implemented (February-April 2022)' (this capture, raw:63). Phase 2: 'As a result of the operation, seven of the top 20 anime infringement sites in Brazil during that period were closed.' (2024 capture, raw:65), where 'that period' is that release's SimilarWeb window '*4: January 2023 – March 2023 by SimilarWeb data.' (2024 capture, raw:93). The operation page carries only the phase-2 figure and re-scopes it to the whole campaign in three places - frontmatter target_entity 'seven of Brazil's top 20 anime-infringement sites were closed across the campaign' (wiki/operations/coda-cbep-brazil-operation-animes-anime-piracy-takedown-2023-2024.md:28), Background (same file:109) and Results and Impact (same file:134) - dropping phase 1's 12 entirely. The 'across the campaign' mis-scope also sits in the phase-2 source page summary (wiki/sources/2024_coda_operation-animes-2-brazil-korea-coa-16-sites-takedown.md:37), while the phase-1 source page summary omits the 12 figure. The two figures are not additive and not comparable (different baseline periods, and phase 2's ranking is of anime sites during Jan-Mar 2023 while phase 1's is of animation sites during Feb-Apr 2022).

CORPUS SEARCH ('Operation Animes', 'Operação Animes', 'Operation Anime 2', goyabu, animeyabu, animeshouse, animesbr, meuanime, and the three coda-cj.jp/en/news URLs): no uncited in-corpus source page about this operation exists - the only wiki/sources/ hits are the two already cited. No linkage gap. The MJSP's own gov.br releases for both phases (URLs at raw:79 and 2024 capture, raw:91) are NOT in the corpus; they are the government-side primary records this row lacks.

CAPTURE TIERS: the GdF/MET capture is USABLE for raw:12-48 -- the verbatim Italian release body as republished by the Citta Metropolitana di Firenze MET institutional portal, recovered over plain HTTP after an HTTPS cert-altname failure (raw:7, 57); raw:52-75 ("Tier-1 verification notes", "Key extracted facts") is agent-authored and not cited. NOTE the capture has lost Italian diacritics throughout ("e stato eseguito", "attivita illecita", "Autorita giudiziaria", "responsabilita"); quotes below are exact to the CAPTURE, which is what the cite resolves to. The EUIPO+Europol 2024 capture is RECONSTRUCTION-tier (a 23-line agent digest of a strategic report) and carries NO Impero-specific fact -- its only relevant lines are ecosystem generalities (that raw:19-23) -- so it is cited in no cell and does not move latest_record_date.
MODALITY (from the Italian verbs, not the frontmatter): arrest-search -- "hanno dato esecuzione a un decreto di perquisizione personale, informatica e locale emesso dalla" Procura di Milano "nei confronti di 13 persone" (raw:22), and in Germany "le operazioni sono state condotte nei confronti di 2 soggetti italiani" under the EIO (raw:24). Searches against persons, no arrest verb anywhere. domain-seizure -- the same seizure decree covered "e di un sito web utilizzati per l'attivita illecita" (raw:26): a court-ordered sequestro of the website, i.e. transfer of control under state process. content-delisting -- "60 risorse della piattaforma di messaggistica Telegram" seized (raw:26): Telegram channels are platform-hosted resources, not domains or hosting, and their removal is the social-profile/repository removal that v2's content-delisting covers; the principal channel was "Impero IPTV" (raw:28). BORDERLINE FLAGGED: one could argue the 60 Telegram resources belong under domain-seizure because the instrument is a sequestro; they are coded as delisting because the code set distinguishes by WHAT was acted on, and a Telegram channel is not a domain. asset-seizure -- "proventi illeciti per oltre 620.000 euro" seized, "ricostruiti grazie alle indagini finanziarie svolte sui conti aperti dagli indagati su piattaforme di servizi di pagamento digitale e di trasferimento di denaro tramite internet e su account detenuti presso exchange gestori di criptovalute" (raw:26) -- explicitly includes cryptocurrency-exchange accounts. NOT coded: hosting-takedown (no server or hosting action stated; frontmatter results.servers_seized: 0 agrees); payment-disruption (funds in the suspects' own accounts were seized -- no processor or advertising cutoff is stated); intermediary-process (financial-account reconstruction is implied but no disclosure order to a CDN/registrar/host is stated, which is what v2 scopes this code to); end-user-action (the page's Follow-Up explicitly records that end-customer follow-on is NOT disclosed, op page:283).
JUDICIAL: arrests not-reported -- the record describes only searches and seizures; nobody is said to have been arrested (frontmatter results.arrests: 0). indictments = pending, NOT n=13. The 13 are "denunciate"/"indiziate": "nei confronti di 13 persone, — dodici di nazionalita italiana e una di origini albanesi, residenti in diverse regioni della penisola e in Germania — indiziate di essere, in concorso tra loro, gli amministratori di canali social che vendevano abusivamente abbonamenti ai palinsesti TV protetti dal diritto d'autore, diffondendo i flussi IPTV "pirata" attraverso reti telematiche." (raw:22), and the release closes: "Si evidenzia che il procedimento penale verte ancora nella fase delle indagini preliminari e che la responsabilita degli indagati sara definitivamente accertata solo ove intervenga sentenza irrevocabile di condanna." (raw:46). Italian denuncia at the indagini-preliminari stage makes the 13 indagati (persons under investigation), not imputati -- no rinvio a giudizio is stated, so a formal charge count is not in the record; `pending` is the value the protocol provides for "proceedings are underway". This matches the treatment of the sibling GdF operation already coded in this batch (italy-france-germany-tutto-chiaro-cinemagoal-iptv-takedown-2026.json, indictments = pending against "indagati"). The count IS in the record and is preserved here: 13 denunciati (12 Italian nationals + 1 of Albanian origin), of whom 2 (Italian nationals, the Master tier) were targeted in Frankfurt am Main. The wiki frontmatter's results.indictments: 13 (op page:89) is the seed reading of "denunciati" as charges; the coded value deliberately differs and the reason is here. convictions/imprisonments not-reported -- no court outcome exists at the record date and the page's Follow-Up asks for the trial outcome to be tracked (op page:282). latest_record_date 2023-06-22 (release byline; the release also carries a publish_time of 11:47, raw:5).
RECONSTITUTION: not-reported. No cited record speaks to what happened after 22 June 2023. The page's Contradictions & Open Questions list disclosure gaps (platforms not named, customer count, regions, crypto/fiat split, Eurojust dossier, ingest method, end-customer follow-on) but flags NO succession or reconstitution question, so open-question was not used; the seizure of only 60 of a Telegram ecosystem's channels invites the question but the corpus does not pose it.
CORPUS SEARCH (Impero, pezzotto, "620.000"/"620,000" over wiki/sources/): 8 hits, none an uncited source ABOUT this operation. Five mention Impero only as a cross-reference exemplar in other documents (2014-10-21_cjeu_bestwater, 2019-11-28_euipo_bournemouth-phase-3, 2024-09-01_eurojust_flyer-illegal-iptv-services-eu, 2024-10-23_euipo-europol_uncovering-ecosystem (cited anyway), the two 2026 Tutto Chiaro captures). Not cited: it is a reconstruction-tier digest whose Impero sentence is not the publisher's, and it adds nothing the GdF release does not already state. No linkage gap.
WIKI-SIDE OBSERVATIONS: References row [1] records no URL (op page:310) although the capture carries source_url http://met.provincia.fi.it/news.aspx?n=368846 (raw:2). The page's Background attributes example payment providers ("PayPal, Skrill, Revolut", "Wise, Western Union digital, MoneyGram digital", op page:163, 240-241) that the record does NOT name -- the release names only the three account CLASSES; the page does label them as illustrative, but they are absent from the source and were not coded from.

rows.scope_reason: IC census row: pool tag illegal-iptv-ic; medium defaults to iptv-service (re-read as found)

arrests.quote: > Ein kriminelles Unternehmen mit bis zu 80 Taetern vertrieb illegale Zugaenge zu Internet Protocol Television (IPTV) im grossen Stil. Bankguthaben von rund 1,6 Millionen Euro wurden beschlagnahmt und 20 Taeter in Oesterreich festgenommen.
quotes: > Ein kriminelles Unternehmen mit bis zu 80 Taetern vertrieb illegale Zugaenge zu Internet Protocol Television (IPTV) im grossen Stil. Bankguthaben von rund 1,6 Millionen Euro wurden beschlagnahmt und 20 Taeter in Oesterreich festgenommen.

> Nach Ausforschung der Taeter wurden ueber Anordnung der Staatsanwaltschaft mehrere Hausdurchsuchungen durchgefuehrt, wobei eine grosse Anzahl an elektronischen Datentraegern sowie **60 Bankkonten und ein Bankschliessfach** sichergestellt wurden. **Bankguthaben in Hoehe von 1,6 Millionen Euro**, Bargeld sowie ein Audi A7 wurden beschlagnahmt. Die Taeter hatten fuer die Entschluesselung und Verteilung der IPTV-Zugaenge **35 Server angemietet**, um das illegale Streaming professionell zu ermoeglichen. Von den Ermittlern wurden insgesamt **55 elektronische Datentraeger** wie PCs, Festplatten, Smartphones sichergestellt und ausgewertet. Aufgrund der akribischen Ermittlungen konnten **20 Verdaechtige in Wien, Niederoesterreich, Salzburg, Vorarlberg und Tirol** festgenommen werden. Darueber hinaus konnten **Mittaeter in Deutschland und in weiteren europaeischen Laendern ausgeforscht und festgenommen** werden. Die Haupttaetern verfuegten luxurioese Immobilien, Sportwaegen und waren auch im Besitz von mehreren Unternehmen, Vereinen und stillen Gesellschaften. Das illegal erwirtschaftete Geld wurde zum Teil fuer legale Investitionen genutzt und so in den Wirtschaftskreislauf eingefuehrt. Neben den straf- und urheberrechtlichen Delikten werden auch Ermittlungen zu steuer-finanzrechtlichen Delikten gefuehrt.

indictments.quote: > Ein grosses Pay-TV-Unternehmen erstattete 2022 in Deutschland Anzeige wegen Urheberrechtsverletzungen, da Zugaenge zu den Inhalten des Anbieters von einem Onlinevertreiber illegal angeboten wurden. Die Spur fuehrte nach Oesterreich, wo sich einer der Verantwortlichen vermutlich aufhielt. Aus diesem Grund kam es zu einem **Rechtshilfeersuchen der deutschen Justiz an die oesterreichische**. Daraufhin leitete die **Staatsanwaltschaft Wiener Neustadt** ein Ermittlungsverfahren ein, und uebermittelte die deutschen Ermittlungsergebnisse an das **Bundeskriminalamt (BK)**. Die Ermittlerinnen und Ermittler des BK konnten ein grosses Taeternetzwerk ausforschen und in Zusammenarbeit mit den **Landeskriminalaemtern** die in Oesterreich lebenden Taeter dingfest machen. Die Haupttaeter hatten zwischen 2016 und 2023 urheberrechtlich geschuetzte und verschluesselte TV-Signale zu einer der bekanntesten Plattform entschluesselt und ueber illegale Vertreiber und Haendler an tausende Endkunden fuer eine Jahresgebuehr von rund 100 Euro verkauft. Die sogenannten Reseller haben die illegalen TV-Zugaengen vom Lieferanten zu guenstigen Konditionen von rund 20 bis 40 Euro pro Zugang und Jahr erworben und um Drei- bis Vierfache an die Endkunden weiterverkauft.

arrests.quote: Coordination with the Indonesian Directorate General of Intellectual Property (DGIP), the Korean Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism (MCST), and the Korean National Police Agency (KNPA), led to the arrest of three suspects behind the illegal Internet Protocol television (IPTV) service.
quotes: Coordination with the Indonesian Directorate General of Intellectual Property (DGIP), the Korean Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism (MCST), and the Korean National Police Agency (KNPA), led to the arrest of three suspects behind the illegal Internet Protocol television (IPTV) service.
문화체육관광부(장관 유인촌, 이하 문체부)와 부산경찰청, 그리고 인터폴 및 인도네시아 지식재산청과의 국제 공조수사를 통해, 인도네시아에서 한국 교민을 대상으로 불법 IPTV(인터넷 프로토콜 텔레비전) 서비스 'TVOOO'를 운영한 피의자 3명을 검거하고 서비스를 중단시켰다고 밝혔다.
**Penangkapan:** Dua dari tiga pelaku layanan IPTV ilegal lintas negara ditangkap di Korea Selatan.

modality_quotes: The illegal service was first flagged by the copyright holder to Indonesian officials in May 2023. Cooperation through the INTERPOL National Central Bureaus in Jakarta and Seoul, the Indonesian DGIP, and the Korean MCST, led to simultaneous raids being held in both countries in late October, leading to the arrests.
**2023년 10월 말** 진행한 압수수색에는 다음 기관이 합동 참여했다:

Di penghujung bulan Oktober 2023, dilakukan penindakan atau olah TKP yang dilakukan secara serempak di Indonesia dan Korea. Pada penindakan di Indonesia, dari kediaman terlapor ditemukan sejumlah peralatan operasi IPTV yang dapat digunakan untuk menonton siaran dan film Korea secara real time maupun Video on Demand (VOD).
rows.notes: converted from paper2/coding/interpol-i-sop-korea-indonesia-iptv-piracy-takedown-2023.json (coder agent-w1-3, 2026-08-13); date_source=raw-frontmatter; source_of_record=raw/press-releases/2023-12-21_interpol_indonesia-korea-iptv-piracy-takedown-i-sop.md; tier_basis=raw-dir:press-releases; other_cited_captures=2; quotes are the cited lines as of the coding date; stratum from wiki fields (participating_countries=2, participating_agencies=4); official_release_sourced=True. CAPTURE TIERS — every capture for this operation is page-level, so all coded cells are page_only. (i) INTERPOL 2023-12-21 capture: reconstruction — its I-SOP context paragraph contains an event postdating the release date ('with a phase-two extension begun in 2025 funded at KRW 4.2 billion / EUR 2.8 million', raw:27) plus an agent-authored 'Key facts (verbatim from INTERPOL release)' block; the body paragraphs (raw:15-25) read verbatim but the capture fails the verbatim-extraction test as a whole. (ii) MCST 2023-12-04 capture: reconstruction — its closing section describes the INTERPOL release published 17 days AFTER its own date (raw:46). (iii)+(iv) both DJKI captures (2024-01-17, 2023-11-07): WebFetch digests with agent scaffolding ('Lembaga yang disebut verbatim:'). (v) INTERPOL 2025-01-15 phase-II capture: reconstruction digest ('The release cites Phase I achievements including...', raw:25) — not cited in cells (retrospective 'Arrest of operators behind major illegal platforms' adds nothing specific). (vi) MCST 2024-09-10 capture: CAPTURE-UNUSABLE below its agent-digest header — an mcst.go.kr navigation shell (menus/footer/login widgets, raw:45-983) whose release body exists only as unretrieved hwpx/pdf attachments (raw:435-445; L57 class) — never cited. MODALITY: arrest-search from 'led to simultaneous raids being held in both countries in late October, leading to the arrests.' (interpol:21), the 2023-10-말 압수수색 joint-participation list (mcst:28), and Indonesia-side 'dilakukan penindakan atau olah TKP yang dilakukan secara serempak di Indonesia dan Korea' with IPTV operating equipment found at the raided residence (dgip-jan:17). Did NOT code hosting-takedown for the service shutdown: '피의자 3명을 검거하고 서비스를 중단시켰다' (mcst:15) and the INTERPOL headline 'shuts down illegal IPTV service' state a service stop with no server/domain/hosting verb (the 40 set-top boxes in Goyang were 'ditemukan'/found, dgip-jan:24, not stated seized) — this is the unspecified-platform-takedown taxonomy gap the pilot flagged on Noonoo. NOTE: this is the OPPOSITE borderline call from the pilot's Noonoo hosting-takedown:page-only, because the Noonoo record said 'seized' while no TVOOO record uses a seizure/server verb — flagged for coordinator consistency review. JUDICIAL: arrests n=3 ('led to the arrest of three suspects behind the illegal Internet Protocol television (IPTV) service.', interpol:17; '피의자 3명을 검거', mcst:15) with jurisdiction breakdown 'Dua dari tiga pelaku layanan IPTV ilegal lintas negara ditangkap di Korea Selatan.' (dgip-jan:26 — 2 in Korea, 1 by implication in Indonesia). No record reports charging, prosecution, trial, or sentencing (MBC's May/July 2023 고소 are rights-holder criminal complaints, not indictments of the suspects) — indictments/convictions/imprisonments not-reported; right-censoring at 2024-01-17. COUNT/NAME CONFLICTS (no coded cell affected): VOD files 'nearly 110,000' (INTERPOL, interpol:15) vs '약 108,000여 개' (mcst:19) vs '108.000' (dgip-jan:20) — the two national agencies give the more specific 108,000; brand 'TVOOO' (MCST, redacted orthography) vs 'TVDOL' (DJKI Nov capture:15) — same service per the wiki's disambiguation. The DJKI Jan capture also lists 'Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO)' among named institutions (dgip-jan:37), which no other record carries. RECONSTITUTION: no cited record speaks to service status after the late-October-2023 raids; shutdown statements are announcement-time — not-reported, empty cites. CORPUS SEARCH ('TVOOO', 'TVDOL'): four additional corpus pages mention the brand (2024-08-19 MCST bulk-sweep; 2025-01-15 MCST I-SOP phase-II MOU + photo-news; 2025-12-01 DJKI Seoul global meeting) — all retrospective programmatic references to the takedown as a Phase-I deliverable, none a record of this operation's own facts, none adds judicial or reconstitution data; no linkage gap.

Dedup: grep for TVo hits the Korea-Indonesia 'TVOOO' IPTV case (interpol-i-sop-korea-indonesia-iptv-piracy-takedown-2023, Dec 2023) -- a DIFFERENT case (Indonesian IPTV operators via INTERPOL; this row is a Korean-run streaming site with US HSI, Feb 2024, KRW ~400m proceeds); verdict new. Judicial: 2 suspects '검거하고 송치' = apprehended and referred to the prosecution -> arrests n=2 (검거 can be non-custodial booking in Korean police usage; custody status not stated) and indictments pending (referral-inferred: 송치 = case sent to prosecutors, charge not yet filed). Modality: residence search-and-seizure (압수수색) + apprehension -> arrest-search; the TVo site was closed voluntarily by the operators in Aug 2022 BEFORE the arrests ('자진 폐쇄') -- pre-action self-closure, not an enforcement takedown, so no infrastructure code and no voluntary-transfer (no settlement). Also flags a P2P-assisted streaming technique at other sites (general). Reconstitution not addressed.

rows.title_original: Operators of unlicensed subscription-like websites criminally exposed in China for the first time. A total of 13 people, including the operators of the two cases, were arrested one after the other. - Content Overseas Distribution Association（CODA）
rows.scope_reason: IC census row: pool tag illegal-iptv-ic; medium defaults to iptv-service (re-read as found)

arrests.quote: The Public Security Bureau of China’s Jiangsu Province conducted a roundup from January to June 2024, arresting 13 people, including the operator, on suspicion of violating copyright laws for two incidents of creating unlicensed subscription-like websites in the form of abusing legal streaming services and selling account information to view the videos in the library,
quotes: The Public Security Bureau of China’s Jiangsu Province conducted a roundup from January to June 2024, arresting 13 people, including the operator, on suspicion of violating copyright laws for two incidents of creating unlicensed subscription-like websites in the form of abusing legal streaming services and selling account information to view the videos in the library,

In the first case, on January 8, 2024, the Public Security Bureau of Taizhou City, Jiangsu Province, China, dispatched 54 agents and other personnel to Chongqing, Jiangsu, Shandong, Shanghai, Hebei, and Anhui Provinces to conduct simultaneous raids against several suspects in various locations. The raid revealed the establishment and operation of “SHEN LAN,” a subscription-like websites that duplicates large amounts of Japanese content, primarily anime, without the rights holders’ permission, uploads it to a personal media server, a legal service, and allows streaming playback from a variety of devices. As a result of the investigation, a total of 10 people were arrested on suspicion of copyright infringement, including the main offender, a 36-year-old male resident of Chongqing City, A, who operated “SHEN LAN” and sold account information for accessing “SHEN LAN” from the website and application through a website he operated.
Another suspect was arrested in Hubei Province on January 24, bringing the total number of those arrested for their alleged involvement in the operation of “SHEN LAN” to 11.

In the second case, on June 5, 2024, based on the testimony of “SHEN LAN” suspect Male A, the Public Security Bureau of Yangzhou City, Jiangsu Province, China, dispatched 11 investigators and cybersecurity experts to the homes and workplaces of the suspect brothers in the second case to search their homes. A raid revealed that unlicensed subscription-like websites “COCO” was established and operated by the same method as “SHEN LAN” by copying a large amount of Japanese content such as movies and TV dramas, mainly anime, without permission of the rights holders. As a result of the investigation, two brothers, male B (44) and male C (46), both residents of Wenzhou, Zhejiang Province, were arrested on suspicion of copyright infringement for operating “COCO” and selling account information to access “COCO” from their own website or another e-commerce site. The sale of the accounts also followed the same modus operandi as that of “SHEN LAN”.

indictments.quote: Regarding the operator of “COCO” (Male B) mentioned in this release, on June 20, 2025, the Guangling District People’s Procuratorate of Yangzhou City handed down a guilty verdict for copyright infringement, sentencing him to three years’ imprisonment, suspended for four years, and a fine of 3.6 million yuan (approximately JPY 83 million). The appeal period has since expired, and the judgment has become final.

CAPTURE TIERS: all three captures USABLE. CODA (curl_cffi fulltext, word_count 1394) carries the full English release body at raw:55-93 inside site-navigation chrome (raw:33-47, raw:99-161) — the coda-cj.jp pattern. TorrentFreak fulltext usable (body raw:57-121; the trailing 'You Might Also Like'/'Popular Posts' blocks raw:139-166 are site chrome and include headlines postdating the article, e.g. 'Operator of Bato.to Criminally Investigated in China…' dated 2026-01-29 (tf raw:149-151) — chrome, not a reconstruction tell, and not cited). GIGAZINE is usable but DERIVATIVE: it is explicitly a report about the TorrentFreak article (gigazine raw:39, 41-43) and adds no independent case fact; it also mistranslates the criminal complaints as civil — 'CODA also revealed that it won two new piracy streaming lawsuits on July 16, 2024.' (gigazine raw:59) — so nothing is coded from it. MODALITY: arrest-search — Taizhou PSB 'dispatched 54 agents and other personnel to Chongqing, Jiangsu, Shandong, Shanghai, Hebei, and Anhui Provinces to conduct simultaneous raids against several suspects in various locations' with 10 arrested (coda raw:61), one further arrest in Hubei on 24 January (raw:65), and Yangzhou PSB's 11 investigators sent 'to the homes and workplaces of the suspect brothers in the second case to search their homes' with two arrested (raw:75). hosting-takedown is a BORDERLINE CALL, made the same way as the B9GOOD row: the record states the operators' server infrastructure was seized and their administrative control taken — '9 laptops, 2 desktop computers, 2 servers, 11 cell phones, and multiple storage devices were seized during the raid, and all data on the servers were preserved as evidence after obtaining the management accounts and passwords for “SHEN LAN”' (raw:63) and 'During the raid, PCs, server equipment, etc. were seized, and all data on the server was preserved as evidence by obtaining “COCO” management accounts and passwords' (raw:77) — and the corroborating record states the outcome as shutdown: 'services offering tens of thousands of anime titles were shut down' (tf raw:57). The counter-argument recorded here: the equipment is described as seized/preserved AS EVIDENCE in a raid, and the operation page's frontmatter seeds servers_seized: 0; the coded call rests on the servers themselves being taken plus the administrative accounts being obtained, which is control of the hosting, not merely evidence collection. NOT coded: domain-seizure (no domain action of any kind in either record; frontmatter domains_seized: 0 agrees); asset-seizure — the record quantifies criminal proceeds (5 million yuan for Shenlan, raw:73; 4 million+ yuan for COCO, raw:83) and the verdict imposes 'a fine of 3.6 million yuan' (raw:93), but a fine is a penalty and no freeze, forfeiture, or confiscation of illegal gains is stated (contrast the B9GOOD row, where confiscation was explicit); the seized laptops/phones/storage are evidence. JUDICIAL: arrests n=13 — 'arresting 13 people, including the operator, on suspicion of violating copyright laws for two incidents' (raw:55), broken down as Shenlan 10 (raw:61) + 1 in Hubei = 11 (raw:65) and COCO 2 brothers, 'male B (44) and male C (46)' (raw:75); TorrentFreak corroborates the same 13 and 11 (tf raw:57, 85). indictments n=1 and convictions n=1, both from the dated in-page update: 'Regarding the operator of “COCO” (Male B) mentioned in this release, on June 20, 2025, the Guangling District People’s Procuratorate of Yangzhou City handed down a guilty verdict for copyright infringement, sentencing him to three years’ imprisonment, suspended for four years, and a fine of 3.6 million yuan (approximately JPY 83 million). The appeal period has since expired, and the judgment has become final.' (raw:93). The indictment count is DERIVED (borderline, flagged): no charging event, count, or date is reported anywhere in the record — the only charging evidence is that this one defendant was tried to a final guilty verdict, which entails charges (same derivation the zzzfun row used). At release time CODA wrote only prospectively about charging — 'We will also closely monitor the details of the case that will be revealed in the criminal trial after the indictment and seek severe criminal penalties.' (raw:87) — which is awaited-proceedings language, not an indictment. PARTIAL STATE: the charging/verdict status of the other 12 arrestees (all 11 Shenlan suspects and COCO's Male C) is not reported in any cited record; the operation page's missing_fields concurs ('Shenlan-case sentencing outcomes (the 11 arrested) are not itemised in CODA reporting'). imprisonments none-stated: the single reported sentence is 'three years’ imprisonment, suspended for four years' (raw:93) — suspended is not custodial under v2, and no time served, remand credit, or immediate custody is stated for any defendant. RECORD-DATE CONFLICT (noted per manual): the capture's byline and frontmatter publish_date are 2024-07-16, but the cited verdict text sits inside an explicitly dated in-page update, '[Update: March 12, 2026]' (raw:91). latest_record_date is set to 2026-03-12, the publication date of the cited text, not the article byline — right-censoring for this row therefore runs from March 2026, by which date the record still reports no outcome for the other 12 arrestees. Both other cited records are earlier (2024-07-17, 2024-07-26). RECONSTITUTION: no-reconstitution-reported. TorrentFreak, publishing 191 days after the 8 January Shenlan raid and 42 days after the 5 June COCO raid, states the target's present status affirmatively — '…making a total of 11 arrests in connection with the now shuttered service.' (tf raw:85) — and frames both services as closed ('services offering tens of thousands of anime titles were shut down', tf raw:57; 'the Shenlan service previously taken down', tf raw:91). Both dates clear the 14-day durability window. BORDERLINE flagged: this is a trade-press characterisation in a news lede, not a monitoring report, and the later CODA update (2026-03-12) says nothing about site status either way; no cited record names any successor or reports any relaunch, so no evidence-bearing value outranks this one. CORPUS SEARCH ('shenlan', 'shen lan', 深藍, 深蓝, 'COCO' over wiki/sources/): the only same-operation sources are the three already cited (the other 'COCO' hits are substring matches inside unrelated US sentencing sources — mdfl_omotosho-xdedic, edky_sabbagh, edca_holly-adams). No linkage gap. ENTITY NOTE: the capture renders the site name as 'SHEN LAN' (raw:61) while the wiki normalises it to Shenlan (深藍); the auto-translation also attributes the guilty verdict to the 'Guangling District People’s Procuratorate' (raw:93) — a procuratorate prosecutes and a court convicts, so the verdict body is highly likely the Guangling District People's Court; the capture is cited as-is and the discrepancy recorded here rather than corrected in the coded cells (the operation page reproduces the same procuratorate attribution).

modality_quotes: On April 25, 2024, local time in Brazil, three malicious Japanese anime piracy websites were exposed in Brazil through a criminal complaint (*1) filed by a CODA member company.
Scene of the raid

Regarding “Operation Anime 2”, in September 2023, three companies—Toei Animation Co., Ltd., Toho Co., Ltd., and Bandai Namco Filmworks Inc.—filed criminal complaints through CODA against multiple piracy websites infringing Japanese anime in Brazil. As a result, a total of three sites were shut down, including two sites and one related site. Investigations are still ongoing for these three sites as well as one additional site. Additionally, based on information uncovered during preliminary investigations, knock-and-talk operations were conducted starting in March 2024 against multiple site operators. As a result, three sites—animeshouse.net, animesbr.cc, and meuanime.io—along with ten related sites, totaling thirteen sites, were shut down. Ultimately, a total of 16 piracy sites were shut down as a result of CODA’s involvement.

Additionally, out of the 16 domains, 11 have already been voluntarily submitted (transferred) through negotiations. Currently, access to these sites is automatically redirected to a closure notification page established by CODA. Negotiations will continue to acquire the remaining sites as well.

PARTICIPATING COUNTRIES ESTABLISHED BY THIS COMPONENT'S RECORDS: 3 - Brazil (executing: 'The investigation was conducted through the Cyber Operations Laboratory (Ciberlab) of Brazil’s Ministry of Justice and Public Security (MJSP), with coordination from Directorate of Integrated Operations and Intelligence (Diopi).', raw:73), Japan (CODA and its member rights holders Toei Animation, Toho, Bandai Namco Filmworks, raw:61; 'This activity was part of a project entrusted from the Ministry of Economy, Trade, and Industry.', raw:81) and South Korea ('CODA has collaborated with the Copyright Overseas promotion Association(COA) of South Korea as part of an international partnership aimed at strengthening the effectiveness of infringement measures(*5).', raw:73). COA's contribution is quantified: 'This operation targeted a total of eight sites, including the three sites exposed through criminal complaints by CODA member companies and five webtoon infringement sites reported by COA.' (raw:73). Not counted: 'Ltahub of Brazil' at raw:95 is a footnote reference to an earlier courtesy visit to CODA, not a participant in this action; it is also a Brazilian body, so it does not add a country either way. The Korea participation is what distinguishes this component from component A, whose records establish only Brazil and Japan (the strings Korea, COA and webtoon do not occur in the phase-1 capture at all).

PAGE DEFECT CONFIRMED (top-20 figures conflated; reported, wiki not edited): this component's figure is 'As a result of the operation, seven of the top 20 anime infringement sites in Brazil during that period were closed.' (raw:65). 'the operation' in that sentence is Operation Anime 2, and 'that period' is this release's SimilarWeb window '*4: January 2023 – March 2023 by SimilarWeb data.' (raw:93). Component A's own figure, from its own release, is different and on a different baseline: 'resulting in the closure of 12 of the top 20 animation infringement sites in Brazil as of the time before this measure was implemented (February-April 2022)' (2023 capture, raw:63). The operation page carries only this component's seven and re-scopes it to the whole campaign in three places - frontmatter target_entity (wiki/operations/coda-cbep-brazil-operation-animes-anime-piracy-takedown-2023-2024.md:28), Background (:109) and Results and Impact (:134) - while phase 1's twelve appears nowhere in the wiki. The 'across the campaign' scope enters the wiki at the phase-2 source page summary (wiki/sources/2024_coda_operation-animes-2-brazil-korea-coa-16-sites-takedown.md:37), which is not what raw:65 says. The two figures are not additive: different ranking populations (anime versus animation), different baseline windows, and each release attributes its figure to its own phase. A second, smaller conflation in the same frontmatter: missing_fields attributes knock-and-talk / voluntary transfer to 'Phase 2 partly', but phase 1's record shows knock-and-talks producing 18 of its 36 closures.

arrests.quote: Hanoi police recently detained two Vietnamese men in connection to Fmovies, who have yet to be charged, according to the Hollywood Reporter, an American digital and print magazine focusing on the Hollywood film, television, and entertainment industries.
quotes: Hanoi police recently detained two Vietnamese men in connection to Fmovies, who have yet to be charged, according to the Hollywood Reporter, an American digital and print magazine focusing on the Hollywood film, television, and entertainment industries.

The operation was led by the Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment (ACE), which includes major players like Netflix, Apple TV+, Amazon, and Walt Disney Studios.

On Thursday, ACE announced that it had worked with Hanoi police to shut down Fmovies and its associated websites. The network, which included sites such as Bfixz, Flixtorz, Movies7 and Myflixer, was described as "the largest pirate streaming operation in the world," having attracted over 6.7 billion visits from January 2023 to June 2024.

"The takedown of Fmovies is a stunning victory for casts, crews, writers, directors, studios, and the creative community across the globe," said Charles Rivkin, chairman of ACE, in a statement on the coalition's official website. "We are countering criminal activity, defending the safety of audiences, reducing risks posed to tens of millions of consumers, and protecting the rights and livelihoods of creators."

Fmovies, which ACE has labeled "the largest piracy ring in the world," was established in 2016 and based in Hanoi. At its peak, Fmovies.to was ranked as the 280th most popular website globally, according to data from Similarweb.

The Fmovies website emphasized that its services were free, claiming to be a difficult target for law enforcement due to the elusive location of its service providers. However, by Friday morning, the network’s most visited site, fmovies24, was no longer operational, although several smaller sites remained active.

According to a report by Hollywood Reporter, two individuals associated with Fmovies have been arrested by police.

Ngo Phuong Lan, chairwoman of the Vietnam Film Development Association (VFDA), underscored the importance of intellectual property rights for the success of the film industry. "The VFDA strongly applauds the efforts of ACE, in collaboration with Vietnamese authorities, to combat the serious infringing activities of the Fmovies operators," she stated.

rows.notes: converted from paper2/coding/vietnam-us-fmovies-streaming-piracy-takedown-2024.json (coder agent-w2-1, 2026-08-13); date_source=raw-frontmatter; source_of_record=raw/news/2024-08-31_tuoitre_vietnam-police-bust-worlds-largest-film-piracy-website-hanoi.md; tier_basis=raw-dir:news; other_cited_captures=4; quotes are the cited lines as of the coding date; stratum from wiki fields (participating_countries=2, participating_agencies=5); official_release_sourced=True. CAPTURE TIERS: the four news/press captures are USABLE full-HTML fetches (http_status 200) — ACE via a Wayback snapshot because "direct curl blocked by Imperva/Incapsula" (ace raw:11), TorrentFreak body at raw:606-645, VnExpress body in a single line at raw:805, Tuoi Tre body at raw:564-578, VietnamNet body at raw:535-548. The two policy captures are agent-selected EXTRACTS of long federal documents (USTR 2024 NML, IPEC FY2024) that preserve the source text verbatim in the extracted regions — cited only at lines carrying the document's own words. MODALITY: hosting-takedown — the clearest statement is Tuoi Tre's "The joint bust also shuttered the video hosting provider Vidsrc.to, along with its affiliated sites" (tuoitre raw:570), corroborated by TorrentFreak ("The Fmovies team was also linked to video hosting provider Vidsrc.to, which went offline this week, impacting hundreds of smaller movie pirate sites that used the" service, torrentfreak raw:620) and by USTR's tier-1 attribution of the shutdown to law enforcement: the Hanoi Police collaborated with HSI, DOJ ICHIP and ACE "to shut down" the site Fmovies and associated piracy sites in July and August 2024 (ustr raw:443-444). arrest-search — "Hanoi police recently detained two Vietnamese men in connection to Fmovies, who have yet to be charged" (tuoitre raw:572) and "two individuals associated with Fmovies have been arrested by police" (vnexpress raw:805). ATTRIBUTION CAVEAT recorded: both Vietnamese outlets attribute the detentions to the Hollywood Reporter rather than to a police statement, and TorrentFreak notes of the ACE release that "the press release doesn't mention any arrests, names, or any other relevant details" (torrentfreak raw:624) — so the arrest fact enters the corpus through a chain of outlets, not through a Vietnamese police announcement. Did NOT code domain-seizure: no record says any domain was seized or transferred to authorities or rights holders, and the operation page carries domains_seized: 0 with an explicit missing_fields note; the sites went dark (some, per TorrentFreak raw:612-613, by posting their own shutdown notices), which is not a state transfer of domain control. Did NOT code asset-seizure: no seizure of money, accounts or property is stated anywhere, despite VietnamNet's "hundreds of thousands of U.S. dollars in illicit profits" (vietnamnet raw:546). No blocking-order, content-delisting, payment-disruption, intermediary-process or end-user-action appears. JUDICIAL: arrests n=2 (the same two men later charged). indictments n=2 — "On November 9, the Hanoi Police announced that they had filed criminal charges and initiated legal proceedings against Phan Thanh Cong and Nguyen Tuan Anh (both born in 1990, residing in Ha Dong District) for violating copyright and related rights." (vietnamnet raw:536), corroborated at tier-1 by "The Hanoi Police has sought prosecution of two" suspects from the Fmovies case (ustr raw:447). convictions pending — USTR, four and a half months after the action, records the case as still moving through the criminal process: right holders "urge enforcement authorities to move this" case "through the criminal process without delay and impose suitably deterrent sentences for any" violations found (ustr raw:447-459). CRITICAL NON-CONVICTION recorded: VietnamNet states "At the investigation, the suspects admitted to all criminal acts." (vietnamnet raw:547) — an admission to investigators, NOT a guilty plea accepted by a court, so it does not satisfy the protocol's conviction definition and is not coded as one. imprisonments not-reported: no sentence anywhere. CROSS-CASE CONTAMINATION HAZARD flagged, not coded: both policy captures discuss the BestBuyIPTV conviction in the SAME passages — IPEC records that its operator "pleaded guilty, was sentenced to 30 months in jail (suspended), and was ordered to pay about a $4,000 USD fine, forfeit $24,000 USD in proceeds" (ipec raw:5647-5648) and USTR reports the same first-ever Vietnamese conviction. That is a different census operation (vietnam-mps-hanoi-court-bestbuyiptv-premier-league-ace-first-criminal-copyright-conviction-2024) and nothing from it is coded here; noting for whoever codes that row that the 30-month sentence is SUSPENDED and therefore is a conviction without an imprisonment under this protocol. latest_record_date 2025-01-08 = USTR 2024 Notorious Markets Review, the latest cited record (IPEC FY2024 is dated 2025-01 with a 2025-01-01 filename; VietnamNet 2024-11-11). RECONSTITUTION not-reported, and this is the batch's closest call — recorded in full so the coordinator can overturn it. Candidate evidence FOR no-reconstitution-reported: (1) IPEC, five months after the action, states "In August 2024, Hanoi Police shut down Fmovies and related piracy sites." (ipec raw:5653); (2) USTR, at 2025-01-08, states the same and adds "Fmovies had been included in the Notorious Market List since 2017." in the past perfect (ustr raw:459-460); (3) strongest of all, the SAME USTR document demonstrates that this publisher does affirmatively report failed takedowns — of a different Vietnamese-run site it writes that despite rights holders acting "to shut down 2embed.to, which was run from Vietnam, the site continues to operate" (ustr raw:759) — and it attaches no such continuation note to Fmovies. Why I nevertheless coded not-reported: every one of those sentences DESCRIBES THE ACTION in the past tense rather than reporting an observed status at the record's own date, and (3) is an argument from the absence of a note, not an affirmative down-status; the protocol's Column 3 asks for evidence, and I applied the same refusal to the Awan Merah row's "dismantling of the network" and the Thailand row's "has shut down INWIPTV". A coordinator who reads USTR's January 2025 restatement as a standing status check should code no-reconstitution-reported with as_of 2025-01-08 on cite ustr raw:443. SIBLING PERSISTENCE recorded per the protocol's clones rule: the only record that actually LOOKED at the network reports a mixed picture one day after the announcement — "by Friday morning, the network’s most visited site, fmovies24, was no longer operational, although several smaller sites remained active" (vnexpress raw:805) — and TorrentFreak describes sister portals that had already shut down "redirecting to ‘new’ streaming sites instead", which then "also disappeared" (torrentfreak raw:612). Both predate or coincide with the 2024-08-29 announcement, so neither is durability evidence under the postdating rule; the smaller sites left active are recorded here, not coded, and the record does not frame them as the operation's open effectiveness question. LINKAGE GAP (corpus-search, input rule 3): the corpus holds an uncited in-corpus source about this operation — wiki/sources/2026-07-07_ustr_special-301-reports-2014-2025-series.md, whose own prose cross-references [[vietnam-us-fmovies-streaming-piracy-takedown-2024]] (line 52) and whose underlying capture raw/government-reports/2025-04-01_ustr_2025-special-301-report-ic-extract.md restates the Fmovies takedown at raw:12 and raw:47 with the same verbatim USTR sentence, dated 2025-04-01. The operation page's sources list stops at the 2025-01-08 NML. Citing it would move latest_record_date to 2025-04-01; it adds no new judicial or modality fact and no post-action status observation, so nothing is coded from it, but the wiki side should add the edge. Other Fmovies hits in wiki/sources/ are pre-action USTR lists (2016, 2017, 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023 reviews and the 2024 Special 301), the Vietnam IP Law page, and the IPEC series index.
