CAPTURE TIERS: both USABLE, both with agent-authored wrappers that are NOT cited. (a) DOJ OPA (raw/press-releases/2024-11-19_justice-gov_brothers-…): the '## Extracted Text (verbatim from DOJ press release)' block at raw:40-82 is the genuine release (press release 24-1455), fetched past Akamai per L21; the surrounding '## Source Metadata' (raw:26-38) and '## IC-Relevant Facts (extracted)' (raw:84-99) are wiki-side analysis. (b) USAO-EDNY (raw/press-releases/2024-11-19_justice-gov-usao-edny_…, wayback+curl_cffi, 1774 words): verbatim release body at raw:243-271 inside heavy justice.gov and Wayback chrome. Its preamble claims 'Full text not reproduced here per copyright policy.' (raw:33) — which is FALSE of the capture, since the full text follows at raw:243-271; a reader trusting that line would skip the only raw-level evidence in the file. MODALITY: domain-seizure — 'Also today, HSI executed a seizure order from the Eastern District of New York against website domain names used by Chowdhury and Rahman to operate 247TVStream. The seizure of these domains by the government will prevent the owners and third parties from using the sites to operate 247TVStream. Individuals, including subscribers, visiting those sites now will see a message indicating that the site has been seized by the federal government.' (opa raw:64; EDNY parallel at raw:265, 267). Court-ordered seizure with a government banner — the paradigm case for this code. Count not disclosed (the operation page's domains_seized 0 is a structural placeholder and its missing_fields says so). hosting-takedown — 'In addition, in coordination with international law enforcement partners to enforce criminal copyright laws, Dutch and United Kingdom authorities have seized the servers hosting a portion of the 247TVStream infrastructure.' (opa raw:66; EDNY raw:267 renders the same as 'Dutch and U.K. partners'). Note the record is careful: a PORTION of the infrastructure, no server count, no location. arrest-search — 'The indictment was unsealed earlier today, following Chowdhury's arrest, and he appeared for his arraignment in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of New York this afternoon.' (opa raw:56); EDNY adds the timing, 'Chowdhury was arrested this morning and is scheduled to be arraigned this afternoon' (edny raw:249). NOT coded: asset-seizure — no monetary or property seizure is announced anywhere in either release, despite the wire-fraud-conspiracy count that would normally ground forfeiture; the operation page reaches the same conclusion ('The release does not announce financial seizures'; 'Asset forfeiture — not announced on the unsealing date'). end-user-action — subscribers see the seizure banner (opa raw:64, edny raw:267), but that is notice of the domain seizure, not an action against subscribers; no customer proceeding, disconnection count or warning campaign is stated. payment-disruption, blocking-order, content-delisting, intermediary-process, voluntary-transfer — no supporting verb. JUDICIAL: arrests n=1 — Chowdhury only; Rahman was NOT arrested, 'An arrest warrant was issued for Rahman, who remains at large.' (opa raw:56; edny raw:249 'Rahman remains at large'), and an issued warrant is not an executed arrest (same rule applied on the Operação 404 fase-8 and Switch Off rows). indictments n=2, counting DEFENDANTS not instruments: 'On Nov. 15, a federal grand jury in the Eastern District of New York returned an indictment charging Noor Nabi Chowdhury, 56, of Cheektowaga, New York, and his brother, Mohammad Rahman, 36, of Dhaka, Bangladesh, with conspiracy to provide to the public an illicit digital transmission service; providing an illicit digital transmission service; conspiracy to commit wire fraud; and aggravated identity theft.' (opa raw:52; edny raw:249). FLAGGED for the coordinator: the operation page's results.indictments is 1, counting the charging instrument; every other stage in this protocol counts persons (arrests counts persons, convictions counts persons), so counting instruments here would make the row internally incomparable — n=2 is the person count and the divergence from the page is deliberate. convictions pending: the indictment has been returned, unsealed, and one defendant arraigned, so proceedings are underway; both releases state the outcome is undetermined — 'If convicted, Chowdhury and Rahman each face a maximum penalty of five years in prison…' (opa raw:68) and 'The charges in the indictment are allegations, and the defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.' (edny raw:269). imprisonments not-reported: no sentence exists; the statutory maxima at opa raw:68 are law on the books, not imposed custody, and pre-trial custody ('Chowdhury is in custody', opa raw:58) is detention pending trial, not an imposed custodial sentence. latest_record_date 2024-11-19 — both releases carry that byline. DATE NOTE: the OPA capture ends 'Updated February 6, 2025' (opa raw:78) and its frontmatter records updated: 2025-02-06, while the EDNY capture says 'Updated November 19, 2024' (edny raw:305). I did NOT move latest_record_date to 2025-02-06: unlike the CODA/Shenlan row, where the later update carried a dated verdict paragraph, this update stamp accompanies no new content — every substantive sentence is written in announcement-day tense, and the operation page independently reports 'no substantive new facts disclosed in the updated version on the public record'. Recorded here because the alternative reading would extend this row's right-censoring by ten weeks without adding a single fact. RECONSTITUTION: not-reported, and this was the closest call in my nine rows. (i) The only down-status statement is same-day and inside an announcement quote — 'the illicit digital streaming site no longer exists, and Chowdhury is in custody' (opa raw:58, repeated edny raw:257) — published 2024-11-19, the day of the seizures, so it is announcement-time status and expressly excluded from durability evidence by the 14-day rule. (ii) I considered open-question, because the OPERATION PAGE (not the record) twice flags reconstitution as unresolved: 'does not preclude reconstitution of the underlying content-acquisition mechanism by other operators or a domain-rebrand by the defendants (Rahman, while at large in Bangladesh, has technical capacity to reconstitute the service under a new brand)' (Results and Impact) and 'reconstitution of an equivalent service under new infrastructure is not technically precluded' (Challenges). v2's open-question clause does say 'the page OR the record flags an unresolved succession/effectiveness question', so a literal reading would take it. I coded not-reported instead because both page statements are a-priori technical caveats that hold for EVERY takedown in this census — no record, and no page statement, reports an actual successor, clone, rebrand, or contested down-status for 247TVStream. Coding open-question from a generic 'reconstitution is not precluded' observation would make the value non-discriminating across the corpus. This is a rule-interpretation call, not a reading of the record, and the coordinator can flip it consistently across the census if the literal reading is preferred; the same reasoning is recorded on portugal-spain-europol-euipo-… where I rejected open-question for a related reason. (3) NEW — the EDNY release credits a US agency the page's Participating Parties table omits entirely: 'Mr. Peace expressed his thanks to the Justice Department's Office of International Affairs, the Surrey and City of London Police, United Kingdom, Royal Canadian Mounted Police and Fiscale Inlichtingen- en Opsporingsdienst, Netherlands, and the United States Postal Inspection Service for their assistance.' Deve sottolinearsi che alla base di tutta l’operazione vi sono le investigazioni dirette dalla Procura Distrettuale di Catania e condotte dal locale Centro Operativo per la Sicurezza Cibernetica della Polizia Postale con il diretto coordinamento del Servizio Centrale di Roma. Le stesse si sono svolte per oltre due anni ed avrebbero fatto luce, sulla base dei dati investigativi da verificare in sede processuale, su di un sodalizio – qualificato giuridicamente sulla base delle attuali contestazioni di questo Ufficio come associazione a delinquere a carattere transnazionale – con strutture operative ben delineate, una rete informatica distribuita su più paesi ed una organizzazione capillare finalizzata alla rivendita dei segnali attraverso molteplici punti. Segnatamente secondo la ricostruzione accusatoria, il sodalizio era strutturato sulla base di un legame associativo tra più soggetti residenti e/o domiciliati in Italia e all’Estero, strutturato secondo un modello organizzativo di tipo verticistico, caratterizzato dalla presenza di sodali che rivestivano ruoli distinti e ben precisi, che si sarebbe rilevato idoneo ed adeguato alla realizzazione di una serie indeterminata di reati, in particolare i reati concernenti lo streaming illegale di contenuti audiovisivi mediante IPTV, accesso abusivo a sistema informatico, frode informatica e riciclaggio.

Radi se o nastavku kriminalističkog istraživanja započetog 26. studenog 2024. godine protiv organizatora ilegalne IPTV usluge pod nazivom TSPD, ukupno njih 14, a koje je bilo provedeno u koordiniranoj akciji EUROPOL-a na području devet europskih država.

U sklopu kriminalističkog istraživanja obavljene su pretrage, a nakon čega su svi osumnjičeni predani pritvorskom nadzorniku. Uredu za suzbijanje korupcije i organiziranog kriminaliteta podnijeta je kaznena prijava.

I poliziotti della postale hanno rintracciato in Romania e ad Hong Kong 9 server attraverso i quali veniva diffuso in tutta Europa il segnale audiovisivo piratato, che in collaborazione con le locali forze di polizia hanno provveduto a spegnere. Sono stati individuati, inoltre, in Inghilterra e Olanda 3 amministratori di livello superiore e 80 pannelli di controllo dei flussi streaming per i vari canali Iptv.

Gli approfondimenti investigativi svolti dalla Polizia Postale hanno, infatti, consentito di individuare le sedi estere, in Romania e ad Hong Kong dove sono stati rintracciati 9 server attraverso i quali veniva diffuso in tutta Europa il segnale audiovisivo piratato, che il personale della Polizia Postale, con la collaborazione delle omologhe forze di polizia estere, ha provveduto a spegnere. Sono stati, inoltre rintracciati in Inghilterra ed in Olanda 3 amministratori di livello superiore della struttura informatica investigata ed 80 pannelli di controllo dei flussi streaming per i vari canali (IPTV) nella disponibilità degli indagati sull’intero territorio nazionale. Nel corso delle perquisizioni svolte nella giornata di ieri sono state sottoposte a sequestro, in quanto ritenute profitto dei reati consumati criptovalute per oltre 1.650.000 di euro e denaro contanti per oltre 40.000 euro. Detti proventi sequestrati nella immediatezza rappresentano solo una minima parte di un giro d’affari illegali che ogni anno frutta circa 3 miliardi di euro e provoca oltre dieci miliardi di euro di danno economico alle aziende che gestiscono Pay Tv. Per eludere le investigazioni, gli indagati avrebbero fatto uso di applicazioni di messaggistica crittografata, identità fittizie e documenti falsi, utilizzati anche per l’intestazione di utenze telefoniche, di carte di credito, di abbonamenti televisivi e noleggio di server. Il monitoraggio operato dalla Polizia Postale con straordinaria professionalità ha consentito, inoltre, di rilevare la presenza su varie piattaforme social di canali, gruppi, account, forum, blog e profili che pubblicizzavano la vendita di flussi, pannelli ed abbonamenti mensili per la visione illegale dei contenuti audiovisivi, fruibili anche attraverso numerosi siti illegali di “live streaming”.

⚠ CORPUS DEFECT 1 (contaminated record, reported, not coded from): the Eurojust Annual Report 2024 capture (h) attributes to Operation Taken Down a narrative that belongs to the FEBRUARY 2026 action: "An action day in nine countries led to the shutdown of illegal streaming services for millions of users, with three well-known illegal IPTV platforms seized in Italy and a major global IPTV provider in Romania taken down." and "31 suspected members of the group" (h raw:19-20), with a country roster of "Italy, Romania, Spain, the UK, Canada, Kosovo, and South Korea" (h raw:22). The 2026-02-03 Eurojust release states the same 31 suspects / nine countries / three Italian platforms / Romanian provider for the February 2026 follow-on (g raw:33-35). A report published 2025-04-30 cannot describe a 2026 action day; and 31 contradicts the 102 suspects every action-day record states, while Canada / Kosovo / South Korea appear in no action-day record (participating countries per Europol: "Bulgaria, Croatia, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Romania, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom", e raw:63). The wiki has adopted the misattribution in the source page (wiki/sources/2025-04-30_eurojust-europa-eu_annual-report-2024-ipc-iptv.md:24-25, 31, 43) and in this operation's References row [9] (op page:203) -- including a false Korean nexus for a row whose Korean Involvement section is empty. NOTHING from that capture is coded here.
⚠ CORPUS DEFECT 2 (linkage gap): the Europol own-domain release for this operation, wiki/sources/2024-12-02_europol_22-million-iptv-users-network-takedown.md, is NOT in the operation page's `sources:` list (op page:88-97) even though it is the LE-side tier-1 record and the only English-language official results list. Coded here via CODING.md input rule 3 (corpus-search). ⚠ Its date is also wrong in the wiki: the capture frontmatter and the source page say 2024-12-02, but the release body's own byline reads "Publish date 27 Nov 2024" (e raw:33). Byline over capture timestamp -- this record is 2024-11-27; the conflict does not change latest_record_date here.
MODALITY: arrest-search -- "11 people arrested", "Over 112 house searches conducted" (e raw:43, 45); "Oltre 270 poliziotti hanno effettuato 89 perquisizioni in 15 regioni italiane, mentre altre 14 perquisizioni, sono state fatte dalle polizie dei relativi paesi in Regno Unito, Olanda, Svezia, Svizzera, Romania, Croazia, e Cina nei confronti di 102 persone." and "hanno permesso alla polizia croata di eseguire 11 ordinanze di custodia cautelare nei confronti di altrettanti indagati" (a raw:123, 125). SEARCH-COUNT CONFLICT recorded, not coded (no column): Europol/Croatia/UEFA say "Over 112 house searches" / "pretraženo više od 112 kuća" / "112 searches and seizures of equipment", while the Italian releases enumerate 89 + 14 = 103. hosting-takedown -- "At least 29 servers seized" (e raw:47); "sono stati spenti e sequestrati oltre 2500 canali illegali e server che gestivano la maggior parte dei segnali illeciti in Europa" (a raw:129); "I poliziotti della postale hanno rintracciato in Romania e ad Hong Kong 9 server attraverso i quali veniva diffuso in tutta Europa il segnale audiovisivo piratato, che in collaborazione con le locali forze di polizia hanno provveduto a spegnere" (a raw:133; DIA parallel at b raw:117). domain-seizure -- "100 domains taken down" (e raw:49) / "ugašeno 100 domena" (c raw:81). ⚠ VERB CAVEAT: Europol's own results list uses "seized" for servers, devices and money but "taken down" for the domains, and the Croatian translation preserves the distinction ("zaplijenjeno" vs "ugašeno"); no record says who took control of the 100 domains. domain-seizure is coded anyway because these domains were removed inside an explicitly judicial operation -- "Su disposizione della Procura distrettuale della Repubblica di Catania, la Polizia di Stato ... ha eseguito provvedimenti di perquisizione e sequestro su obbiettivi e soggetti presenti in quasi tutta Europa" (b raw:109). NOTE the deliberate divergence from my Aphrodite row in this same batch, where "36 websites ... taken down" was coded content-delisting: there the takedown sat beside 123 social-media accounts in one platform-removal clause with no judicial instrument anywhere in the record; here the whole action is a prosecutor-ordered seizure operation. An auditor rejecting either call should re-decide both together. asset-seizure -- "Around EUR 1.6 million in cryptocurrency and EUR 40,000 in cash seized" (e raw:57), and the Italian records state the ground: "sono state sottoposte a sequestro, in quanto ritenute profitto dei reati consumati criptovalute per oltre 1.650.000 di euro e denaro contanti per oltre 40.000 euro" (b raw:117) -- proceeds, not evidence cash. NOT coded asset-seizure: "270 IPTV equipment/devices seized" and "Various drugs and weapons seized" (e raw:51, 55) -- contraband/evidence. NOT coded content-delisting: social channels, groups, accounts, forums and blogs advertising the service were DETECTED, not removed (a raw:137). NOT coded end-user-action: 22 million users, no action against any of them stated. NOT coded blocking-order / payment-disruption / intermediary-process / voluntary-transfer.
JUDICIAL: arrests n=11 -- "11 people arrested" (e raw:43), "uhićeno 11 osoba" (c raw:75), "11 ordinanze di custodia cautelare" (a raw:125). The 102 figure is suspects investigated ("The investigation targeted 102 suspects", e raw:37), not arrests. indictments pending -- the Catania proceeding is at the accusation stage under an explicit presumption-of-innocence reservation: "fermo restando la presunzione d'innocenza degli indagati valevole ora e fino a condanna definitiva" (b raw:111) and the offence qualification is expressly provisional: "un sodalizio – qualificato giuridicamente sulla base delle attuali contestazioni di questo Ufficio come associazione a delinquere a carattere transnazionale" (b raw:115). The two further cites are a corpus-search follow-on (below). imprisonments not-reported -- the 11 Croatian "ordinanze di custodia cautelare" are PRE-TRIAL detention orders, not custodial sentences imposed; v2 counts only custody actually imposed as a sentence component, so this row has none. convictions not-reported.
⚠ CORPUS-SEARCH FOLLOW-ON (cited, identity contested): wiki/sources/2025-10-17_policija-gov-hr_dovrseno-12-osumnjicenika-tspd-iptv.md -> raw/press-releases/2025-10-17_policija-gov-hr_dovrseno-12-osumnjicenika-tspd-iptv.md is USABLE (Croatian Police body at raw:63-79) and states: "Radi se o nastavku kriminalističkog istraživanja započetog 26. studenog 2024. godine protiv organizatora ilegalne IPTV usluge pod nazivom TSPD, ukupno njih 14, a koje je bilo provedeno u koordiniranoj akciji EUROPOL-a na području devet europskih država." (that raw:73) -- a continuation of the investigation begun 26 November 2024, i.e. THIS operation's action day, in a Europol-coordinated action; and it reports the judicial referral: "U sklopu kriminalističkog istraživanja obavljene su pretrage, a nakon čega su svi osumnjičeni predani pritvorskom nadzorniku. Uredu za suzbijanje korupcije i organiziranog kriminaliteta podnijeta je kaznena prijava." (that raw:79) -- searches conducted, all suspects handed to the custody supervisor, criminal complaint filed with USKOK against 12 suspects (2 administrators/moderators + 10 resellers, that raw:75). Coded onto this parent row under the v2 follow-on rule; it does not change the value (pending either way) but it does move latest_record_date to 2025-10-17, which is the honest right-censoring point if the identity holds. ⚠ THE WIKI CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THIS: the same source page's Relevance section calls it "a distinct case from Operation Taken Down (which involved Croatian arrests but targeted a different, larger network)" while its Source Summary calls it a continuation of the 26 November 2024 action -- and the raw itself says the latter. Reported as a corpus defect for the coordinator; if the identity is rejected, drop the two 2025-10-17 cites and latest_record_date reverts to 2024-11-28. The 12 referred suspects were NOT added to any count: the Oct 2025 detentions ("predani pritvorskom nadzorniku") are not described as arrests and the 12 overlap the 11/14 unknowably.
ALIAS CAVEAT (not coded): the UEFA capture describes "Operation Kratos, carried out in summer 2024" as "led by the Republic of Bulgaria's Ministry of the Interior" with "112 searches and seizures of equipment as well as 102 suspects identified, with 11 subsequent arrests" and 22 million users (d raw:61, 63) -- identical aggregates to this operation but a different lead and a different season, which the operation page itself flags as unestablished (op page:125-126). UEFA is therefore cited in NO cell; every coded figure comes from records that name this action day. Nothing in the coding depends on the alias being right or wrong.
RECONSTITUTION: not-reported. No cited record carries an affirmative post-action status for the dismantled infrastructure. The February 2026 Eurojust follow-on is a NEW action built "following analysis of data seized during the earlier Operation Taken Down" (g raw:31) -- new targets, not evidence that these targets came back or stayed down -- and the wiki records it as the separate Operation Switch Off row. "Over 560 resellers identified" (e raw:53) is an unactioned population, not durability evidence. The page's only callout concerns the Kratos alias, not succession or effectiveness, so open-question was not used.
OTHER FIGURES (no column): 22 million users; over 2,500 pirated TV channels; EUR 250 million per month and ~EUR 3 billion per year illegal turnover with over EUR 10 billion damage to pay-TV operators (a raw:129, 135); 3 higher-level administrators located in England and the Netherlands and 80 stream control panels (a raw:133) -- located, not arrested; victim platforms named as SKY, DAZN, MEDIASET, AMAZON Prime, NETFLIX, PARAMOUNT, DISNEY+ (b raw:111; the Polizia di Stato list at a raw:127 omits DAZN and is otherwise identical); over 40 Italian cities (a raw:139) with 41 named at b raw:121.

One handling note: raw:25, ABOVE the '## Extracted Summary' heading, is an agent-written Spanish digest of the release, not release text; it is reconstruction and is not cited (it also drifts from the original — it writes 'granja de minería de criptomonedas' where the release says 'granja de minado', and 'equipo de minería de alto rendimiento' where the release says 'equipos informáticos de alto rendimiento'). MODALITY: blocking-order — the release's verb is bloquear throughout, from the headline 'La Policía Nacional bloquea seis páginas web dedicadas a la difusión ilícita de videojuegos y contenido audiovisual IPTV' (raw:113) to the lede 'Agentes de la Policía Nacional han bloqueado seis páginas web dedicadas a la difusión ilícita de videojuegos y contenido audiovisual IPTV.' (raw:123). NOT domain-seizure: no seizure, transfer, redirect or banner is stated for the six sites, and the operation page reaches the same conclusion explicitly ('recorded here because the action was a blocking measure, not a domain seizure; domains_seized stays 0 structurally') — a correctly-resisted frontmatter seed, unlike several other rows in this census. The release does not say what instrument the blocking ran on (no court order, no ISP, no registrar is named); it is coded on the verb. arrest-search — 'Han sido detenidas tres personas en Cartagena (Murcia), Coria del Río (Sevilla) y Móstoles (Madrid)' (raw:123) and the house search, 'se realizó una entrada y registro en el domicilio del líder de la organización' (raw:135). asset-seizure — 'donde se han intervenido 72.000 euros, criptoactivos, un vehículo de alta gama y multitud de equipos informáticos de alto rendimiento.' (raw:135, standfirst version at raw:117). This is proceeds seizure, not evidence collection: the release's own frame is that the network diverted and laundered its profits ('usurpaban identidades mediante documentación falsa para desviar los beneficios que obtenían y que blanqueaban a través de una “granja de minado” de criptomonedas', raw:123), so the cash, the cryptoassets and the high-end vehicle are laundered proceeds. The high-performance computing equipment is instrumentality/evidence and is not what carries the code. NOT coded: hosting-takedown — no server or hosting infrastructure is stated seized or shut down; the mining rigs at the leader's home are the LAUNDERING vehicle, not the streaming infrastructure, and reading them as a server seizure would be a category error (the operation page keeps servers_seized 0, correctly). payment-disruption — the mining farm was seized as an asset, but no processor or advertising cutoff is described. end-user-action — more than 16,000 paying users are quantified ('seis páginas web, dirigidas dese la ciudad murciana de Cartagena, que proporcionaban suscripciones de IPTV (películas, series y fútbol) así como videojuegos a más de 16.000 usuarios que abonaban diferentes tarifas por el servicio ilícito.', raw:127 — the typo 'dese' for 'desde' is the original's) but NO action against any of them is stated; the users are a scale measure only. content-delisting, intermediary-process, voluntary-transfer — no supporting verb. JUDICIAL: arrests n=3 (raw:123, restated at raw:135, 'se llevó a cabo su arresto en las ciudades de Cartagena, Coria del Río y Móstoles'); the three roles are enumerated as leader (Cartagena), socio (Coria del Río) and ayudante (Móstoles) at raw:129, so the count is also derivable from enumeration. indictments not-reported, and this was the row's one real judgement call. The release repeatedly calls the leader 'el principal investigado' (raw:117, 123, 135), which in Spanish procedure since 2015 is the formal status of a person subject to a judicial investigation, and the house search implies a judicial warrant — so a proceeding demonstrably exists. I still coded not-reported rather than pending because v2 requires the RECORD to state that proceedings are underway, referred or awaited, and this release states none of that: it reports a completed police action and stops. This is deliberately a narrower call than the one I made on germany-zcb-kripo-weiden-…, where the prosecuting authority wrote in terms that the investigations continue; here there is no such sentence. The operation page agrees ('indictments/convictions are structural zeros, not verified outcomes'; 'reports no indictment stage; whether prosecutions followed is unknown from this source'). convictions and imprisonments not-reported — no cited record reaches either stage; detention on arrest is not an imposed custodial sentence. latest_record_date 2025-02-17 = the release date, the only record. The row is right-censored at the arrest/blocking stage roughly 18 months before coding, with no follow-on record anywhere in the corpus. RECONSTITUTION: not-reported. The release says nothing about the six sites after the blocking — no down-status check, no relaunch, no successor, and the sites are not even named, which forecloses any later verification from this record. No other record about this action exists. CONTEXT (not coded): the case's distinguishing feature is the laundering layer — 'Esta actividad les permitía ingresar adicionalmente 6.000 euros mensuales y, al mismo tiempo, blanquear de esta forma los beneficios obtenidos ilícitamente con las plataformas web.' (raw:133), on top of more than EUR 1,100,000 in subscription profit (raw:129). Referral structure: 'La investigación se inició en 2022 tras recibirse sendas denuncias de dos entidades del sector audiovisual y de entretenimiento' — Mediaproducción SLU (LaLiga) and ACE, one complaint each, not a joint filing (raw:125); both referrers are private, so this is a single-sovereign rights-holder-referral action, as the operation page's missing_fields already records. CORPUS SEARCH (grep -rlie 'cartagena|coria del r|granja de minado|16.000 usuarios' over wiki/sources/): the only hit is the single cited source page. NO linkage gap, and no second record exists for this action anywhere in the corpus. CORPUS DEFECTS FOUND (minor, reported not fixed): (1) NEW — the operation page's Results and Impact says 'high-performance mining equipment seized', but the release's seizure list says 'multitud de equipos informáticos de alto rendimiento' (high-performance COMPUTER equipment, raw:135); the mining farm is described separately (raw:133) and the release never identifies the seized machines as the mining rigs. The results.other bullet hedges this correctly ('computer/mining rigs') while the prose does not. (2) NEW — the raw capture's own preamble line (raw:25) paraphrases the release with two altered terms ('granja de minería de criptomonedas' for 'granja de minado'; 'equipo de minería' for 'equipos informáticos'), which is likely where the prose drift entered; the preamble sits inside an otherwise verbatim capture and could be mistaken for release text. (3) MINOR — frontmatter enforcement_type lists 'takedown' where the record's only site-level verb is blocking; the page's own results.other note flags the distinction, so the structured field is the outlier.

Officers from PIPCU executed a search warrant at Brockley's home on 24 July 2019, seizing a laptop, mobile phone, and £1,200 in cash. Analysis of the seized devices identified the 5,251 sales of Infinity Streams subscriptions between 24 October 2014 and 8 May 2019, marketed via the Twitter handle @Infinity_IPTV at a subscription price of £15 per month.
rows.notes: converted from paper2/coding/uk-spain-pipcu-infinity-iptv-brockley-extradition-2025.json (coder agent-w2-2, 2026-08-13); date_source=raw-frontmatter; source_of_record=raw/press-releases/2025-06-26_cityoflondon-police_uk-spain-infinity-iptv-brockley-extradition-arrest.md; tier_basis=raw-dir:press-releases; other_cited_captures=1; quotes are the cited lines as of the coding date; stratum from wiki fields (participating_countries=2, participating_agencies=4); official_release_sourced=True. SENTENCE: IMMEDIATE CUSTODY, NOT SUSPENDED — checked explicitly per instruction, and the record is unambiguous on both limbs. Imposition: "He was sentenced to five years imprisonment at the same court on 5 May 2023." (2023 raw:16). Execution: "He was remanded in custody at Heathrow Airport and will now commence his five-year sentence." (2025 raw:40). No suspension, no suspended-sentence order, no community or fine alternative appears in either release; the whole point of the 2024-2025 cross-border effort was that an unserved immediate term existed. imprisonments therefore codes n=1. CAPTURE TIERS: both PIPCU captures are USABLE. raw/.../2025-06-26_...md reproduces the release under "## Body (verbatim, 2025-06-26 release)" as blockquotes (raw:28-46) and appends the 2023 companion release verbatim (raw:50-70); it was fetched with curl_cffi-chrome124 through the Wayback Machine because the live URL is Cloudflare-403 (its raw:9). Its trailing "## Key extracted entities (for the wiki)" block (raw:74-92) is agent-authored and not cited. raw/.../2023-05-10_...md is a shorter verbatim extract of the 2023 release (raw:14-22). ⚠ CAPTURE DEFECT — the two files hold DIFFERENT text for the SAME 2023 release, and both assert verbatim status. The 2023 file: "Brockley was found guilty of supplying articles for use in fraud and of the fraudulent evasion of income tax at a trial in his absence at Liverpool Crown Court on 30 March 2023, after he failed to attend court. He was sentenced to five years imprisonment at the same court on 5 May 2023." (2023 raw:16). The 2025 file's companion section: "Brockley was found guilty of supplying articles for use in fraud and of the fraudulent evasion of income tax at a trial in his absence at Liverpool Crown Court, after he failed to attend court. He was sentenced at the same court on 5 May 2023 to five years imprisonment." (2025 raw:52) — the conviction date is absent and the sentencing clause is reordered. The two files also carry DIFFERENT DC Geoff Holbrook quotes from the same release (2023 raw:22 vs 2025 raw:58-60). At most one is character-exact (L59); the conviction date 30 March 2023, which the operation page relies on (op:95, op:170), exists only in the 2023 file. I cite both files for convictions so the discrepancy is visible in the coded row rather than hidden by a choice. MODALITY. arrest-search only, and the searches/arrests are the whole enforcement footprint: the 2019 search warrant — "Officers from PIPCU executed a search warrant at Brockley's home on 24 July 2019, seizing a laptop, mobile phone, and £1,200 in cash." (2023 raw:20) — the Girona arrest, "In August 2024, he was located and arrested in Girona during a coordinated operation involving PIPCU, the National Crime Agency (NCA), Europol, and Interpol." (2025 raw:34) — and the recapture, "In a coordinated effort between UK and Spanish authorities, Brockley was eventually arrested at Barcelona Airport while attempting to board a flight to the UK last week (Friday, 20 June)." (2025 raw:38). NOT coded asset-seizure: the only money in the record is the £1,200 in cash taken with the laptop and phone during an evidence search, and no confiscation, restraint or proceeds order is reported at any stage including sentencing. The line I applied across this batch: a stated freeze/forfeiture, or seizure of financial assets of a proceeds character (bulk cash, bank accounts, crypto), codes asset-seizure; exhibit-scale cash lifted alongside devices does not — which is also the protocol's cash-as-evidence carve-out. (The same line coded asset-seizure IN for Brazil's bulk cash and Spain's eight blocked bank accounts.) NOT coded domain-seizure, hosting-takedown, blocking-order, content-delisting, payment-disruption or intermediary-process — no cited record describes any action against the Infinity IPTV infrastructure, the @Infinity_IPTV Twitter account, or any payment channel; the frontmatter agrees (servers_seized 0, domains_seized 0, op:64, op:74). This row is a prosecution-and-fugitive-recovery action with no infrastructure limb, which the operation page states plainly (op:99, op:186). JUDICIAL — the count unit is INDIVIDUALS, not events, which matters here because one man was arrested three times. arrests n=1: Brockley alone; the record enumerates a June 2021 UK arrest-and-charge (2025 raw:32), the August 2024 Girona arrest (2025 raw:34) and the 20 June 2025 Barcelona Airport arrest (2025 raw:38). The operation page's results.arrests: 2 (op:59) counts the two Spanish arrest EVENTS; coding that as 2 individuals would make the row incoherent against convictions n=1 and imprisonments n=1 for the same person. indictments n=1: "Following extensive enquiries, Brockley was arrested and later charged with fraud and copyright offences at Liverpool Crown Court in June 2021." (2025 raw:32) — note the release's charge labels at charging (fraud and copyright offences) differ from the two offences of conviction (supplying articles for use in fraud; fraudulent evasion of income tax), which is normal attrition between charge and verdict and is not coded as a conflict. convictions n=1: guilty in absentia on both counts (2023 raw:16; 2025 raw:52) — a trial verdict, not a plea. latest_record_date 2025-06-26. RECONSTITUTION open-question, page_only — see the evidence field. I did not code no-reconstitution-reported: nothing in the record affirms the Infinity service is down (the target coded here is the reseller, and the page itself frames the untouched provider tier as the operation's open effectiveness question, which is precisely the protocol's open-question trigger rather than its sibling-sites-in-notes case). arrests.quote: Es wurden zunächst drei Beschuldigte in Untersuchungshaft genommen: Der Haftbefehl gegen einen 25-jährigen Münchner konnte zwischenzeitlich aufgehoben werden, da sich nach dem vorläufigen Stand der Auswertung der sichergestellten Daten der dringende Tatverdacht nicht bestätigt hat. Die Ermittlungen dauern aber auch gegen diesen Beschuldigten weiter an. Ein Haftbefehl gegen einen 25-Jährigen aus Hamburg wurde mittlerweile erweitert, nachdem sich im Rahmen der vorläufigen Auswertung der bei ihm sichergestellten Datenträger der dringende Tatverdacht unter anderem der Anstiftung zum schweren sexuellen Missbrauch von Kindern über einen Messenger-Dienst ergeben hatte. Weiterhin in einer Justizvollzugsanstalt befindet sich ein 25-Jähriger aus dem Landkreis Tirschenreuth. Bei dem Softwareentwickler soll es sich nach dem gegenwärtigen Ermittlungsstand um den mutmaßlichen Haupttäter handeln.

Am 03.06.2025 erfolgten schließlich gleichzeitige Durchsuchungen an neun Objekten im Landkreis Tirschenreuth (ein Objekt), in München (zwei Objekte), im Landkreis Pfaffenhofen an der Ilm (ein Objekt) und in Hamburg (fünf Objekte). Insgesamt wurden gut 100 Einsatzkräfte mehrerer Dienststellen eingesetzt und von Weiden aus gemeinsam mit einer Staatsanwältin der ZCB koordiniert.

Es wurden zunächst drei Beschuldigte in Untersuchungshaft genommen: Der Haftbefehl gegen einen 25-jährigen Münchner konnte zwischenzeitlich aufgehoben werden, da sich nach dem vorläufigen Stand der Auswertung der sichergestellten Daten der dringende Tatverdacht nicht bestätigt hat. Die Ermittlungen dauern aber auch gegen diesen Beschuldigten weiter an. Ein Haftbefehl gegen einen 25-Jährigen aus Hamburg wurde mittlerweile erweitert, nachdem sich im Rahmen der vorläufigen Auswertung der bei ihm sichergestellten Datenträger der dringende Tatverdacht unter anderem der Anstiftung zum schweren sexuellen Missbrauch von Kindern über einen Messenger-Dienst ergeben hatte. Weiterhin in einer Justizvollzugsanstalt befindet sich ein 25-Jähriger aus dem Landkreis Tirschenreuth. Bei dem Softwareentwickler soll es sich nach dem gegenwärtigen Ermittlungsstand um den mutmaßlichen Haupttäter handeln.

Die Sicherstellung einer kompletten „Serverlandschaft", einer Vielzahl an Mobiltelefonen, USB-Sticks und Spielekonsolen sowie die Sicherungen von umfangreichen Clouddaten sind ein erfreulicher Zwischenerfolg für die Ermittler. Zudem wurde eine Vielzahl von Servern im In- und Ausland beschlagnahmt, auf denen die Täter die illegalen Streamingdienste betrieben haben sollen. Die Auswertung dieser immensen Datenmengen dauert im Moment an und wird noch einige Zeit in Anspruch nehmen.
Vermögensabschöpfung - kriminelles Verhalten darf sich nicht lohnen

Bei Ermittlungsverfahren, insbesondere mit hohen Taterlösen, kommt auch regelmäßig der Abschöpfung mutmaßlich durch Straftaten erlangter Vermögenswerte große Bedeutung zu. Hierbei wurden die Weidener Ermittler u.a. durch Fachkräfte für Vermögensabschöpfung und Kryptowährungen der Kriminalpolizeiinspektion mit Zentralaufgaben Oberpfalz unterstützt. Es konnten im Rahmen des Einsatzes Vermögenswerte, darunter Bargeld, Goldmünzen und Kryptowährungen, im Wert von ca. 500.000 EUR gesichert werden.

No third-person self-reference, no post-dating events, no WebSearch provenance. Every cell is therefore raw-level, page_only false. Contrast the SUPERSEDED capture for the same release, raw/press-releases/2025-06-03_justiz-bayern-de_zcb-bamberg-illegal-streaming-five-suspects-tirschenreuth.md, which IS reconstruction tier — it is headed 'Verbatim summary' but is an English bullet digest (30 lines) that speaks of the release in the third person, dates itself to the action day rather than the publication day, and states one fact the verbatim release does not support ('One suspect additionally charged with child-exploitation material offences (parallel proceedings)', superseded raw:22 — the release describes an EXPANDED arrest warrant in this same investigation, not a parallel proceeding). Nothing is coded from it. (raw:35), with about 100 officers coordinated from Weiden with a ZCB prosecutor (raw:35), and three suspects taken into custody (raw:37). hosting-takedown — 'Zudem wurde eine Vielzahl von Servern im In- und Ausland beschlagnahmt, auf denen die Täter die illegalen Streamingdienste betrieben haben sollen.' (raw:51): the servers ON WHICH the illegal streaming services were operated were seized, which is the definition; the same line records the seizure of a complete server landscape. Count undisclosed — the operation page flags servers_seized as missing-not-zero, which is the correct reading. asset-seizure — this is confiscation, not evidence collection, and the release says so with its own section heading 'Vermögensabschöpfung - kriminelles Verhalten darf sich nicht lohnen' (raw:45), followed by 'Es konnten im Rahmen des Einsatzes Vermögenswerte, darunter Bargeld, Goldmünzen und Kryptowährungen, im Wert von ca. 500.000 EUR gesichert werden.' (raw:47); asset-recovery and cryptocurrency specialists of the KPI-Z Oberpfalz supported it (raw:47). The mobile phones, USB sticks, games consoles and cloud data (raw:51) are evidence, not assets. (raw:53), with court-issued arrest warrants already in hand and terabytes of evidence under analysis (raw:51). No Anklageerhebung (formal charging) is reported, so this is not n=<int>. Here the release affirmatively says the proceedings continue, which is what v2's pending clause asks for. convictions and imprisonments not-reported: no cited record speaks to either stage. Untersuchungshaft is pre-trial detention, not an imposed custodial sentence, so it does not make imprisonments n=3 (same call as the Hof row). latest_record_date 2025-07-18 = the release date, the only record; the row is right-censored at the investigation stage. arrests.quote: Piratería audiovisual: detuvieron a vendedores ilegales de MagisTV en Argentina DeporTV -- º Domingo 26 Julio 2026 Capital Federal DeportTV Polideportivo Motor Fórmula 1 Turismo Carretera Turismo Nacional Rally Raid Rally Dakar Motociclismo Fútbol Liga Profesional Lionel Messi Selección Argentina Copa Libertadores Champions League Copa Sudamericana Ascenso Básquet Liga Nacional de Básquet Liga Argentina Selecciones Argentinas Argentinos por el mundo NBA Básquet Femenino Tenis Vóley Rugby Boxeo Hockey DeporTV Preferencias Modo alto contraste Polideportivo Motor Fórmula 1 Turismo Carretera Turismo Nacional Rally Raid Rally Dakar Motociclismo Fútbol Liga Profesional Lionel Messi Selección Argentina Copa Libertadores Champions League Copa Sudamericana Ascenso Básquet Liga Nacional de Básquet Liga Argentina Selecciones Argentinas Argentinos por el mundo NBA Básquet Femenino Tenis Vóley Rugby Boxeo Hockey 24-07-2025 15:43 - Fútbol Piratería audiovisual: detuvieron a vendedores ilegales de MagisTV en Argentina Cinco allanamientos en Chubut, Mendoza y Río Negro terminaron con órdenes de detención por la distribución de MagisTV Pro, una de las plataformas IPTV piratas más grandes de la región. La acción judicial fue impulsada por LaLiga y la Alianza Contra la Piratería. 24-07-2025 | 15:43 Imagen general con IA En una acción conjunta entre LaLiga de España y la Alianza Contra la Piratería, se concretaron cinco allanamientos simultáneos en Chubut, Mendoza y Río Negro, con el objetivo de desarticular una red de distribución ilegal de contenidos deportivos a través de la plataforma pirata MagisTV . Las órdenes de detención fueron emitidas por el Juzgado de Garantías N.º 4 de San Isidro y ejecutadas con apoyo de la Policía Federal y fuerzas locales. Entre los principales objetivos estuvo el proveedor de internet UV Mundo Digital, con sedes en Trelew y Rawson, que ofrecía dispositivos y suscripciones a MagisTV Pro bajo apariencia de legalidad. La empresa, registrada ante ENACOM y miembro de CABASE, comercializaba los servicios incluso en sus propios locales y redes sociales. Según explicaron desde LaLiga, que actúa como querellante en la causa, este tipo de operaciones refleja “la falta de compromiso” de ciertos proveedores de internet en la lucha contra el fraude audiovisual. “CABASE está influenciada por algunas ISP que no respetan la legalidad”, señaló su presidente de LaLiga, Javier Tebas , quien también destacó el rol de entidades colaboradoras como Mercado Libre y Mercado Pago en la investigación. Tebas (izquierda) durante una acción contra la piratería (Foto: X@LaLiga). Además de los allanamientos, la justicia solicitó la detención de al menos cuatro personas identificadas como operadores clave en la venta ilegal de MagisTV Pro. Estas personas recibían pagos a través de plataformas digitales como Mercado Pago, Naranja X y Binance, y acumularon ingresos que en algunos casos superaron los 160 millones de pesos argentinos . La investigación permitió rastrear evidencias bancarias, registros de IP y comunicaciones extraídas de aplicaciones de mensajería que vinculan directamente a los detenidos con la distribución ilegal de contenidos audiovisuales. El operativo formó parte de una estrategia regional más amplia que tiene como objetivo desarticular redes piratas de IPTV en América Latina . El uso de plataformas ilegales representa también un riesgo para los usuarios, debido a la exposición a malware, estafas digitales y robo de datos personales.  Entre los avances recientes en la lucha antipiratería destacan el desarrollo de bloqueos dinámicos por DNS e IP, la eliminación judicial de aplicaciones como MagisTV y FlujoTV -pendiente aún de ejecución por parte de Google- y la organización del primer “War Room” antipiratería en Argentina. Entre los principales objetivos estuvo el proveedor de internet UV Mundo Digital, con sedes en Trelew y Rawson, que ofrecía dispositivos y suscripciones a MagisTV Pro bajo apariencia de legalidad. La empresa, registrada ante ENACOM y miembro de CABASE, comercializaba los servicios incluso en sus propios locales y redes sociales. Según explicaron desde LaLiga, que actúa como querellante en la causa, este tipo de operaciones refleja “la falta de compromiso” de ciertos proveedores de internet en la lucha contra el fraude audiovisual. “CABASE está influenciada por algunas ISP que no respetan la legalidad”, señaló su presidente de LaLiga, Javier Tebas , quien también destacó el rol de entidades colaboradoras como Mercado Libre y Mercado Pago en la investigación. Tebas (izquierda) durante una acción contra la piratería (Foto: X@LaLiga). Además de los allanamientos, la justicia solicitó la detención de al menos cuatro personas identificadas como operadores clave en la venta ilegal de MagisTV Pro. Estas personas recibían pagos a través de plataformas digitales como Mercado Pago, Naranja X y Binance, y acumularon ingresos que en algunos casos superaron los 160 millones de pesos argentinos . La investigación permitió rastrear evidencias bancarias, registros de IP y comunicaciones extraídas de aplicaciones de mensajería que vinculan directamente a los detenidos con la distribución ilegal de contenidos audiovisuales. El operativo formó parte de una estrategia regional más amplia que tiene como objetivo desarticular redes piratas de IPTV en América Latina . El uso de plataformas ilegales representa también un riesgo para los usuarios, debido a la exposición a malware, estafas digitales y robo de datos personales.  Entre los avances recientes en la lucha antipiratería destacan el desarrollo de bloqueos dinámicos por DNS e IP, la eliminación judicial de aplicaciones como MagisTV y FlujoTV -pendiente aún de ejecución por parte de Google- y la organización del primer “War Room” antipiratería en Argentina. This is a redirect-as-control case and it qualifies because it follows state process: the redirect came out of an Egyptian criminal enforcement action (raids, arrests, prosecution referral), not a settlement, so it is domain-seizure and NOT voluntary-transfer (contrast the December 2024 Markkystreams row, where the same 'Watch Legally' redirect followed a negotiated handover). arrest-search — ACE's own account of the raids, quoted by Ars: 'On the night of Sunday, August 24, into the morning of Monday, August 25, Egyptian authorities carried out synchronized raids targeting two individuals behind the piracy network operating the Streameast group of websites. Twenty-two police officers were deployed in the operation.' (ars raw:1299), with the arrests at raw:1300 and the Egyptian account at ahram0905 raw:579. asset-seizure — the confiscated items include proceeds, not only evidence: 'Investigators also found active e-wallets connected to the confiscated devices, containing funds from the proceeds of their crimes.' (ahram0905 raw:575); 'Investigators also confiscated cash and multiple credit cards… They also confiscated £150,000 ($200,000) in cryptocurrency.' (ahram0905 raw:581, HTML entity £ in the raw); 'Investigators also confiscated cash, credit cards, and cryptocurrency holdings' (ahram0308 raw:590). The three laptops and mobile phones are EVIDENCE and are not what carries this code (v2 excludes evidence-cash; the e-wallet funds, cash, credit cards and cryptocurrency are proceeds). Real estate was TRACED, not stated seized (ahram0905 raw:581) — noted, not coded. intermediary-process is a BORDERLINE CALL: MPA states 'A coordinated investigation by the MPA/ACE global team, supported by disclosure court orders, led to the identification of the operators in Egypt.' (mpa raw:71) — disclosure process used to identify operators is the definition, but no recipient intermediary (registrar, CDN, host) is named in any record, so the code rests on the function rather than a named recipient. NOT coded: hosting-takedown — the records say the pair 'had established and managed 705 unlicensed websites and servers' (ahram0905 raw:563, ahram0308 raw:588), which describes what they ran, not what was seized or shut down; the operation page's own missing_fields says 'server seizure count not disclosed; sources describe 705 websites and servers managed, not seized'. Also NOT coded: blocking-order, content-delisting, payment-disruption, end-user-action — no record verb supports them. JUDICIAL: arrests n=2 — 'The sting resulted in the arrest of two men over suspicion of copyright infringement in El Sheikh Zayed City near the Greater Cairo metro area.' (ars raw:1300); 'the two men were arrested on 24 August in El-Sheikh Zaid, Giza Governorate' and 'have since been detained' (ahram0905 raw:579); 'Local police arrested two men on suspicion of copyright infringement, and various assets were seized.' (tf raw:309). No record gives a different arrest count. indictments n=2 — 'Egypt's public prosecutor has referred two defendants to criminal trial on charges of establishing and operating a transnational criminal organization that specialized in pirating live sports broadcasts and violating intellectual property rights through a network of websites, the prosecution said on Sunday.' (ahram0308 raw:510, HTML entity ’ in the raw's 'Egypt's'); referral to criminal trial on stated charges is the charging event, and the count is explicit. convictions pending, REFERRAL-INFERRED per v2: the same referral statement puts the next stage underway, and the prosecution frames the matter as continuing ('The Public Prosecution said it will continue to take decisive action against cybercrime, pursue digital piracy networks, and track illicit proceeds through international judicial cooperation', ahram0308 raw:584); no verdict is reported in any cited record. imprisonments not-reported (empty cites) — no cited record speaks to sentencing; I did NOT chain a second inference from the referral, since v2's referral rule reaches only the NEXT stage. latest_record_date 2026-03-08 = the Ahram trial-referral report, the latest cited record; the row is right-censored there, ~18 months after the raids, with charges filed and no verdict. CONFLICTS (none affect a coded value): domain counts — ACE says '80 associated domains' (ace raw:436), MPA says the service ran 'across over 170 domains' (mpa raw:30) and that 173 have so far been transferred (mpa raw:72), while the Egyptian Ministry of Interior says the pair 'established and managed 705 unlicensed websites and servers' (ahram0905 raw:563) and EG-CERT confirmed 'hundreds of internet domains' (ahram0308 raw:580) — three different denominators (branded network / transferred set / total managed infrastructure) rather than a contradiction, recorded here. Device counts — Egyptian MOI via Ahram: 'three laptops and two mobile phones' (ahram0905 raw:575); ACE via Deadline in Ars: 'three laptops and four smartphones… and 10 credit cards with about $123,561' (ars raw:1300); the Egyptian official statement is the more authoritative for what Egyptian police seized, but neither is a coded value. Action date — the raid spans the night of 24 into 25 August (ars raw:1299) while the arrest reporting dates the arrests to 24 August (ahram0905 raw:579). Foreign-agency support (an IC-qualification issue, not a coded column) is reported only at second hand: 'ACE worked with Egyptian authorities, Europol, the US Department of Justice, the Office of the US Trade Representative, and the National Intellectual Property Rights Coordination Centre, per The Athletic.' (ars raw:1297; LAT raw:214 carries the same list, also crediting The Athletic) — the ACE release itself names no foreign public agency, which matches the operation page's caveat. The Egyptian side names ACE's contribution as technical: 'The probe was supported by technical information from the Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment (ACE)… as part of international cooperation to track the network's operations.' (ahram0308 raw:576). RECONSTITUTION — open-question, and the reasoning matters because two other values were live. (i) no-reconstitution-reported was rejected on dates: 'All Streameast sites now redirect to the ACE “Watch Legally” page.' (ahram0905 raw:599, AP raw:16943) is dated 11-12 days after the 24-25 August action and 0-2 days after the 3 September announcement — inside the 14-day window, so it is announcement-time status, not durability evidence. The later restatements are recaps, not fresh observations: Ahram's 2026-03-08 piece recycles its own September paragraphs verbatim in a background block (ahram0308 raw:586-596, ending 'Following the crackdown, all StreamEast domains were redirected to ACE's “Watch Legally” page'), and MPA's October filing reports transfer progress ('173 domains (so far)… with additional transfers upcoming', mpa raw:72) rather than a status check on the target. (ii) successor-named was rejected on the postdating rule: the surviving 'original' Streameast is not a successor spawned by this action — it predates it and was itself the target of the August 2024 HSI domain seizures (tf raw:273-276), so under v2 it is history, not durability. (iii) open-question is coded because the records themselves — not merely the wiki page — frame the survival as this operation's open effectiveness question: TorrentFreak's headline is 'ACE Shuts Down Giant ‘Streameast’ Piracy Ring, But the Original Survives' (tf raw:241) and its body says 'The press release doesn't mention that the original Streameast is still in operation, but ACE is undoubtedly aware of its existence' (tf raw:298) and that operator 'Quick' told users 'the service is operating as usual' (tf raw:300, with the quoted denial at raw:301); Ars runs the section head 'Original Streameast still pirating' and writes 'The endurance of the popular piracy brand is a reflection of the entangled problems facing sports rights owners and sports fans.' (ars raw:1292, 1338, 1341); ACE's own spokesperson concedes the distinction — 'ACE is aware that the original site is a different website from the one shut down in Egypt.' (ars raw:1340). This is the exception the v2 clone rule carves out, so it beats the (in any case out-of-window) down-status. as_of 2025-09-03 = date of both records carrying that framing. The only prior action any cited record discusses is the August 2024 HSI seizure of 'several domain names linked to Streameast' (tf raw:273; ars raw:1341-1343), which the records say failed to remove the original ('The seizures were carried out by the book but did not achieve the desired effect. Streameast remained available through alternative and regularly updated domains.', tf raw:274). So the relationship between this 2025 criminal action and the December 2024 Markkystreams settlement is NOT resolvable from this row's records, and I did not code it. CORPUS SEARCH (grep -rli 'streameast|crackstreams' over wiki/sources/): 17 files, of which the eight cited plus three about the DIFFERENT December 2024 Markkystreams operation (2024-12-20 ACE, The Desk, Broadband TV News) — those three are inputs to the already-coded ace-markkystreams-… row, not to this one, and the wiki already links the two operations (related_operations + the 'Original-versus-copycat dispute' callout), so there is NO linkage gap of the kind input-rule 3 targets. Worth recording for the coordinator: the corpus's own Markkystreams source pages state that 'streameast[dot]to' was in the 138-domain December 2024 transfer set and flag the connection to this September 2025 Egyptian action as unresolved in the public record (wiki/sources/2024-12-20_ace_markkystreams-largest-live-sports-piracy-ring-138-domains.md:24, :28, :55) — consistent with what I found at record level, i.e. the corpus is honest about the gap rather than wrong about it. Remaining hits are Egypt/ACE context files (Egypt IP Law 82/2002, Movizland, Laroza, INWIPTV) that mention neither this action nor its targets in a codable way. [v3 harmonization 2026-08-13] v3: reconstitution open-question -> target-persisted. The cited records state the target itself ('Streameast live-sports piracy network', the page's own target_entity) stayed reachable after the action; that is a disruption that did not remove the target, which v2 had no value for and which open-question hid. [v3 CORRECTION 2026-08-13, codex targeted audit] This cell was recoded to `target-persisted` on 2026-08-13 and that was WRONG. The cited Ars Technica line says ACE 'is aware that the original site is a different website from the one shut down in Egypt' (raw/news/2025-09-03_arstechnica_streameast-copycat-sports-piracy-sting.md:1338-1341), so the surviving site is not this row's target; and the TorrentFreak passage about seizures that 'did not achieve the desired effect' concerns the August 2024 HSI action, which PREdates the coded 2025 action and is inadmissible under the postdating rule. CAPTURE TIERS. (a) raw/press-releases/2025-09-16_...-iptv66-piracy-takedown.md is the workhorse and is USABLE for its quoted material: it carries, under the heading "# Source extract (verbatim)", the verbatim Spanish paragraphs of BOTH PGR releases — the 16 Sep announcement (raw:32-52) and the ~21 Sep coercion release (raw:60-74), captured via curl_cffi chrome124 against Cloudflare (raw:98). Everything I cite is from those quote blocks. The file's later "# Key working English summary" (raw:76-96) is an agent-authored digest that mixes in secondary-press material (Diario Libre, Piracy Monitor: the 1,400-channel / 14,000-title catalogue, USD 23M damages, the domain list) — RECONSTRUCTION tier, not cited. (b) raw/press-releases/2025-09-21_...-medidas-coercion-caso-complejo.md is RECONSTRUCTION tier throughout: an English-language rewrite of a Spanish release with editorial headings ("Network details (reiterated)") that reproduces the same secondary-press figures; not cited, because the same release's verbatim Spanish is available in (a) at raw:60-74. (c) raw/press-releases/2025-09-18_...-solicita-18-meses-prision.md is RECONSTRUCTION tier and hits the protocol's sharpest tell — a capture dated 18 September that reports the outcome of the 21 September hearing ("The court subsequently (on or about 21 September 2025) rejected the 18-month preventive-prison request...", that raw:50) — plus English editorial headings over a Spanish release, with only its lead sentence in Spanish (that raw:15). Not cited; the 18-month request is verbatim in (a) at raw:64. MODALITY. arrest-search only: "Un equipo de 30 fiscales encabezan 19 allanamientos..." (raw:34), "En los allanamientos, practicados en el Distrito Nacional, San Pedro de Macoris y Jarabacoa, se ocuparon equipos electronicos, documentos y vehiculos." (raw:40), "los detenidos forman parte de una red de seis imputados" (raw:44). NOT coded asset-seizure — the line I applied across this batch is that a stated freeze/forfeiture or the seizure of financial assets (cash, funds, cryptocurrency) codes asset-seizure, while physical items impounded during a raid do not; here the only items named are electronic equipment, documents and vehicles, and the operation page itself records that no cryptocurrency-seizure quantum, wallet count or account freeze appears in any PGR release (op:226, op:267). (The same line lands the other way in brazil-mjsp-operacao-404-fase-2-2020, where the record names bulk cash.) NOT coded domain-seizure or hosting-takedown: the PGR releases claim neither, and the operation page states "0 domain seizures explicitly claimed in the PGR releases" and "0 servers explicitly identified as seized" (op:224-225) — the .com/.is/.es domains sit outside Dominican seizure authority. JUDICIAL. arrests n=6: "Las investigaciones establecieron que los detenidos forman parte de una red de seis imputados, de los cuales cuatro ya habian sido condenados en los Estados Unidos en el ano 2017 por hechos similares de pirateria digital." (raw:44), reinforced by the coercion release's "contra seis integrantes de la red de pirateria digital desmantelada mediante la Operacion Domo" (raw:60) and the six-name bail list (raw:64). indictments n=6: "Los integrantes de la red enfrentaran cargos por violacion a la propiedad intelectual y lavado de activos, delitos sancionados en Ley 65-00 sobre Derecho de Autor, la Ley 53-07 sobre Crimenes y Delitos de Alta Tecnologia, asi como la Ley 155-17 contra el Lavado de Activos y Financiamiento del Terrorismo." (raw:52) plus the court's imposition of coercion measures on the six named imputados (raw:64). BORDERLINE, flagged: the charging verb is future ("enfrentaran cargos") and Dominican procedure reaches its formal acusacion only after the investigation — which the "tramitacion compleja" declaration (raw:62) deliberately extends — so a stricter reading would code pending. I code n=6 because all six hold imputado status with named statutes and court-imposed coercion measures, which is the charging stage the protocol's "indictments (charges)" heading describes. convictions/imprisonments not-reported: the case was pre-trial at the last record and the operation page records "0 convictions to date" (op:222). NOTE on the custodial boundary: the only custody question in the record is PRE-TRIAL — "El Ministerio Publico habia solicitado al tribunal que impusiera a los imputados 18 meses de prision preventiva... pero, la jueza Fatima Veloz dispuso una garantia economica de RD$7,000,000 para Leonardo Alberto Casci Ocumarez y Raul Ernesto Guzman Lora; de RD$5,000,000 para Keomirys Torres Lopez; de RD$3,000,000 para Victor Luis Torres Lopez; de RD$1,500,000 para Raul Ernesto Guzman Croes, y de RD$3,000,000 para Leony Esmeralda Croes, ademas del impedimento de salida del pais y la presentacion periodica." (raw:64). Preventive prison is not a sentence, so neither its request nor its denial touches the imprisonments cell. latest_record_date 2025-09-21 (the coercion release, quoted verbatim in the 09-16 capture). RECONSTITUTION open-question, page_only — see the evidence field; no PGR record speaks to the platforms' status after 16 September 2025. CORPUS SEARCH (IPTV66 | Operacion Domo | Servidor Privado | Casci Ocumarez over wiki/sources/) returned the three cited PGR pages plus three unrelated hits (_index, an ASEP Panama resolution, a LaLiga Argentina page) AND ONE REAL LINKAGE GAP: wiki/sources/2026-07-07_us-doj_pro-ip-act-annual-reports-fy2014-fy2023-series.md, whose FY2022 extract records "case-based mentoring of the Dominican Republic's DICAT on digital-piracy investigation 'IPTV66' — operational security, secure bitcoin purchases, record keeping (May 2022) (p. 32)" (raw/government-reports/2024-06-18_us-doj_pro-ip-act-annual-report-fy2022-ic-extract.md:16, and again at raw:30 and raw:38). That is a US tier-1 own-record of US involvement in the IPTV66 investigation, and the operation page currently asserts the opposite in two places — "No US Department of Justice or HSI own-domain release referencing the same operation / defendant set was located" (op:241, op:269) and missing_fields "us-side-press-release-or-charging-document-confirmation" (op:46). The wiki page should cite it. It changes no coded cell: it is ICHIP capacity-building three years before the action, with no modality, judicial or durability content, so it does not enter latest_record_date.

Lines raw:12-30 are the GdF gdf.gov.it release body, labelled "Testo riportato verbatim" (raw:16) and reading as continuous Italian release prose including the standing presumption-of-innocence preamble that a summarizer would not invent (raw:18) — treated as USABLE and the only thing coded from. The capture carries no fetch metadata at all (no http_status, no content_hash, no word_count, no fetcher), so the usable call rests on the internal evidence just described rather than on a recorded 200. PROTOCOL DEFECT (repeat): v2's three tiers are defined per CAPTURE, and this file — like the fase-5 pilot capture, where the same gap was flagged — is two tiers in one file. The protocol does not authorize a per-line split, and I have made one; a v3 rule for hybrid captures is needed, otherwise coders will keep improvising it. MODALITY: arrest-search only — "Militari del Comando Provinciale della Guardia di finanza di Cagliari hanno svolto, in questi giorni, sequestri e perquisizioni in diverse regioni italiane a contrasto dello streaming illegale di contenuti televisivi e a tutela del diritto d'autore." (raw:20). Did NOT code hosting-takedown: the release names servers only as a LAYER OF THE CHAIN whose participants were identified — "identificando una serie di soggetti coinvolti lungo la filiera della pirateria, inclusi fornitori di contenuti, reti di distribuzione e server" (raw:22) — and never says a server was seized or shut down; the object of the 'sequestri' is left unspecified, and the operation page's frontmatter and missing_fields both record servers_seized as unknown/zero. BORDERLINE CALL — end-user-action NOT coded: the GdF command's quoted statement says the operation makes it possible "di sanzionare penalmente e amministrativamente tutti i potenziali acquirenti in fase di identificazione" (raw:28), and the digest lists forthcoming bank-flow and chat analysis to enumerate subscribers (raw:45). Both are PROSPECTIVE — purchasers are described as still in the identification phase, and no sanction against any end user is stated to have been imposed. The protocol's rule is to code what the record says happened, so this stays out; it is the single most likely cell to change if a follow-up release lands. Did NOT code intermediary-process: the cross-border step is authority-to-authority evidence acquisition ("le attività investigative stanno ora proseguendo per la ricostruzione dell'intera filiera e l'acquisizione di ulteriori fonti di prova" with the involvement of US and Netherlands authorities, raw:24), not a subpoena or disclosure order served on a CDN, registrar or host. No domain, platform or brand name appears anywhere in the release, so no domain-seizure, blocking-order or content-delisting is available. JUDICIAL: arrests not-reported — the record uses indagati (persons under investigation) throughout and never states a detention; the operation page lists results.arrests in missing_fields for the same reason; the frontmatter seed arrests: 0 is not read as a source statement. indictments pending — the GdF preamble states the case is in the preliminary-investigation phase with judgment awaited: "per quanto fino emerso nella fase delle indagini preliminari, salvo gli ulteriori approfondimenti e in attesa di giudizio" (raw:18, the publisher's own wording reproduced including its 'fino emerso' typo), and the investigation is expressly continuing with foreign-authority evidence acquisition (raw:24). rows.notes:
converted from paper2/coding/multichoice-irdeto-kenya-score808-waka-tv-sports-piracy-enforcement-2024-2025--wakatv-2025.json (coder agent-split-ke, 2026-08-13); date_source=source-page; source_of_record=raw/news/2025-10-13_tech-ish_waka-tv-eldoret-dci-raid-prosecution.md; tier_basis=raw-dir:news; other_cited_captures=0; quotes are the cited lines as of the coding date; stratum from wiki fields (participating_countries=1, participating_agencies=0); official_release_sourced=False; component_of=multichoice-irdeto-kenya-score808-waka-tv-sports-piracy-enforcement-2024-2025. COMPONENT B of a two-action page (COMPOSITE_SPLIT). Coded from the WAKA TV record ONLY. Nothing is carried over from the combined file paper2/coding/multichoice-irdeto-kenya-score808-waka-tv-sports-piracy-enforcement-2024-2025.json: its hosting-takedown code and its relaunch-reported durability both came from the 2024 score808 records and neither survives contact with this component (see MODALITY and RECONSTITUTION).

CAPTURE TIERS AND INPUT SCOPE. Techish Kenya, raw/news/2025-10-13_tech-ish_waka-tv-eldoret-dci-raid-prosecution.md — USABLE (curl_cffi, 1004 words); article body at raw:73-125 inside site navigation and related-post chrome. Two exclusions inside that body: the embedded tweet at raw:107-113 is a third-party commentator's post reproduced by the article ('— Dickson Otieno (@DicksonOtieno) October 13, 2025'), not the outlet's reporting, so its line 'Involvement: Multichoice.' (raw:109) is not cited; and raw:85-97 is a 'Make tech - ish your favourite news source' Google-News promo interrupting the article. The two 2024 records the parent page cites (MultiChoice press release, Piracy Monitor) are about score808, a different target and a different action eleven months earlier, and are NOT inputs to this row — the MultiChoice one is in any case CAPTURE-UNUSABLE (its entire extracted text is a cookie-consent banner; documented on the score808 component).

MODALITY. arrest-search, raw-level, and it is the ONLY code this component earns: 'a sting operation in Eldoret led to the arrest of a man allegedly behind the sale and distribution of pirated WAKA TV and other IPTV services.' (raw:73); 'Kelvin Kiplang’at Singoéi was nabbed in Kiplombe, Uasin Gishu County, following a joint operation led by the Kenya Copyright Board (KECOBO) in collaboration with the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) and other enforcement agencies.' (raw:75); 'A raid at the suspect’s premises uncovered two mobile phones, 135 printed marketing flyers, and a “WAKA TV pirate control panel” allegedly used to manage accounts.' (raw:81).

NO INFRASTRUCTURE CODE — stated explicitly because the combined file had one and it was score808's. hosting-takedown is the live borderline call and I rejected it: no record states that a server, host or the WAKA TV service was seized or shut down. What the record states is that the raid 'uncovered' a control panel on the suspect's premises — a seizure verb already carried by arrest-search — and that 'Using that panel, officers were able to instantly disconnect 64 unauthorized subscribers who had been accessing pirated IPTV streams.' (raw:81). Disconnecting subscriber accounts through a recovered management interface is not the seizure or shutdown of hosting infrastructure, and the article's own closing treats the service's continued existence as unsettled rather than ended (raw:125). Flagged for the coordinator: if the census elsewhere treats an operator's seized account-management panel as hosting-takedown, this row should move with the rest, but on the record's verbs alone it does not. end-user-action is NOT coded: CODING.md v3 restricted the code to measures applied to identified end users and names this very row as one of the two that lose it — the 64 disconnections are service interruption, i.e. the effect of the enforcement already coded, and no subscriber is identified, fined, written to or proceeded against. Also not coded, with no supporting verb anywhere: domain-seizure, blocking-order, content-delisting, payment-disruption, intermediary-process, voluntary-transfer, asset-seizure (the two phones, 135 flyers and control panel are evidence/instrumentalities; the KES 300,000 cash bail is a bail deposit paid BY the defendant, not a seizure).

JUDICIAL. Counting unit natural persons; one man, Kelvin Kiplang'at Singoéi, throughout. arrests n=1, raw-level (raw:73 'the arrest of a man', raw:75 'was nabbed', raw:117 'After his arrest'). indictments n=1, raw-level but DERIVED and flagged: no record uses the word 'charged'. The charging event is 'After his arrest, Singoéi appeared before the Chief Magistrate’s Court in Eldoret on October 7, 2025.' with 'He was released on a cash bail of KES 300,000 with a surety of the same amount.' and 'The case is scheduled for pre-trial on October 13, 2025, and prosecutors say they’ll present evidence and witness statements linking him to the elaborate piracy network.' (all raw:117), preceded by 'The DCI says Singoéi was processed by KECOBO after the bust and prepared for prosecution.' (raw:83); the article's own headline is 'starts court prosecutions' (raw:67). A named natural person before a magistrate, with bail terms imposed and a pre-trial date set, is past a pre-charge referral, so this is n=1 and not 'pending'. Kenya is a common-law jurisdiction, so no non-common-law term mapping applies. convictions pending: the same passage puts the matter at pre-trial on 13 October 2025 with prosecutors stating they will present evidence and witness statements — a proceeding underway, no verdict in any cited record. imprisonments not-reported: he was RELEASED on bail, which is the opposite of custody, and no sentence exists to have a custodial component; this is silence, not 'none-stated', because no record describes a completed outcome. (Pre-trial remand would not have counted here in any event.) latest_record_date 2025-10-13 = the Techish byline in the capture, 'Hillary Keverenge October 13, 2025' (raw:69), which is also the day the pre-trial was set for — the row is right-censored at the pre-trial threshold with nothing published after it in the corpus.

RECONSTITUTION — the task's KNOWN ISSUE, resolved against this component. The combined file coded relaunch-reported on the strength of 'However, the score808.us site was again active at the time of this article (early November, 2024) which may mean that a backup of the site had been implemented elsewhere.' That evidence attaches to the score808 component and CANNOT attach here on two independent grounds: it concerns a different target (score808.us, not WAKA TV), and it PREDATES this action by about eleven months, so CODING.md's rule that durability evidence must postdate the coded action excludes it outright. Coded open-question instead, record-raised (hence page_only false): the article closes 'For now, 64 disconnected subscribers somewhere in Eldoret are probably staring at blank screens, waiting to see if their next “fix” comes back or if this is the end of the WAKA TV era.' (raw:125) and hedges at raw:121, 'The days of casually buying WAKA TV from Telegram channels and rental shops may be numbered.' — the record posing, in its own words, the unresolved question whether the target survives the action. Calibrated against the corpus's existing treatment of the same shape: Laroza is open-question on TorrentFreak's 'How effective this message is, has yet to be seen.', and Streameast is open-question on a record-raised effectiveness question. The alternative reading, which I record because it is defensible: this is contemporaneous journalistic speculation published within a week of the arrest rather than an observation of post-action status, which would make the cell not-reported. I chose open-question because the code is defined by the presence of an unresolved effectiveness question about this target, not by an elapsed interval, and CODING.md deliberately declines to narrow it. no-reconstitution-reported is ruled out: no record affirms the service down, and even a down-status here would fall inside the 14-day announcement window.

PARTICIPATING COUNTRIES ESTABLISHED BY THE RECORD: ONE — Kenya. The executing bodies are KECOBO (lead), the DCI 'and other enforcement agencies' (raw:75), all Kenyan; the court is the Chief Magistrate's Court in Eldoret (raw:117). No foreign law-enforcement body appears. The only cross-border actor named is MultiChoice, and only as victim and general anti-piracy actor: 'MultiChoice, one of the biggest victims of illicit IPTV redistribution, has been an active player in anti-piracy enforcement. KECOBO credited collaboration with broadcasters and investigators for helping track down the operation.' (raw:119) — no country is attached to it in this record, and it is a private company either way. NOTE a page-level over-reach the split exposes: the operation page's participating_agencies list Irdeto and MultiChoice/SuperSport for the operation as a whole, and the page's own missing_fields concedes that 'Irdeto's and SuperSport's WAKA-TV-specific (2025) role is inferred from the score808 (2024) sources; source [3] names only MultiChoice generically for the WAKA TV matter.' Irdeto is named nowhere in the WAKA TV record.

CORPUS SEARCH (CODING.md input step 3): grep -i 'score808|score 808|WAKA TV|KECOBO|Kenya Copyright Board|Singo' over wiki/sources/ returns five files — the three the parent page cites, wiki/sources/_index.md (catalog), and wiki/sources/2024-03-07_justice-gov-za_doj-multichoice-mou-combatting-piracy.md, a South African DOJ–MultiChoice memorandum of understanding, a different matter. No source page about WAKA TV exists beyond the one cited. NO linkage gap.

DEFECTS FOUND (reported, not fixed — raw/ and wiki/ are read-only for this pass). (1) STRUCTURAL, and it is the reason for this split: the parent page presents two unrelated targets, two years apart, with two separate suspects, under one standalone operation heading, and its aggregate frontmatter (results.arrests: 2, enforcement_type, status: ongoing) blends them — the 'ongoing' status is true only of the WAKA TV prosecution, while score808 has no reported judicial step at all. (2) The parent page's Contradictions & Open Questions section reads 'No separate content recorded for this section.' although its own cited record leaves this component's outcome explicitly unresolved (raw:125) and reports the OTHER component's target back online (Piracy Monitor raw:125). (3) The parent page's source page for this record states 'Verified via web search (L2/L17)' and lists corroboration by 'Techweez, TechMoran, Music In Africa', none of which is in the corpus — so the WAKA TV component rests on exactly one captured record, and every judicial cell above is single-sourced. (4) Minor: the wiki source page and the parent page both render the defendant's name 'Kelvin Kiplang'at Singoéi' consistently with the capture, but the capture's 'Singoéi' spelling is the outlet's and is uncorroborated in-corpus.
