rows.notes: converted from paper2/coding/portugal-spain-europol-euipo-iptv-crypto-cyber-patrol-2025.json (coder agent-w2-3, 2026-08-13); date_source=raw-frontmatter; source_of_record=raw/press-releases/2025-11-19_europol_eur-47-million-crypto-traced-disrupt-digital-piracy.md; tier_basis=raw-dir:press-releases; other_cited_captures=1; quotes are the cited lines as of the coding date; stratum from wiki fields (participating_countries=2, participating_agencies=3); official_release_sourced=True. CORPUS-SEARCH FIND (input rule 3) — THE OPERATION PAGE IS MISSING ITS BEST SOURCE. The page's frontmatter `sources` lists only two entries (the PJ Portugal capture and a 2024 EUIPO/Europol strategic report), and its References section names the Europol newsroom release by URL only. But the corpus HOLDS that release as a full source page and a usable capture: wiki/sources/2025-11-19_europol_eur-47-million-crypto-traced-disrupt-digital-piracy.md → raw/press-releases/2025-11-19_europol_eur-47-million-crypto-traced-disrupt-digital-piracy.md (jina, 674 words, http 200, full release body at raw:27-63). Its source page even lists this operation in pages_updated. Found with `ls wiki/sources/ | grep '^2025-11'` plus a content grep for '11.8 million|69 piracy|cyber-patrol week|crypto traced'. Coded as an input per rule 3; the linkage gap is reported for the coordinator to repair on the wiki side. It matters: without it this whole row would have been page-only. CAPTURE TIERS: (a) EUROPOL (corpus-search) is USABLE — verbatim own-domain release body raw:27-63 inside a small newsletter/metadata tail (raw:65-105). (b) PJ PORTUGAL (raw/press-releases/2025-11-19_pj-portugal_…) is RECONSTRUCTION tier: it is an agent-compiled dossier headed 'Source extract (verbatim and translated key passages)' (raw:24) with sections it wrote itself — a cross-source corroboration table (raw:69-81), an 'L24 cooperating-LE roster' (raw:83-91), an 'L25 tier-1 publisher justification' (raw:93-97) and 'Scope limits' (raw:99-102). It does carry genuine Portuguese verbatim fragments from the PJ release (raw:33, 36, 40), but its Europol section (B) is explicitly assembled at second hand — 'page is a Single-Page Application; full body confirmed via Infosecurity Magazine, OCCRP, Cybernews, EuroWeeklyNews, Piracy Monitor mirror reporting that reproduced Europol-supplied figures.' (raw:52) — which is the manual's WebSearch-summary tell. Cited only with the (reconstruction) marker. (c) The 2024-10-23 EUIPO/Europol 'Uncovering the ecosystem of IP crime' report predates this action by 13 months and is generic strategic analysis, not a record of this week; nothing coded from it. MODALITY: payment-disruption ONLY, and it is raw-level thanks to the Europol capture — '25 illicit IPTV services referred to the participating crypto service providers for disruption;' (europol raw:43) and, decisively for whether the disruption HAPPENED rather than was merely requested, 'By identifying, tracing, and successfully shutting down the crypto accounts of illicit services, the criminal revenue stream is disrupted.' (europol raw:53). The PJ dossier records the same outcome in its summary line on dismantled clandestine financial circuits and interrupted criminal funding flows (pj raw:46). NOT coded, and each omission is a deliberate call: asset-seizure — the EUR 47m/USD 55m is TRACED, not seized: 'Investigators traced cryptocurrency valued at around USD 55 million (over EUR 47 million) through various accounts associated with these services.' (europol raw:47); no freeze, forfeiture or judicial seizure appears in either record, and the operation page says so itself ('The figure traced is a tracing volume, not a court-ordered seizure or confiscation total'). This contradicts the page's own frontmatter seeds — enforcement_type includes `asset_freeze` and mechanisms_used includes `[[cryptocurrency-seizure]]` — which is exactly the frontmatter-seed caveat v2 warns about; the code follows the source verbs. intermediary-process — the operators were identified by OSINT and by investigators buying the services themselves (europol raw:51), not by compelled disclosure to a registrar/CDN/host; the exchange referrals are the disruption itself, already counted as payment-disruption. arrest-search, domain-seizure, hosting-takedown, blocking-order, content-delisting, end-user-action — none stated; '69 sites identified and targeted' (europol raw:41) is identification, and 'Investigations on 44 additional sites' (europol raw:45) is investigative opening. This row is one of the census's rare single-modality, no-judicial rows, and that is the substantive finding about it: a five-day co-located OSINT-and-payment-rails sprint whose only executed enforcement output is crypto-account closure by private exchanges. JUDICIAL: all four stages not-reported, empty cites. No cited record names a suspect, an arrest, a charge or a court. Europol's forward-looking line is about SERVICES, not persons — 'Several of the services remain under continued investigation by both public and private entities.' (europol raw:47) — and the PJ dossier's own scope note says 'No arrests are claimed in the tier-1 sources for this specific cyber-patrol week.' (pj raw:102). I considered `pending` for indictments on the strength of the 44 opened probes and rejected it: v2's pending needs proceedings underway against someone, and both records are explicit that no criminal organisation, operator identity or nationality was disclosed. latest_record_date 2025-11-19 = both same-day releases; the row is right-censored at announcement, with no follow-on record in the corpus. RECONSTITUTION: not-reported. I considered `open-question` because the operation page flags unresolved gaps ('closure status by named exchange not disclosed in tier-1 sources', Follow-Up Actions; the 'Disruption-vs-prosecution gap', Challenges) and rejected it: those gaps are about whether the disruption OUTPUT was executed and prosecuted, not about whether the targets reconstituted. Column 3 asks what happened to the targets after the action, and on that question every cited record is silent — no down-status, no relaunch, no successor, and the targeted services are not even named. Coding open-question here would fold 'we cannot verify the enforcement output' into a variable that measures target durability, which would pollute it; `not-reported` is the honest value. CONFLICTS/CORRECTIONS: (1) The operation page's Contradictions callout asserts a 'Currency discrepancy: PJ release says USD 55 million; Europol release says EUR 47 million.' That is wrong on the Europol side — the Europol release itself gives BOTH figures in one sentence, 'around USD 55 million (over EUR 47 million)' (europol raw:47) — so there is no inter-release discrepancy to reconcile. The uncited Europol capture settles a question the page left open. (2) Visitor figure: Europol's precise number is 11 821 006 (europol raw:47); the page's '~11.8 million' is a faithful rounding. (3) Attribution: the Europol release names only Europol, EUIPO and the Spanish National Police (europol raw:37) — Portugal and the Polícia Judiciária/UNC3T appear only in the PJ release (pj raw:33), and the seven private-sector partners (AAPA, Binance, Chainalysis, Coinbase, Irdeto, Maltego, Premier League) are named only in the PJ dossier (pj raw:44, 67), not in the Europol text. The page presents the partner list without that attribution split. (4) 'More than 15 countries and private sector organisations joined Europol in this collaborative effort' (europol raw:59) — the page's restriction of participating_countries to Portugal and Spain is correct and well-founded. CORPUS SEARCH: `ls wiki/sources/ | grep '^2025-11'` (89 files) plus `grep -rlie '11.8 million|69 piracy|cyber-patrol week|crypto traced|cryptocurrency traced' wiki/sources/` returned nine hits; only two are about this action — the cited PJ page and the UNCITED Europol page above. No source page exists in the corpus for any of the four tier-2 outlets the operation page lists in its References (Infosecurity Magazine, OCCRP, Cybernews, Piracy Monitor), so those references are unbacked by any capture. CORPUS DEFECTS FOUND (reported, not fixed): (1) NEW and material — the missing `sources` entry for the Europol own-domain release described above; the page cites it as a bare URL in References while the corpus holds both a source page and a usable full-text capture, and the source page's own Cross-references section already points back at this operation. (2) NEW — the 'Currency discrepancy' open question in Contradictions & Open Questions is resolved by that same capture and should be closed. (3) NEW — the frontmatter's `enforcement_type: asset_freeze` and `mechanisms_used: [[cryptocurrency-seizure]]` are not supported by either record (traced ≠ frozen ≠ seized); the page's own prose says so, so the structured fields and the prose disagree. (4) NEW — the References section lists four tier-2 outlets with no corresponding source pages or captures in the corpus, i.e. they are uncheckable citations.

The 'suspensao' verb is aggregated with 'bloqueio' in one sentence and could cover registrar-level suspension, but no state/court transfer of domain control is stated. content-delisting (new v2 code) — "retirada de milhares de materiais piratas de repositorios e redes sociais" and removal of audio/video content incl. games and music (raw:19). arrest-search — "44 mandados de busca e apreensao, entre os quais, quatro de prisao preventiva e tres prisoes em flagrante" (raw:21); Ecuador-leg raids corroborate at page level: ~20 Guayaquil commercial establishments "were raided under judicial orders" by National Police + SENADI + SRI with 1,193 TV boxes and 1,240+ decoders seized (SENADI raw:23,29-33, reconstruction) — device seizures are merchandise/evidence in raids, not asset-seizure. Judicial: arrests n=3 (three prisoes em flagrante, MJSP raw:21); the 4 preventive arrest warrants are warrants issued, not arrests — execution status not reported. CONFLICT: the Indecopi reconstruction capture states "44 search warrants, 7 arrests" (raw/press-releases/2025-11-28_gob-pe-indecopi_participa-operativo-internacional-bloqueo-500-sitios.md:30), apparently summing warrants+arrests (4+3); MJSP's specific official breakdown wins. Indictments not-reported: "podem ser indiciados" (raw:74) is possibility language and "O intuito e identificar e responsabilizar os administradores" (raw:21) is intent, not a statement of proceedings underway — consistent with the fase-7 pilot's not-reported call. Event dates: partner records state 26-27 November 2025 while MJSP states the action on the 27th. latest_record_date 2025-12-04 = AL-INVEST release, the latest record cited in this row (notes-cited, following the fase-7 pilot precedent); all cited records are silent on charges/convictions/sentences — right-censored at 2025-12-04. quotes: L’indagine ha consentito di acquisire indizi di colpevolezza nei confronti dei 31 componenti di un gruppo criminale organizzato a carattere transnazionale, accusati della diffusione di palinsesti televisivi ad accesso condizionato, accesso abusivo a un sistema informatico, frode informatica, intestazione fittizia di beni e riciclaggio.

Oltre cento operatori della Polizia postale hanno effettuato perquisizioni nei confronti di 31 indagati in 11 città del nostro Paese e 14 obiettivi situati all’estero, in collaborazione con le Forze di polizia di Regno Unito, Spagna, Romania, Kosovo. Eseguiti provvedimenti anche in Canada, India, Corea del Sud ed Emirati Arabi uniti grazie alla cooperazione della autorità locali.

January 2026: ICHIP-mentored Romanian economic police officers conducted searches and issued a subpoena for interrogation in three Romanian cities in a joint case with Italian authorities in Operation Switch Off to gather evidence against a large transnational criminal organization involved in illegal streaming of copyright-protected movies and television shows. The total damage reported by the rightsholders, including U.S companies like Amazon Prime, Netflix, Paramount, and Disney+, amounted to $3.5 billion USD. In Italy, three illegal IPTV platforms were seized. An international arrest warrant was issued for a Romanian target who distributed illegal content through six servers operated out of Romania and an African country.

CAPTURE TIERS — eight sources, three tiers, and the two the operation page calls its anchors are the weakest captures. (a) POLIZIA DI STATO (raw/press-releases/2026-01-28_poliziadistato-it_…) is USABLE and is the tier-1 primary this row is built on: the full verbatim Italian release body sits at raw:117-145 inside heavy poliziadistato.it site navigation (raw:33-115, raw:151-299), curl_cffi, 950 words. (b) ACE (raw/press-releases/2026-01-29_ace_…) is USABLE — despite the agent-written '## Summary-Only Archive' preamble at raw:28-38 (which is reconstruction and is NOT cited), the '## Extracted Text' section carries the complete release including the bulleted key-results list (raw:76-102). (c) EUROJUST (raw/press-releases/2026-02-03_eurojust_…) is CAPTURE-UNUSABLE for its body: the '## Extracted Text' block is pure Wayback + eurojust.europa.eu navigation chrome (raw:43-141, ending in 'Art in the building' / '20 years of Eurojust: anniversary essays'), no release text at all, word_count 152; the only substance is the agent-authored summary at raw:31-35, which is RECONSTRUCTION tier and which the file itself labels 'This archive is summary-only.' (raw:39). Nothing is cited from it — everything it summarises (31 suspects, nine-country action day, three Italian platforms, Romanian servers) is available raw-level from the Italian release and ACE. (d) POLIȚIA ROMÂNĂ (raw/press-releases/2026-01-22_politiaromana-ro_…) is CAPTURE-UNUSABLE: http_status 403 and the body is the Romanian block page, 'Site-ul a blocat accesul dumneavoastra din motive de securitate (403 Forbidden).' (raw:31), with text_status still reading 'parsed'. Not cited. This confirms the operation page's own R78b audit note. (e) DOJ 'Cyber & IP Europe' (raw/press-releases/2026-04-18_justice-gov_…) is USABLE — a DOJ program page whose ICHIP activity list contains a Switch Off entry at raw:223. (f) The two EUIPO records (2024-06-13 Sport Week, 2024-11-28 Online Copyright Infringement) predate the operation by 14+ months and are generic IPTV background, not records of this action; nothing coded from them. MODALITY: arrest-search — 'Oltre cento operatori della Polizia postale hanno effettuato perquisizioni nei confronti di 31 indagati in 11 città del nostro Paese e 14 obiettivi situati all’estero, in collaborazione con le Forze di polizia di Regno Unito, Spagna, Romania, Kosovo.' (polizia raw:129), corroborated by ACE's '29 raids in 11 Italian cities' (ace raw:78) and by DOJ for the Romanian leg, 'ICHIP-mentored Romanian economic police officers conducted searches and issued a subpoena for interrogation in three Romanian cities' (doj raw:223). hosting-takedown — 'In Italia sono state sequestrate tre piattaforme Iptv illegali' (polizia raw:141), 'Illegal IPTV infrastructure serving millions of users taken offline' (ace raw:84), 'Six servers seized outside of Italy' (ace raw:94). domain-seizure — the same Italian sentence states judicial seizure banners were affixed to the front-end sites: 'con apposizione di pannelli di sequestro ai siti vetrina e gruppi Telegram utilizzati per la vendita' (polizia raw:141); a seizure panel served under a Catania prosecutorial order is transfer of site control under state process, which is exactly the v2 redirect-as-control case. content-delisting — the Telegram sales channels in that same clause, plus ACE's 'Removal of associated websites and Telegram-based sales channels' (ace raw:92): messaging-channel and associated-site removal is the v2 content-delisting scope. end-user-action is a BORDERLINE CALL, coded the same way as the Kenya row so the census stays internally consistent: 'L'operazione ha bloccato l'attività di un migliaio di rivenditori italiani con oscuramento di oltre 100mila utenti finali in Italia e milioni a livello mondiale.' (polizia raw:139) and 'More than 125,000 end users disconnected in Italy, and millions globally' (ace raw:88). Reading A (coded): the records report end users as a direct object of the action and both sides publish the count as a headline result. Reading B (rejected, recorded): disconnection is the downstream effect of shutting the service, and no end user faces any stated proceeding — under that reading end-user-action should be reserved for enforcement against users (the Italian/Greek fine tracks). Flagging so the coordinator can normalise this code across the census; it is the same judgement call as multichoice-irdeto-kenya-… NOT coded: asset-seizure — the release describes financial-flow ANALYSIS, not seizure ('tracciamento delle transazioni finanziarie, soprattutto in criptovalute', polizia raw:133) and describes the suspects' own crypto investment, fictitious asset registration and shell companies as offence conduct (raw:135); no freeze, forfeiture or confiscation is stated and the operation page's cryptocurrency_seized is empty. blocking-order, payment-disruption, intermediary-process, voluntary-transfer — no supporting verb. JUDICIAL: arrests not-reported. No cited record states a single arrest: the Italian release reports searches against 31 indagati (raw:129), ACE reports '31 suspects' identified (ace raw:78), and DOJ reports only that 'An international arrest warrant was issued for a Romanian target' (doj raw:223) — a warrant issued is not an arrest executed (same call as the Operação 404 fase-8 row on its four preventive-arrest warrants). The operation page's results.arrests: 0 is the repo's zero-for-unknown convention, and I read the record as silence, not as an affirmative 'no arrests'. indictments pending: the Catania prosecutor states it has obtained evidence of guilt against a defined 31-person group, 'acquisire indizi di colpevolezza nei confronti dei 31 componenti di un gruppo criminale organizzato a carattere transnazionale, accusati della diffusione di palinsesti televisivi ad accesso condizionato, accesso abusivo a un sistema informatico, frode informatica, intestazione fittizia di beni e riciclaggio.' (polizia raw:125), those 31 are formally indagati under search (raw:129), and an international arrest warrant has issued for one target (doj raw:223) — proceedings underway, but indizi di colpevolezza and indagato status are pre-trial investigative categories in Italian procedure, not rinvio a giudizio, so this is not n=31. The 31 figure is recorded here rather than in the value. convictions and imprisonments not-reported — no cited record reaches either stage. latest_record_date 2026-04-18, WITH A DATE CONFLICT recorded per the manual: the DOJ capture's frontmatter publish_date is 2022-02-22 (the program page's original creation date) while its collection_date and 'updated' fields are both 2026-04-18, and the page's own content is self-dating — the cited Switch Off paragraph is labelled 'January 2026' and sits in a list containing 'March 2026' entries (raw:219, 229), so the text was published no earlier than March 2026. The wiki source page uses 2026-04-18 and so do I. (The operation page's References table lists this same DOJ source twice with the two different dates, rows [3] 2026-04-18 and [6] 2022-02-22 — see corpus defects.) RECONSTITUTION: not-reported. No cited record speaks to what happened after. ACE's 'infrastructure … taken offline' (ace raw:84) is announcement-day status published 2026-01-29, within days of the 22-28 January action and far inside the 14-day window, so it is not durability evidence. The DOJ record, whose content postdates the action by roughly two months, recounts the action without any status statement about the platforms or the six servers. No successor is named and no relaunch is reported. CONFLICTS ACROSS RECORDS (none of these is a coded Column value; all recorded per the manual): (1) RESELLERS — the Italian tier-1 says roughly a thousand, 'un migliaio di rivenditori italiani' (polizia raw:139), while ACE says 'Approximately 250 Italian resellers dismantled' (ace raw:86); the operation page adopts ACE's 250. A four-fold divergence between the official release and the rights-holder coalition, unexplained in both. (2) END USERS — 'oltre 100mila utenti finali in Italia' (polizia raw:139) versus 'More than 125,000 end users disconnected in Italy' (ace raw:88); the page adopts ACE's figure. (3) 14 COUNTRIES vs 14 TARGETS — the Italian release says searches hit '11 città del nostro Paese e 14 obiettivi situati all’estero' (polizia raw:129), i.e. 14 TARGETS abroad; ACE renders this as '29 raids in 11 Italian cities and 14 countries worldwide' (ace raw:78) and the operation page repeats '14 countries worldwide' in results.other and Results and Impact — while naming only eight foreign jurisdictions anywhere. The tier-1 official wording is the more precise and should govern. (4) SIX SERVERS — ACE says 'Six servers seized outside of Italy' (ace raw:94) and DOJ says the Romanian target 'distributed illegal content through six servers operated out of Romania and an African country' (doj raw:223), while the Italian release says only that the operation IDENTIFIED the provider — 'In Romania è stata individuata una rilevante Iptv mondiale che distribuiva contenuti attraverso sei server, ubicati in Romania e in uno Stato africano.' (polizia raw:143), with no seizure verb. The hosting-takedown code above rests on ACE's seizure statement, not on the Italian sentence; flagged because the operation page's results.servers_seized: 6 reads the seizure into the Italian text. (5) DAMAGE FIGURE — DOJ reports '$3.5 billion USD' of rightsholder damage (doj raw:223) while the Italian release quantifies only 'un giro di affari di milioni di euro mensili' (polizia raw:137); the operation page carries neither as a structured field. CORPUS SEARCH (grep -rlie 'operation switch off|operazione switch off|switch-off' and grep -rli 'IPTVItalia|migliorIPTV|DarkTV|proEuropaTV' over wiki/sources/): every Switch-Off-specific source page is already cited — the five 2026 records plus the two 2024 EUIPO background reports. The broad 'switch-off' pattern also matches generic phrasing in ~30 unrelated IPTV source pages (Piracy Shield, IOCTA, Operation Gotha, etc.), none of which mentions this action. The platform names IPTVItalia/migliorIPTV/DarkTV appear nowhere in wiki/sources/ — they exist only in the ACE raw and in the operation page's target_entity, which also names a fourth service, proEuropaTV, that appears in NO cited record (see corpus defects). convictions.quote: The five defendants sentenced were among eight defendants originally indicted in the Eastern District of Virginia in connection with operating Jetflicks. In addition to the defendants just sentenced in Nevada, defendant Darryl Polo previously pleaded guilty in the Eastern District of Virginia to four counts of criminal copyright infringement and one count of money laundering for his involvement with Jetflicks as well as an equally large illegal streaming site he ran called iStreamItAll. Similarly, defendant Luis Villarino also previously pleaded guilty in the Eastern District of Virginia to conspiracy to commit criminal copyright infringement. In May 2021, a judge in the U.S. District Court for the District of Virginia sentenced Polo and Villarino to, respectively, 57 months in prison and 12 months and a day in prison. After the case was transferred to the District of Nevada for trial, defendant Yoany Vaillant was tried separately from the other five remaining defendants. In November 2024, after an eight-day trial, a federal jury convicted Vaillant of conspiracy to commit criminal copyright infringement. Vaillant is scheduled to be sentenced on Sept. 4.

In addition to the defendants just sentenced in Nevada, defendant Darryl Polo previously pleaded guilty in the Eastern District of Virginia to four counts of criminal copyright infringement and one count of money laundering for his involvement with Jetflicks as well as an equally large illegal streaming site he ran called iStreamItAll. Similarly, defendant Luis Villarino also previously pleaded guilty in the Eastern District of Virginia to conspiracy to commit criminal copyright infringement. In May 2021, a judge in the U.S. District Court for the District of Virginia sentenced Polo and Villarino to, respectively, 57 months in prison and 12 months and a day in prison. After the case was transferred to the District of Nevada for trial, defendant Yoany Vaillant was tried separately from the other five remaining defendants. In November 2024, after an eight-day trial, a federal jury convicted Vaillant of conspiracy to commit criminal copyright infringement. Vaillant is scheduled to be sentenced on Sept. 4.

CAPTURE TIERS: the three news captures are USABLE (curl_cffi, http_status 200, fulltext) — The Online Citizen body at raw:67-105, Bangkok Post body at raw:193-211 inside very heavy site nav, Thai Examiner body at raw:85-155. The BERNAMA capture is RECONSTRUCTION tier: an agent-authored digest with bolded field labels and bullet rosters, and its own frontmatter records why — "bernama.com own page returned HTTP 503 (rate-limit); content recovered from the BERNAMA-bylined republication on thestar.com.my (L11)" (bernama raw:15). Nothing is coded from it; it is used only for latest_record_date and noted below. CAPTURE HYGIENE: The Online Citizen capture embeds the outlet's own machine-written block, headed "AI-Generated Summary" (toc raw:57-63), whose bullets include "Operation Awan Merah involved six countries and Interpol in a coordinated anti-piracy action." — not cited anywhere here; the reporter text below it is what is coded. MODALITY: arrest-search only, in both jurisdictions — Thailand: "The Thai suspect, identified only as Akkharawat, 33, was arrested at a house in tambon Mae Hia, Muang district, Chiang Mai, on Wednesday." (toc raw:75) with a subsequent company-office search; Malaysia: "A Malaysian couple were charged in connection with the same operation following simultaneous raids on three premises in Selangor state. Officers seized computers, laptops and mobile phones used to administer the application." (toc raw:85), corroborated at bangkok-post raw:201 and thai-examiner raw:125. NO other modality is available in any record: nothing is stated about the MyIPTV4K domain, app listing, servers, hosting, payment rails or subscriber base being seized, blocked, delisted or cut off — the operation-page frontmatter agrees (servers_seized: 0, domains_seized: 0, cryptocurrency_seized empty). The seized items on both legs are documents and devices taken as evidence (19 pages of accounting records, 4 pages of payment receipts, 22 pages of email correspondence, a credit-card photocopy, three mobile phones, one laptop, one desktop — toc raw:79, thai-examiner raw:105-109; computers/laptops/phones in Selangor — toc raw:85), so no asset-seizure. Did NOT code content-delisting despite the service being sold through Lazada Malaysia and Lazada Singapore listings (toc raw:97): no record says any listing or account was removed — the marketplace is described as the distribution channel, not as a party that acted. JUDICIAL: arrests n=3, derived-from-enumeration (1 Thailand + 2 Malaysia) — the Thai operator arrested per toc raw:75 and thai-examiner raw:101; the Malaysian couple per "A Malaysian couple were arrested in Selangor state in connection with the same offences, said Pol Col Puwadet Chulakasevi, an economic crime superintendent." (bangkok-post raw:201) and "Both denied the charges following arrest." (toc raw:89). The operation page flags a wording distinction in its own audit note (Thai suspect explicitly arrested; Malaysian couple charged following raids) — resolved here in favour of n=3 because two independent records state the couple were arrested, not merely charged. indictments n=3, derived-from-enumeration — "Authorities arrested Mr. Akkarawat in Mae Hia Subdistrict, Mueang District, Chiang Mai. He was charged with commercial copyright infringement." (thai-examiner raw:101), "Following the raids, Malaysian authorities charged two individuals." (thai-examiner raw:131), and the lede "A Thai man and a Malaysian couple have been charged with copyright infringement as part of a coordinated multinational crackdown on MyIPTV4K" (toc raw:67). This is the charging stage on the face of the records (unlike the Cagliari, Rosenheim and Huge Hit rows, which stop at investigation), so a count is coded rather than pending. convictions pending — all three contest: "The Thai and Malaysian suspects reportedly denied all charges." (bangkok-post raw:205), "The couple pleaded not guilty to all charges." and "Meanwhile, prosecution processes continued in Malaysia." (thai-examiner raw:143), "The investigation is ongoing." (toc raw:105) — proceedings underway with judgment awaited. imprisonments not-reported: no sentence is imposed or stated anywhere; the only custodial language in the corpus is the BERNAMA wire's abstract statutory range ("commercial offences carrying up to four years' imprisonment plus 100,000-800,000 baht fines", bernama raw:35), which is a penalty range, not an imposed outcome — the Singapore-row rule that penalty ranges are not outcomes. NAME CONFLICT recorded, not resolved: the Thai defendant is "Akkharawat" in The Online Citizen (raw:75) and Bangkok Post (raw:195) but "Akkarawat" in Thai Examiner (raw:101) and on the operation page; likewise CIB commissioner Nathasak Chaonasai (bangkok-post raw:195) vs Nattasak Chaowanasai (thai-examiner raw:95) and ECD commander Thatpoom Jaruprat (toc raw:77) vs Tatsaphum Charupraj (thai-examiner raw:95) — transliteration variants of the same people, not different individuals. ROSTER CONFLICT recorded: Bangkok Post states the collaboration "involved Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, South Korea, the United States and Interpol" (raw:199) — six parties including Singapore — while the operation page deliberately excludes Singapore from participating_countries on the ground that its documented role is as the IGCI venue for the Awan Merah meeting (thai-examiner raw:111). Not a Column value; recorded because the record and the wiki page differ. latest_record_date 2026-06-09 = BERNAMA wire byline (reporting a Thai DIP announcement dated 2026-06-08); the three usable captures are 2026-05-28/29. RECONSTITUTION not-reported, with the closest candidate examined and rejected: the DIP Director-General is quoted saying the operation resulted in the "dismantling of the network, which distributed copyrighted films without authorisation to paying subscribers in Thailand and Malaysia." (bernama raw:31). That is (a) a characterisation of the action's effect rather than an observed down-status of MyIPTV4K, (b) dated 2026-06-08/09, eleven days after the 2026-05-28 action and so inside the protocol's 14-day exclusion window, and (c) reconstruction-tier. No record states the MyIPTV4K box, app, Lazada listings or Unimax Pro reseller accounts stopped working, and no successor is named. Also considered and rejected: open-question — the operation page's third friction point ("Conviction not yet secured") is about judicial deterrence pending trial, not about succession or the takedown's durability, so it does not meet the Column 3 trigger. CORPUS SEARCH ('MyIPTV'/'myiptv', 'Awan Merah', 'Unimax' across wiki/sources/ and raw/): hits are exactly the four cited source pages and their four raws. NO LINKAGE GAP.
